The three UniDic dictionaries do not give the same morphemes. On the sentences of GSD train, unidic and unidic-cwj segment 85.88% alike and tag 66.06% alike, unidic-cwj and unidic-csj 88.10% and 73.22% (compare_dictionaries.py). Training data is therefore made for one dictionary, and so is a model.

Licenses of the corpora

UD Japanese-GSD is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 and UD Japanese-PUD under CC BY-SA 3.0 (LICENSE.txt in each repository). This is how this project handles them; it is not legal advice.

  • The corpora, and data converted from them, are not committed to the repository.
  • Converted data is adapted from the annotations of the corpus. If you share it, share it under the license of the corpus, name the corpus and say that the data was converted.
  • A model trained on converted data is released with the corpus, its version and its license stated. Whether the share-alike condition extends to a trained model is not settled by a court. This project takes its model, which holds weights and none of the annotation, not to be an adaptation of the corpus, and distributes it under the MIT license: see License of the model.

Evaluation

lindera-dependency evaluate, behind the train feature, compares an output with the answer, both in the lattice format with the same sentences in the same order.

cargo run --release -p lindera-dependency --features train -- evaluate \
    --gold dev.lattice \
    --system output.lattice

It counts what CaboCha's cabocha-system-eval and J.DepP count, so that the numbers can be set next to theirs. Every ratio comes with its numerator and its denominator; --json writes the same as JSON.

What is counted

  • Chunking: precision, recall and F over bunsetsu. A bunsetsu of the output is right when the answer has a bunsetsu that starts at the same morpheme and has the same length.
  • Dependency, on the sentences whose segmentation is the one of the answer (all of them when the parser was given the bunsetsu of the answer): the bunsetsu whose head is right. Level 0 counts every bunsetsu, level 1 every one but the last of its sentence, level 2 every one but the last two. Level 1 is the number J.DepP reports, and the headline number here.
  • End to end: over the bunsetsu of the answer but the last of each sentence, the ones for which the output has a bunsetsu with the same span, whose head has the span of the head in the answer.

The arc type (D, P) is not compared. A sentence whose morphemes differ between the two files is left out of every count and reported with its number, and a sentence without bunsetsu in the answer is not counted.

An example

For the output of the chunker with its defaults on the dev file of UD Japanese-GSD. The chunker writes every bunsetsu as depending on the next one, so the dependency lines are those of that baseline on the sentences it segmented right:

sentences: 506
left out, different morphemes: 0
not counted, no bunsetsu: 0
chunking precision: 97.02% (4009/4132)
chunking recall: 96.67% (4009/4147)
chunking F: 96.85%
chunking sentences: 85.38% (432/506)
dependency level 0: 68.55% (2308/3367)
dependency level 1: 63.92% (1876/2935)
dependency level 2: 57.84% (1453/2512)
dependency sentences: 16.90% (73/432)
end to end: 60.12% (2189/3641)
end to end sentences: 14.43% (73/506)

"Every bunsetsu depends on the next one" with the bunsetsu of the answer is the baseline any parser has to beat. At level 1 it is 64.10% (2,334 / 3,641) on the dev file, 62.77% (2,490 / 3,967) on the test file and 60.87% (5,386 / 8,849) on UD Japanese-PUD.

Comparing two outputs

With --compare, a second output is evaluated too, and the two are paired: each segmentation of a sentence, each end-to-end arc and each sentence is right in both, in the first only, in the second only or in neither. The p-value is the one of McNemar's exact test, two-sided, on the two discordant counts. The segmentations compare two chunkers, whatever the heads.

cargo run --release -p lindera-dependency --features train -- evaluate \
    --gold dev.lattice --system first.lattice --compare second.lattice

For two chunkers on the 10 folds of the train file (the template of CaboCha, then the default one):

paired segmentations: both 5908, first only 74, second only 107, neither 935, McNemar p = 0.0171
paired arcs: both 29235, first only 117, second only 164, neither 19856, McNemar p = 0.0060
paired sentences: both 887, first only 4, second only 12, neither 6121, McNemar p = 0.0768

Which data for which question

The dev and the test file are small: 3,641 and 3,967 arcs. For an accuracy near 90%, the 95% interval of one such number is about ±1 point, so a difference under a point cannot be told on them alone.

  • Features and settings are compared by cross-validation on the train file, which gives about 49,000 arcs (about ±0.3 point), and with the paired test above.
  • The dev file chooses between settings.
  • The test file and UD Japanese-PUD are for the reported result only.

Cross-validation

lindera-dependency split writes the folds. Sentence i of the input, from 0, is in the test file of fold i mod k and in the training file of every other fold, so the folds are the same wherever the command runs:

cargo run --release -p lindera-dependency --features train -- split \
    --input train.lattice --folds 10 --output-dir folds

This writes fold0.test.lattice and fold0.train.lattice to fold9.test.lattice and fold9.train.lattice. For the train file of UD Japanese-GSD, each test file has 702 or 703 sentences.

scripts/dependency/chunker_experiments.sh is an example of a cross-validation with these commands: it trains on each training file, segments the test file, joins the outputs and evaluates them as one.

API Reference

The API reference is available. Please see following URL:

  • lindera-dependency

Lindera CLI

A morphological analysis command-line interface for Lindera.

  • Installation - Install or build the CLI
  • Commands - Command reference for list, tokenize, build, download, train, and export
  • Tutorial - Step-by-step guide to get started

Installation

Install via Cargo

You can install the binary via cargo:

% cargo install lindera-cli

Download from GitHub Releases

Alternatively, you can download a pre-built binary from the release page:

  • https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases

Obtaining Dictionaries

Lindera does not bundle dictionaries with the binary. The easiest way to obtain one is the download subcommand, which fetches the pre-built dictionary matching the CLI version, installs it in the dictionaries directory (~/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/ipadic on Linux) and prints its path, which --dict takes:

% DICT_DIR=$(lindera download ipadic)
% echo "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ" | lindera tokenize --dict "$DICT_DIR"

See Commands for the available dictionary names and storage locations, and lindera list for the dictionaries in place.

Alternatively, you can download a pre-built dictionary manually from the GitHub Releases page:

# Example: download and extract the IPADIC dictionary
% curl -LO https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases/download/<version>/lindera-ipadic-<version>.zip
% unzip lindera-ipadic-<version>.zip -d /path/to/ipadic

Then specify the extracted dictionary path when using the CLI (note that the archive contains a lindera-ipadic directory):

% echo "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ" | lindera tokenize --dict /path/to/ipadic/lindera-ipadic

Build from Source

Build without dictionaries (default)

Build a binary containing only the tokenizer and trainer without embedded dictionaries:

% cargo build --release

Build with all features

% cargo build --release --all-features

Build with Embedded Dictionaries (Advanced)

For advanced users who want to embed dictionaries directly into the binary, use the embed-* feature flags. This eliminates the need for external dictionary files at runtime but increases the binary size.

IPADIC (Japanese dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-ipadic

IPADIC NEologd (Japanese dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-ipadic-neologd

UniDic (Japanese dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-unidic

UniDic CWJ (Japanese dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-unidic-cwj

The binary carries the 1.2 GB dictionary, and the build takes about 11 GiB of memory. lindera download unidic-cwj gets the dictionary without embedding it.

UniDic CSJ (Japanese dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-unidic-csj

The binary carries the 1.2 GB dictionary, and the build takes 8 to 11 GiB of memory, as for UniDic CWJ. lindera download unidic-csj gets the dictionary without embedding it.

SudachiDict (Japanese dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-sudachidict

ko-dic (Korean dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-ko-dic

CC-CEDICT (Chinese dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-cc-cedict

Jieba (Chinese dictionary)

% cargo build --release --features=embed-jieba

[!TIP] After building with an embed-* feature flag, use the embedded:// scheme to load the embedded dictionary:

% echo "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ" | lindera tokenize --dict embedded://ipadic

See Feature Flags for details.

Commands

The Lindera CLI provides six main commands:

  • list - List the morphological analysis dictionaries and their status
  • tokenize - Perform morphological analysis on text
  • build - Build a dictionary from source CSV files
  • download - Download a pre-built dictionary from the GitHub releases page
  • train - Train a CRF model from annotated corpus data
  • export - Export a trained model to dictionary format

Warnings and log messages

Every command writes its results to standard output and the warnings of the Lindera libraries to standard error. For example, when tokenize reads more than 32 KiB of text without a sentence delimiter, it cuts the sentence there (see Sentence Splitting) and warns:

% head -c 40000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' a | lindera tokenize --dict embedded://ipadic -o wakati > /dev/null
[WARN  lindera_segmenter::segmenter] no sentence delimiter (\n, \t, 。, 、) found within 32768 bytes from offset 0; forcing a sentence boundary to bound lattice size (see https://github.com/lindera/lindera/issues/871)

The RUST_LOG environment variable selects the messages, for example RUST_LOG=error for errors only, and RUST_LOG_STYLE=never turns their colors off; see RUST_LOG.

When standard output has no reader

When the program that reads the standard output of a command exits first, as head does once it has the lines it wants, the command ends quietly, with exit code 0 and no message:

  • tokenize, list and download write their result there, so they stop at the first write that has no reader. tokenize reads no more of its input. Another error while they write, such as a full disk, is written to standard error, and the exit code is 1.
  • train and export only report there on the files they write, so they drop the lines that cannot be written, as the training does with its progress, and write the model or the dictionary files all the same. Standard output never makes them fail.

When standard error has no reader, the commands drop their own messages there in the same way, such as the progress and notices of download and the notices of list, and go on to write their result. When standard error is non-blocking and full, as a parent process that reads it late can leave it, they wait until it takes each message, as the training does with its progress.

Up to v6.2.0, the commands failed instead; see the migration guide.

list

List the dictionaries that --dict can take: those embedded in the binary (via the embed-* feature flags) and those in the dictionaries directory, where lindera download puts them, each with the version of Lindera that built it.

List parameters

This command takes no arguments. It looks for dictionaries in the directory named by LINDERA_DICTIONARIES_DIR, as lindera download does (see Storage location).

List usage

% lindera list

Skipped /home/user/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/6.2.0: not a dictionary (no metadata.json) and not a model (no model.json)
NAME    VERSION  STATUS  DICT
ipadic  7.0.0    ok      embedded://ipadic
ipadic  7.0.0    ok      /home/user/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/ipadic

The table, on stdout, has one dictionary per line: the embedded dictionaries first, then the subdirectories of the dictionaries directory, by name.

  • NAME is the kind of the embedded dictionary, or the name of the directory.
  • VERSION is the version of Lindera that built the dictionary (lindera_version in its metadata.json), or unknown for a dictionary built before v7.0.0.
  • STATUS is ok; incomplete when required files are missing (download it again with lindera download <name> --force); or other version when another version of Lindera built the dictionary, or one that does not say (for a downloadable dictionary, lindera download <name> replaces it).
  • DICT is the value to pass to --dict.

Messages go to stderr: a subdirectory with neither metadata.json nor model.json, such as the 6.2.0/ above, where a CLI before v7.0.0 put its downloads, is skipped with a line, and a dictionaries directory without dictionaries is reported with a hint to run lindera download. Entries whose name starts with . are skipped silently.

Models of the dependency parser

The models of the dependency parser follow in a table of their own, when there is one: the models embedded in the binary (the embed-dependency-ipadic feature flag, and embed-dependency-unidic, embed-dependency-unidic-cwj and embed-dependency-unidic-csj) and those that lindera download dependency-ipadic and the like installed, which are the subdirectories with a model.json.

NAME    VERSION  STATUS  DICT
ipadic  7.0.0    ok      embedded://ipadic

NAME               VERSION  STATUS  MODEL
dependency-ipadic  7.0.0    ok      /home/user/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/dependency-ipadic/dependency.model
  • VERSION is the version of Lindera that built the model (lindera_version in its model.json), or unknown for the embedded model, which does not say.
  • STATUS is as for a dictionary: ok, incomplete, or other version, which lindera download dependency-ipadic replaces.
  • MODEL is the value to pass as model to the token filter japanese_dependency: the model file, or embedded://ipadic.

tokenize

Perform morphological analysis (tokenization) on Japanese, Chinese, or Korean text using various dictionaries.

Parameters

  • --dict / -d: Dictionary URI or path (required)

    • File path: /path/to/dictionary, such as the path that lindera download prints, or file:///path/to/dictionary

    • Embedded: embedded://ipadic, embedded://unidic, etc.

    • A dictionary name alone, such as ipadic, is not accepted, unless a directory of that name exists. The error points to the embedded dictionary and to the directory of the downloaded one:

      Error: LinderaError { kind: Args, source: --dict takes a URI or a path, and 'ipadic' names a dictionary: pass embedded://ipadic for the dictionary embedded in the CLI, or the path of a downloaded one, /home/user/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/ipadic }

  • --output / -o: Output format (default: mecab)

    • mecab: MeCab-compatible format with part-of-speech info
    • wakati: Space-separated tokens only, one line per input line (an empty line for a line without tokens)
    • json: Detailed JSON format with all token information

  • --user-dict / -u: User dictionary path (optional). An entry whose context ID lies outside the system dictionary's connection matrix is an error (see Context IDs).

  • --mode / -m: Tokenization mode (default: normal)

    • normal: Standard tokenization
    • decompose: Decompose compound words

  • --char-filter / -c: Character filter configuration (JSON)

  • --token-filter / -t: Token filter configuration (JSON)

  • --keep-whitespace: Keep whitespace tokens in the output. Whitespace then also stays in the lattice, so the other tokens can differ from those of the default output, in which whitespace is dropped and, unless the dictionary's metadata.json turns it off (SudachiDict does), skipped in the lattice as MeCab does

  • --disable-skip-whitespace: Keep whitespace in the lattice as a node of its own (a whitespace dictionary entry or the SPACE unknown word) instead of skipping it, while still dropping it from the output (the behavior before v7). With ko-dic, whose connection costs for that node are all zero, every space then resets the connection context. Skipping is on by default for every dictionary whose metadata.json does not turn it off (SudachiDict does). No effect with --keep-whitespace. See the Segmenter documentation

  • --max-grouping-len: Cap on unknown-word grouping, in characters beyond the first (MeCab's max-grouping-size; MeCab defaults to 24). The cap is applied at each position: a run (characters that each share a char.def category with the one before, as in MeCab) longer than the cap is not grouped there, the single-character candidate (plus the length ladder and dictionary words) remains, and the remaining tail is grouped again once it fits, so no unknown token exceeds cap+1 characters. 0 or omitted: unbounded. See the Segmenter documentation for an example

  • --disable-unknown-word-ladder: Disable the MeCab/Vibrato-inspired unknown-word length ladder (char.def's LENGTH field). Enabled by default. Disabling it leaves out these candidates, as before v6; other changes since then, such as unknown words that start inside a grouped run, still apply. See the Segmenter documentation

  • --break-characters <CHARS>: Break characters, each character of CHARS (default: ・). No unknown word crosses a boundary between a break character and another character, in any mode, and in decompose mode no system-dictionary word does either; user-dictionary words and words of break characters only stay. See the Segmenter documentation

  • --disable-break-characters: Use no break characters, which gives MeCab's segmentation: with a dictionary whose char.def puts ・ in the katakana category (IPADIC and UniDic do, SudachiDict does not), an unknown katakana word runs through ・ (レノン・ジョン stays one word), while a dictionary word before it still ends there (ジョン・レノン splits). Cannot be combined with --break-characters

  • --disable-space-penalty: Disable the left-space penalty (mecab-ko's left-space-penalty-factor) that a dictionary shipping rules in its metadata.json applies by default (ko-dic ships mecab-ko-dic's). A candidate that starts right after whitespace and whose first part-of-speech tag is listed gets the cost added; disabling it together with --disable-skip-whitespace turns off both changes since v6.0 in how Korean is read around spaces (this penalty and whitespace skipping), but not the other output changes since then, such as the split of punctuation runs like .". See the Segmenter documentation

  • --space-penalty-rules: Use explicit left-space penalty rules as JSON instead of the dictionary's, e.g. '{"rules":[{"pos":["JKS","JX"],"cost":6000}]}'. Mutually exclusive with --disable-space-penalty

  • --mmap: Use memory-mapped file loading for the dictionary directory's word list. Ignored for embedded:// dictionaries and when the mmap feature is disabled. Rebuilding or truncating the dictionary directory while a process holds it mapped can cause a SIGBUS on the next lookup.

  • --nbest / -N: Number of N-best results to return (default: 1). When set to 2 or more, N-best output is enabled.

  • --nbest-unique: Deduplicate N-best results by removing paths that produce the same segmentation: each result is the cheapest path of its word boundaries.

  • --nbest-cost-threshold: Maximum cost difference from the best result. Only results with cost within best_cost + threshold are returned; both costs are totals over the whole input line.

  • --max-threads: Number of threads that tokenize, 1 or more (default: 1). The output is the same for every number. See Tokenizing on several threads

  • Input file: Optional file path (default: stdin). The input is read line by line, and each line is tokenized on its own. Only the line terminator (\n, or \r\n) is removed: whitespace at the start or end of a line is handled as elsewhere in the line (spaces and tabs, which are SPACE characters, are skipped and dropped from the output; U+3000 is a token with IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd and UniDic), and the byte offsets in the JSON output index the line. Unlike MeCab, which outputs the \r of a CRLF line as an unknown word, Lindera removes it

Basic usage

# Tokenize text using a dictionary directory
echo "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict /path/to/dictionary

# Tokenize text using embedded dictionary
echo "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic

# Tokenize with different output format
echo "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  --output json

# Tokenize text from file
lindera tokenize \
  --dict /path/to/dictionary \
  --output wakati \
  input.txt

습니다  EF,*,F,습니다,*,*,*,*
.       SF,*,*,*,*,*,*,*
EOS

User dictionary examples

Lindera supports user dictionaries to add custom words alongside system dictionaries. User dictionaries can be in CSV or binary format.

Use user dictionary (CSV format)

% echo "東京スカイツリーの最寄り駅はとうきょうスカイツリー駅です" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  --user-dict ./resources/user_dict/ipadic_simple_userdic.csv

東京スカイツリー        カスタム名詞,*,*,*,*,*,東京スカイツリー,トウキョウスカイツリー,*
の      助詞,連体化,*,*,*,*,の,ノ,ノ
最寄り駅        名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,最寄り駅,モヨリエキ,モヨリエキ
は      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,は,ハ,ワ
とうきょうスカイツリー駅        カスタム名詞,*,*,*,*,*,とうきょうスカイツリー駅,トウキョウスカイツリーエキ,*
です    助動詞,*,*,*,特殊・デス,基本形,です,デス,デス
EOS

Use user dictionary (Binary format)

% echo "東京スカイツリーの最寄り駅はとうきょうスカイツリー駅です" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict /tmp/lindera-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920 \
  --user-dict ./resources/user_dict/ipadic_simple_userdic.bin

とうきょうスカイツリー駅        カスタム名詞,*,*,*,*,*,とうきょうスカイツリー駅,トウキョウスカイツリーエキ,*
です    助動詞,*,*,*,特殊・デス,基本形,です,デス,デス

Tokenization modes

Lindera provides two tokenization modes: normal and decompose.

Normal mode (default)

Tokenizes faithfully based on words registered in the dictionary:

% echo "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  --mode normal

関西国際空港    名詞,固有名詞,組織,*,*,*,関西国際空港,カンサイコクサイクウコウ,カンサイコクサイクーコー
限定    名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,限定,ゲンテイ,ゲンテイ
トートバッグ    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,*,*,*
EOS

Decompose mode

Tokenizes compound noun words additionally:

% echo "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  --mode decompose

関西    名詞,固有名詞,地域,一般,*,*,関西,カンサイ,カンサイ
国際    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,国際,コクサイ,コクサイ
空港    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,空港,クウコウ,クーコー
限定    名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,限定,ゲンテイ,ゲンテイ
トートバッグ    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,*,*,*
EOS

Output formats

Lindera provides three output formats: mecab, wakati and json.

MeCab format (default)

Outputs results in MeCab-compatible format with part-of-speech information:

% echo "お待ちしております。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  --output mecab

お待ち  名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,お待ち,オマチ,オマチ
し  動詞,自立,*,*,サ変・スル,連用形,する,シ,シ
て  助詞,接続助詞,*,*,*,*,て,テ,テ
おり  動詞,非自立,*,*,五段・ラ行,連用形,おる,オリ,オリ
ます  助動詞,*,*,*,特殊・マス,基本形,ます,マス,マス
。  記号,句点,*,*,*,*,。,。,。
EOS

Wakati format

Outputs only the token text separated by spaces, one line per input line (or per result with -N). A line without tokens, such as an empty line or a line of spaces, gives an empty line, as in MeCab:

% echo "お待ちしております。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  --output wakati

お待ち し て おり ます 。

JSON format

Outputs detailed token information in JSON format:

% echo "お待ちしております。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  --output json

[
  {
    "base_form": "お待ち",
    "byte_end": 9,
    "byte_start": 0,
    "conjugation_form": "*",
    "conjugation_type": "*",
    "part_of_speech": "名詞",
    "part_of_speech_subcategory_1": "サ変接続",
    "part_of_speech_subcategory_2": "*",
    "part_of_speech_subcategory_3": "*",
    "pronunciation": "オマチ",
    "reading": "オマチ",
    "surface": "お待ち",
    "word_id": 14698
  },
  ...
]

byte_start, byte_end and word_id are numbers. The fields of the dictionary's schema are strings, with the text the dictionary has, even when it looks like a number: UniDic CWJ's lexicon_id, for example, goes beyond what a reader that holds numbers as doubles, such as JavaScript's JSON.parse, reads exactly, and comes back as written. Convert a field where you need a number.

N-Best tokenization

Lindera supports N-Best tokenization, which returns the top N tokenization candidates ordered by cost (lower cost = better). This is based on the Forward-DP Backward-A* algorithm, compatible with MeCab's N-Best implementation.

A line is cut into sentences at \t, 。 and 、, but the context is carried across 、 and 。, so the candidates for a line without a tab are the N best segmentations of the whole line (for the few exceptions, see Sentence Splitting). A tab ends a segment: a line with tabs is searched segment by segment, and its candidates are the N cheapest combinations of one path per segment. Every candidate segments the whole line.

Basic N-Best example

% echo "すもももももももものうち" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  -N 3

NBEST 1 (cost=21245)
すもも  名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,すもも,スモモ,スモモ
も      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,も,モ,モ
もも    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,もも,モモ,モモ
も      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,も,モ,モ
もも    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,もも,モモ,モモ
の      助詞,連体化,*,*,*,*,の,ノ,ノ
うち    名詞,非自立,副詞可能,*,*,*,うち,ウチ,ウチ
EOS
NBEST 2 (cost=24541)
すもも  名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,すもも,スモモ,スモモ
もも    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,もも,モモ,モモ
も      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,も,モ,モ
もも    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,もも,モモ,モモ
も      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,も,モ,モ
の      助詞,連体化,*,*,*,*,の,ノ,ノ
うち    名詞,非自立,副詞可能,*,*,*,うち,ウチ,ウチ
EOS
NBEST 3 (cost=24541)
すもも  名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,すもも,スモモ,スモモ
も      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,も,モ,モ
もも    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,もも,モモ,モモ
もも    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,もも,モモ,モモ
も      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,も,モ,モ
の      助詞,連体化,*,*,*,*,の,ノ,ノ
うち    名詞,非自立,副詞可能,*,*,*,うち,ウチ,ウチ
EOS

Results 2 and 3 are different segmentations with the same cost (24541).

N-Best with unique results

When the same segmentation appears in multiple paths (differing only in the dictionary entries of their words, such as their parts of speech), use --nbest-unique to deduplicate. Each result is then the cheapest path of its word boundaries, and the search does not go through the other paths, which can be millions for a short line:

% echo "営業部長谷川です" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  -N 5 --nbest-unique -o wakati

NBEST 1 (cost=15760)
営業 部長 谷川 です
NBEST 2 (cost=17747)
営業 部 長谷川 です
NBEST 3 (cost=18365)
営業 部 長谷 川 です
NBEST 4 (cost=21125)
営業 部 長 谷川 です
NBEST 5 (cost=22259)
営業 部長 谷 川 です

N-Best with cost threshold

Use --nbest-cost-threshold to limit results to paths within a certain cost range of the best path:

% echo "営業部長谷川です" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  -N 10 --nbest-unique --nbest-cost-threshold 5000 -o wakati

NBEST 1 (cost=15760)
営業 部長 谷川 です
NBEST 2 (cost=17747)
営業 部 長谷川 です
NBEST 3 (cost=18365)
営業 部 長谷 川 です

Only 3 results are returned: the 4th result of the example above costs 21125, which exceeds 15760 + 5000 = 20760.

Tokenizing on several threads

--max-threads N with N of 2 or more tokenizes the lines of the input on N threads. Every line is still tokenized on its own, by a tokenizer with the same settings, and the output is written in input order, so it is the same, byte for byte, as on one thread, in every output format, with N-best and with filters:

lindera tokenize --dict embedded://ipadic --max-threads 8 large.txt > large.mecab
  • One more thread reads the input, in chunks of whole lines, and the output of a chunk is written once the output of the chunks before it is. The chunks read but not yet written are bounded (2 per tokenizing thread), and so is the memory they take.
  • Every tokenizing thread holds its own copy of the user dictionary, if any; the system dictionary is shared.
  • As on one thread, the output is buffered: a line that cannot be read (not UTF-8) or tokenized ends the command with exit code 1 after the output of the lines before it, and a standard output without a reader ends it with exit code 0, without reading the rest of the input.
  • A warning, such as the one of a forced sentence cut, comes from the thread that tokenizes its line, so the warnings of several lines can reach stderr in another order than their lines.
  • The default is 1, unlike the default of lindera train --max-threads (the number of CPU cores), so that the CPU use and the memory of existing scripts stay as they were. A short input gains nothing from more threads.

Advanced tokenization with filters

Lindera provides an analytical framework that combines character filters, tokenizers, and token filters for advanced text processing. Filters are configured using JSON.

% echo "すもももももももものうち" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ipadic \
  --char-filter 'unicode_normalize:{"kind":"nfkc"}' \
  --token-filter 'japanese_keep_tags:{"tags":["名詞,一般"]}'

すもも  名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,すもも,スモモ,スモモ
もも    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,もも,モモ,モモ
もも    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,もも,モモ,モモ
EOS

build

Build (compile) a morphological analysis dictionary from source CSV files for use with Lindera.

Build parameters

  • --src / -s: Source directory containing dictionary CSV files (or single CSV file for user dictionary)
  • --dest / -d: Destination directory for compiled dictionary output
  • --metadata / -m: Metadata configuration file (metadata.json) that defines dictionary structure
  • --user / -u: Build user dictionary instead of system dictionary (optional flag)
  • --system-dict: The system dictionary the user dictionary is for, as a URI or a directory path, the forms tokenize --dict accepts (optional; only with --user). The build then checks every row's context IDs against its connection matrix (see Context ID check)
  • --context-id-freq / -f: Context-ID access-frequency file used to reorder connection-cost IDs (optional; only meaningful when the dictionary's metadata.json sets connection_id_mapping: true)

Dictionary types

System dictionary

A full morphological analysis dictionary containing:

  • Lexicon entries (word definitions)
  • Connection cost matrix
  • Unknown word handling rules
  • Character type definitions

User dictionary

A supplementary dictionary for custom words that works alongside a system dictionary.

Context ID check

When it builds a system dictionary, lindera build checks that every context ID lies inside the connection matrix, as MeCab's mecab-dict-index does. In every lex.csv row and unk.def line, the right context ID must be below the first value of the matrix.def header, and the left context ID below the second. A dictionary that breaks this fails to build, with an error that names the file, the line, the ID and the matrix size. For example, with a 2 x 2 matrix.def and a lex.csv whose second row has the right context ID 2:

Error: LinderaError { kind: Content, source: ./dict-source/lex.csv: line 2: right context id 2 is out of range for the connection matrix (matrix.def size 2 2; right context ids must be below 2) }
  • If the dictionary's metadata.json sets skip_invalid_cost_or_id to true, such a lex.csv row is dropped instead, with a warning on standard error (see Warnings and log messages). An unk.def line is always checked.
  • A matrix.def row whose IDs fall outside its axes is an error too, and so is an unk.def line with fewer than four fields.
  • A user dictionary (--user) is checked only when --system-dict names the system dictionary it is for, as described below.

With --system-dict, lindera build --user checks every row of the user dictionary against the connection matrix of that system dictionary, with the same bounds. A simple row is checked with the default context IDs of metadata.json (default_left_context_id and default_right_context_id). The first row outside the matrix fails the build, with an error that names its CSV line and surface, and no .bin file is written. For example, against IPADIC's 1316 x 1316 matrix, with a userdic.csv whose second row has the left context ID 60000:

% lindera build --src ./userdic.csv --dest ./user_dict --metadata ./lindera-ipadic/metadata.json --user --system-dict embedded://ipadic
Error: LinderaError { kind: Content, source: user dictionary line 2 (surface: '東京スカイツリー'): left context id 60000 is out of range for the connection matrix (matrix.def size 1316 1316; left context ids must be below 1316) }

Without --system-dict, the build does not know the system dictionary, and the user dictionary builds. lindera tokenize --user-dict then checks it against the system dictionary and fails with an error that names the first entry outside the matrix by its word id (see Context IDs). A .csv given to lindera tokenize --user-dict is built for the system dictionary of --dict as it is loaded, so its error names the CSV line and surface, as with --system-dict.

Cells missing from matrix.def

A matrix.def does not have to list every cell. lindera build gives a cell that it leaves out the cost 0, as MeCab's mecab-dict-index does. Up to v6.2.0, such a cell cost 32767 (i16::MAX), which made the connection very expensive. For example, with the following matrix.def, the connections from the right context ID 1 to the left context IDs 0 and 1 cost 10 and 20, and the other seven cells cost 0:

3 3
1 0 10
1 1 20

The bundled dictionaries and the matrix.def that lindera export writes list every cell, so this rule does not change them.

char.def and unk.def check

When it builds a system dictionary, lindera build also checks char.def and unk.def against each other, as mecab-dict-index does:

  • A range line of char.def names only categories defined on an earlier line.
  • Each category is defined once.
  • Every unk.def line names a category that char.def defines.
  • Every char.def category has at least one unk.def line.

A dictionary that breaks one of these fails to build, with an error that names the file, the category and, except for a category without an unk.def line, the line. Such a dictionary used to build, and then lindera tokenize panicked on a character of an undefined category, gave some categories the settings of others, stopped its output before a character that no word or unknown word covers, or ignored the unk.def line. For example, with a char.def that defines the SPACE category and an unk.def that has no SPACE line:

Error: LinderaError { kind: Content, source: ./dict-source/unk.def: no line for category SPACE, which char.def defines; every char.def category needs at least one unk.def line }

lindera train checks its --char-def and --unk-def in the same way before it trains (see Training Pipeline).

char.def format

A dictionary's metadata.json selects the format of its char.def with char_def_format (#1388):

  • "mecab", the default when the field is omitted: MeCab's format. The last line that covers a code point decides its categories, and the first of them, its default category, alone creates unknown words.
  • "sudachi": Sudachi's format, which SudachiDict uses. A code point gets the categories of every line that covers it. Besides the categories that the file defines, a range line can name ALL (every category) and the flags NOOOVBOW (no unknown word starts at the character) and NOOOVEOW (no unknown word starts right after it), and a code point can be outside the BMP. The file must define DEFAULT, cannot define ALL, NOOOVBOW or NOOOVEOW as a category, and can define at most 64 categories. Every category of a character creates unknown words, over runs cut as Sudachi cuts them, and a position where nothing else starts gets a one-character unknown word of DEFAULT, as in Sudachi. A character is whitespace (for --keep-whitespace, --disable-skip-whitespace and the left-space penalty) only when SPACE is its only category, so that the characters that ALL puts in every category, such as combining marks and ZWJ, are not.

lindera train reads --char-def in MeCab's format only.

Lexicon format

A dictionary's metadata.json selects the format of its lexicon CSV files with lexicon_format (#1389):

  • "mecab", the default when the field is omitted: MeCab's format. Every field is taken as written.
  • "sudachi": Sudachi's format, which SudachiDict uses. A backslash, u and four hex digits, or a backslash, u and one to six hex digits in braces, stand for the code point that the digits name, and the builder decodes them in every field, as Sudachi's dictionary builder does: SudachiDict writes http:// as http:\u002f\u002f and 1,2塁 as 1\u002c2塁. The escapes are decoded left to right, the text that one stands for is not decoded again, and a backslash before an escape stays, since there is no escape for the backslash itself. An escape for a value that is not a Unicode scalar value (a surrogate, or above U+10FFFF), or for NUL, which separates the details of an entry in a built dictionary, fails the build with an error that names the file and the line. The user dictionaries built for the dictionary, with lindera build --user and its metadata.json or from a .csv file loaded with the dictionary, are decoded in the same way.

unk.def is read as written in both formats, as Sudachi reads it.

Examples

Build IPADIC (Japanese dictionary)

# Download and extract IPADIC source files
% curl -L -o /tmp/mecab-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920.tar.gz "https://Lindera.dev/mecab-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920.tar.gz"
% tar zxvf /tmp/mecab-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920.tar.gz -C /tmp

# Build the dictionary
% lindera build \
  --src /tmp/mecab-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920 \
  --dest /tmp/lindera-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920 \
  --metadata ./lindera-ipadic/metadata.json

Build IPADIC NEologd (Japanese dictionary)

% curl -L -o /tmp/mecab-ipadic-neologd-0.0.7-20200820.tar.gz "https://lindera.dev/mecab-ipadic-neologd-0.0.7-20200820.tar.gz"
% tar zxvf /tmp/mecab-ipadic-neologd-0.0.7-20200820.tar.gz -C /tmp

  --src /tmp/mecab-ipadic-neologd-0.0.7-20200820 \

download

Download the pre-built dictionary archive matching the CLI version from the GitHub releases page and install it in the dictionaries directory. The same command gets the model of the dependency parser, which a release publishes next to the dictionaries: see Downloading the model of the dependency parser.

Download parameters

  • Name (required): a dictionary, one of ipadic, ipadic-neologd, unidic, unidic-cwj, unidic-csj, sudachidict, ko-dic, cc-cedict, jieba; or a model of the dependency parser, one of dependency-ipadic, dependency-unidic, dependency-unidic-cwj, dependency-unidic-csj: the one for the dictionary of that name
  • --force: Re-download and replace the dictionary or the model even when the CLI's version built it

Storage location

lindera download <name> installs the dictionary in <dictionaries directory>/<name>/ and prints that path, the value to pass to --dict. The LINDERA_DICTIONARIES_DIR environment variable names the dictionaries directory, by default lindera/dictionaries in the OS's local data directory; see LINDERA_DICTIONARIES_DIR for the default location on each OS and for LINDERA_DATA_DIR, the variable before v7.0.0.

A complete dictionary already in place is kept when the CLI's version built it, as the lindera_version of its metadata.json says. When another version of Lindera built it, or its metadata.json does not say, as for a dictionary built before v7.0.0, lindera download downloads it again without --force, and says so on stderr, for example Downloaded dictionary 'ipadic', replacing the one built by an unknown version of Lindera.

Download usage

% lindera download ipadic

Downloading https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases/download/v7.0.0/lindera-ipadic-7.0.0.zip
Downloaded dictionary 'ipadic'
/home/user/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/ipadic

On a terminal, a progress line follows the first line. The installed path is printed to stdout (progress and notices go to stderr), also when the dictionary is already there, so it can be captured in scripts and passed to tokenize:

% DICT_DIR=$(lindera download ipadic)
% echo "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。" | lindera tokenize --dict "$DICT_DIR"

Notes:

  • The archive version always matches the CLI version; running a development build whose version has no published release yet fails with HTTP 404.
  • Integrity is verified via the HTTPS transport and the ZIP archive's built-in per-file CRC32 checksums.
  • The largest dictionary (ipadic-neologd) is a ~305 MB download and requires roughly twice that amount of free disk space during extraction.

Downloading the model of the dependency parser

lindera download dependency-ipadic gets the model for IPADIC of the token filter japanese_dependency, lindera-dependency-ipadic-<version>.zip on the page of the release of the CLI's version, from 7.1.0 on. It installs it in <dictionaries directory>/dependency-ipadic/, next to the dictionaries, and prints the path of the model file in it, which is what the filter takes as model. dependency-unidic, dependency-unidic-cwj and dependency-unidic-csj get the models for UniDic the same way:

% MODEL=$(lindera download dependency-ipadic)
% DICT_DIR=$(lindera download ipadic)
% echo "彼は赤い花を見た。" | lindera tokenize --dict "$DICT_DIR" --output json \
    --token-filter "japanese_dependency:{\"model\":\"$MODEL\"}"

The directory holds dependency.model, model.json and NOTICE.txt, which has the license of the model. A model in place is kept when the CLI's version built it, as the lindera_version of its model.json says, and replaced otherwise, as a dictionary is. With the model in place:

% lindera download dependency-ipadic

Model 'dependency-ipadic' is already downloaded; use --force to re-download it
/home/user/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/dependency-ipadic/dependency.model

A version without a release, or with a release before 7.1.0, has no model to download:

Error: LinderaError { kind: NotFound, source: model archive not found: https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases/download/v7.0.0/lindera-dependency-ipadic-7.0.0.zip (HTTP 404). Version 7.0.0 may not have a published release yet; see https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases }

The filter needs a build of the CLI with the dependency feature. The model belongs to IPADIC: use it with that dictionary.

train

Train a new morphological analysis model from annotated corpus data. To use this feature, you must build with the train feature flag enabled. (The train feature flag is enabled by default.)

Train parameters

  • --seed / -s: Seed lexicon file (CSV format) to be weighted
  • --corpus / -c: Training corpus (annotated text)
  • --char-def / -C: Character definition file (char.def)
  • --unk-def / -u: Unknown word definition file (unk.def) to be weighted
  • --feature-def / -f: Feature definition file (feature.def)
  • --rewrite-def / -r: Rewrite rule definition file (rewrite.def)
  • --output / -o: Output model file
  • --lambda / -l: Regularization coefficient, finite and >= 0 (0 disables regularization); with l2, MeCab's learner's -c C is 1 / C (default: 1.0, MeCab's -c 1.0)
  • --regularization / -R: Regularization type: l1, l2, or elasticnet, in any case; elastic_net and elastic-net also select Elastic Net (default: l2)
  • --elastic-net-l1-ratio: L1 ratio for Elastic Net regularization (0.0-1.0), only used with --regularization elasticnet; 0 uses only L2, 1 uses only L1 (default: 0.5)
  • --max-iterations / -i: Maximum number of iterations for training, 1 or more (default: 100)
  • --eta / -e: Tolerance of the convergence test: training stops before --max-iterations once the relative change of the objective stays below this value for 3 iterations in a row; 0 disables the test (default: 0.00005, the default of MeCab's learner)
  • --max-threads / -t: Maximum number of threads, 1 or more (defaults to CPU core count; affects only speed, never the trained model)
  • --break-characters <CHARS> / --disable-break-characters: The break characters of the unknown-word candidates, as for lindera tokenize (default: ・). Train with the value the dictionary will be used with; the corpus's own tokens are kept whatever they span

Basic workflow

1. Prepare training files

Seed lexicon file (seed.csv):

The seed lexicon file contains initial dictionary entries used for training the CRF model. Each line represents a word entry with comma-separated fields:

  • Surface
  • Left context ID
  • Right context ID
  • Word cost
  • Part-of-speech tags (multiple fields)
  • Base form
  • Reading (katakana)
  • Pronunciation

Note: The exact field definitions differ between dictionary formats (IPADIC, UniDic, ko-dic, CC-CEDICT). Please refer to each dictionary's format specification for details.

外国,0,0,0,名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,外国,ガイコク,ガイコク
人,0,0,0,名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,人,ジン,ジン

The file is read as CSV, as lindera build reads lex.csv: a field may be quoted (",",0,0,0,...), and a line that starts with # is an entry, not a comment. See Seed Lexicon for the details.

Training corpus (corpus.txt):

The training corpus file contains annotated text data used to train the CRF model. Each line consists of:

  • A surface form (word) followed by a tab character
  • Comma-separated morphological features (part-of-speech tags, base form, reading, pronunciation)
  • Sentences are separated by "EOS" (End Of Sentence) markers
外国	名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,外国,ガイコク,ガイコク
人	名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,人,ジン,ジン
参政	名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,参政,サンセイ,サンセイ
権	名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,権,ケン,ケン
EOS

For detailed information about file formats and advanced features, see Training Pipeline.

2. Train model

lindera train \
  --seed ./resources/training/seed.csv \
  --corpus ./resources/training/corpus.txt \
  --unk-def ./resources/training/unk.def \
  --char-def ./resources/training/char.def \
  --feature-def ./resources/training/feature.def \
  --rewrite-def ./resources/training/rewrite.def \
  --output /tmp/lindera/training/model.dat \
  --max-iterations 100

3. Training results

lindera train writes the model to the --output file. Once it has built the training lattices, it prints how the gold tokens of the corpus were labelled (see How training works). With the files in ./resources/training/:

Lattice statistics: gold_lexicon=14 gold_unknown=0 gold_virtual=0 virtual_labels=0 negative_lexicon=0 negative_unknown=17

When no gold token is a seed word, or fewer than half of the gold tokens whose surface has seed rows are, it then writes a warning on stderr, with the first gold token whose surface has seed rows but none with its feature string, next to those rows (see How training works).

Once training stops, it prints why, with the number of iterations and of evaluations of the loss and its gradient (see --eta above):

L-BFGS stopped after 8 iterations and 9 evaluations of the loss and its gradient: converged

When an iteration left the objective unchanged or the line search failed far from the optimum, it then writes a warning on stderr (see How training works).

The trained model contains:

  • Seed words: every seed lexicon row, with a learned weight and context IDs
  • Unknown words: every unk.def entry, in file order, with a learned weight and context IDs

Corpus words that are not in the seed lexicon are not added as words. They are learned through the unk.def entries, or through virtual labels, which are trained but not exported.

export

Export a trained model file to Lindera dictionary format files. This feature requires building with the train feature flag enabled.

Export parameters

  • --model / -m: Path to the trained model file (.dat format)
  • --output / -o: Directory to output the dictionary files
  • --metadata: Optional metadata.json file to update with trained model information
  • --cost-factor: Override cost factor for weight-to-cost conversion (default: value from trained model, typically 700)

Output files

The export command creates the following dictionary files in the output directory:

  • lex.csv: Lexicon file with learned weights (MeCab-compatible cost via tocost())
  • matrix.def: Dense connection cost matrix covering all (right_id, left_id) pairs of the model's context IDs, plus 0 for BOS/EOS. A pair without a trained weight costs 0, as in training and in MeCab
  • unk.def: Unknown word definitions, one line for each unk.def entry of the training input, in the same order
  • char.def: Character type definitions
  • feature.def: Feature template definitions (copied from trained model)
  • rewrite.def: Feature rewrite rules (copied from trained model)
  • left-id.def: Left context ID to feature string mapping
  • right-id.def: Right context ID to feature string mapping
  • metadata.json: Updated metadata file (if --metadata option is provided)

Model format version

lindera export reads a model of the current format version (3.0.0) only. A model.dat written by an earlier version, which includes every model.dat written before 7.0.0, is rejected, and has to be trained again with lindera train. For a model trained with the 6.1.0 CLI:

Error: LinderaError { kind: Deserialize, source: failed to deserialize model: failed without error information; enable debug assertions and the `alloc` feature in rancor for error information. The file is not a legacy JSON model either, so it was most likely written by a different version of lindera-trainer; re-run `lindera train` to regenerate it. }

Complete workflow example

1. Train model

lindera train \
  --seed ./resources/training/seed.csv \
  --corpus ./resources/training/corpus.txt \
  --unk-def ./resources/training/unk.def \
  --char-def ./resources/training/char.def \
  --feature-def ./resources/training/feature.def \
  --rewrite-def ./resources/training/rewrite.def \
  --output /tmp/lindera/training/model.dat \
  --max-iterations 100

2. Export to dictionary format

lindera export \
  --model /tmp/lindera/training/model.dat \
  --metadata ./resources/training/metadata.json \
  --output /tmp/lindera/training/dictionary

3. Build dictionary

lindera build \
  --src /tmp/lindera/training/dictionary \
  --dest /tmp/lindera/training/compiled_dictionary \
  --metadata /tmp/lindera/training/dictionary/metadata.json

4. Use trained dictionary

echo "これは外国人参政権です。" | lindera tokenize -d /tmp/lindera/training/compiled_dictionary

これ	名詞,代名詞,一般,*,*,*,これ,コレ,コレ
は	助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,は,ハ,ワ
外国	名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,外国,ガイコク,ガイコク
人	名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,人,ジン,ジン
参政	名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,参政,サンセイ,サンセイ
権	名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,権,ケン,ケン
です	助動詞,*,*,*,特殊・デス,基本形,です,デス,デス
。	記号,句点,*,*,*,*,。,。,。
EOS

Metadata update feature

When the --metadata option is provided, the export command will:

  1. Read the base metadata.json file to preserve existing configuration
  2. Update specific fields with values from the trained model:
    • default_word_cost: Calculated from feature weight median
    • model_info: Training statistics including feature count, label count, matrix size (connection_matrix_size, the size of matrix.def as rows x columns), the number of training iterations that ran (training_iterations, at most --max-iterations), the regularization coefficient (regularization), its type (regularization_type: l1, l2 or elasticnet) and, for Elastic Net only, its L1 ratio (elastic_net_l1_ratio), and the model format version. No timestamp is written, so exporting the same model twice produces identical output
  3. Preserve existing settings such as dictionary name, character encoding, schema definitions, and other user-defined configuration

Tutorial

This tutorial walks you through the basic usage of the Lindera CLI, from installation to advanced text processing.

1. Install the CLI

Install Lindera CLI:

% cargo install lindera-cli

Verify the installation:

% lindera --help

2. Download a dictionary

Download the pre-built IPADIC dictionary from the GitHub releases page. It is installed in the dictionaries directory (~/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/ipadic on Linux), and lindera download prints its path, kept here in DICT_DIR for the steps below:

% DICT_DIR=$(lindera download ipadic)

See Commands for the available dictionary names and storage locations.

3. Basic tokenization

Tokenize Japanese text using the downloaded IPADIC dictionary, referencing it by its path:

% echo "東京は日本の首都です。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict "$DICT_DIR"

Expected output:

東京    名詞,固有名詞,地域,一般,*,*,東京,トウキョウ,トーキョー
は      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,は,ハ,ワ
日本    名詞,固有名詞,地域,国,*,*,日本,ニホン,ニホン
の      助詞,連体化,*,*,*,*,の,ノ,ノ
首都    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,首都,シュト,シュト
です    助動詞,*,*,*,特殊・デス,基本形,です,デス,デス
。      記号,句点,*,*,*,*,。,。,。
EOS

4. Try different output formats

Wakati format (word segmentation only)

% echo "東京は日本の首都です。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict "$DICT_DIR" \
  --output wakati

Expected output:

東京 は 日本 の 首都 です 。

JSON format (detailed information)

% echo "東京は日本の首都です。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict "$DICT_DIR" \
  --output json

This produces a JSON array with detailed token information including byte offsets, part-of-speech tags, readings, and more.

5. Use decompose mode

Decompose mode splits compound nouns into their constituent parts:

% echo "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict "$DICT_DIR" \
  --mode decompose

Expected output:

関西    名詞,固有名詞,地域,一般,*,*,関西,カンサイ,カンサイ
国際    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,国際,コクサイ,コクサイ
空港    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,空港,クウコウ,クーコー
限定    名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,限定,ゲンテイ,ゲンテイ
トートバッグ    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,*,*,*
EOS

Compare with normal mode, where "関西国際空港" remains as a single token.

6. Apply character and token filters

Use Unicode normalization and keep only common nouns:

% echo "Ｌｉｎｄｅｒａは形態素解析ｴﾝｼﾞﾝです。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict "$DICT_DIR" \
  --char-filter 'unicode_normalize:{"kind":"nfkc"}' \
  --token-filter 'japanese_keep_tags:{"tags":["名詞,一般","名詞,サ変接続","名詞,固有名詞,組織"]}'

Expected output:

Lindera 名詞,固有名詞,組織,*,*,*,*,*,*
形態素  名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,形態素,ケイタイソ,ケイタイソ
解析    名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,解析,カイセキ,カイセキ
エンジン        名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,エンジン,エンジン,エンジン
EOS

The Unicode normalization converts full-width characters to half-width, and the token filter keeps only tokens matching the specified part-of-speech tags.

You can also combine multiple filters:

% echo "すもももももももものうち" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict "$DICT_DIR" \
  --token-filter 'japanese_stop_tags:{"tags":["助詞,格助詞,一般","助詞,係助詞","助詞,連体化","助動詞"]}'

7. Use user dictionary

Create a CSV file with custom word entries (e.g., my_dict.csv):

東京スカイツリー,カスタム名詞,トウキョウスカイツリー

Tokenize with the user dictionary:

% echo "東京スカイツリーの最寄り駅はとうきょうスカイツリー駅です" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict "$DICT_DIR" \
  --user-dict ./my_dict.csv

Without the user dictionary, "東京スカイツリー" would be split into multiple tokens. With the user dictionary, it is recognized as a single token.

For pre-built user dictionary examples, see:

% echo "東京スカイツリーの最寄り駅はとうきょうスカイツリー駅です" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict "$DICT_DIR" \
  --user-dict ./resources/user_dict/ipadic_simple_userdic.csv

Expected output:

東京スカイツリー        カスタム名詞,*,*,*,*,*,東京スカイツリー,トウキョウスカイツリー,*
の      助詞,連体化,*,*,*,*,の,ノ,ノ
最寄り駅        名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,最寄り駅,モヨリエキ,モヨリエキ
は      助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,は,ハ,ワ
とうきょうスカイツリー駅        カスタム名詞,*,*,*,*,*,とうきょうスカイツリー駅,トウキョウスカイツリーエキ,*
です    助動詞,*,*,*,特殊・デス,基本形,です,デス,デス
EOS

Lindera Python

Lindera Python provides Python bindings for the Lindera morphological analysis engine, built with PyO3. It brings Lindera's high-performance tokenization capabilities to the Python ecosystem with support for Python 3.10 and later.

Features

  • Multi-language support: Tokenize Japanese (IPADIC, IPADIC NEologd, UniDic), Korean (ko-dic), and Chinese (CC-CEDICT, Jieba) text
  • Text processing pipeline: Compose character filters and token filters for flexible preprocessing and postprocessing
  • CRF-based dictionary training: Train custom morphological analysis models from annotated corpora (requires train feature)
  • Multiple tokenization modes: Normal and decompose modes for different analysis granularity
  • N-best tokenization: Retrieve multiple tokenization candidates ranked by cost
  • User dictionaries: Extend system dictionaries with custom vocabulary

Documentation

  • Installation -- Prerequisites, build instructions, and feature flags
  • Quick Start -- A minimal example to get started
  • Tokenizer API -- TokenizerBuilder, Tokenizer, and Token class reference
  • Dictionary Management -- Loading, building, and managing dictionaries
  • Text Processing Pipeline -- Character filters and token filters
  • Training -- Training custom CRF models and exporting dictionaries

Installation

Installing from PyPI

Pre-built wheels are available on PyPI:

pip install lindera

The wheels cover CPython 3.10 to 3.15 on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64, glibc), macOS (x86_64 and arm64), and Windows (x64 and arm64). On any other platform, such as musl-based Linux (Alpine), other CPU architectures, or free-threaded CPython, pip install lindera builds the package from the source distribution instead. That build needs the Rust toolchain 1.89 or later (install it via rustup) and a C linker such as cc, and takes several minutes.

[!NOTE] The PyPI package does not include dictionaries. See Obtaining Dictionaries below.

Obtaining Dictionaries

Lindera does not bundle dictionaries with the package. You need to obtain a pre-built dictionary separately.

Download from GitHub Releases

Pre-built dictionaries are available on the GitHub Releases page. Download and extract the dictionary archive to a local directory:

# Example: download and extract the IPADIC dictionary
curl -LO https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases/download/<version>/lindera-ipadic-<version>.zip
unzip lindera-ipadic-<version>.zip -d /path/to/ipadic

Building from Source

If you need to build from source (e.g., to enable specific feature flags), the following prerequisites are required:

  • Python 3.10 or later (up to 3.15)
  • Rust toolchain -- Install via rustup
  • maturin -- Python package for building Rust-based Python extensions

Install maturin with pip:

pip install maturin

Development Build

Build and install lindera-python in development mode:

cd lindera-python
maturin develop

Or let the project Makefile create the virtual environment that maturin develop installs into: make setup-venv creates lindera-python/.venv with maturin and pytest installed:

make setup-venv
source lindera-python/.venv/bin/activate
cd lindera-python
maturin develop

Build with Training Support

The train feature enables CRF-based dictionary training functionality. It is enabled by default:

maturin develop --features train

Feature Flags

FeatureDescriptionDefault
trainCRF training functionalityEnabled
embed-ipadicEmbed Japanese dictionary (IPADIC) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidicEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidic-cwjEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic CWJ, 1.2 GB) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidic-csjEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic CSJ, 1.2 GB) into the binaryDisabled
embed-sudachidictEmbed Japanese dictionary (SudachiDict) into the binaryDisabled
embed-ipadic-neologdEmbed Japanese dictionary (IPADIC NEologd) into the binaryDisabled
embed-ko-dicEmbed Korean dictionary (ko-dic) into the binaryDisabled
embed-cc-cedictEmbed Chinese dictionary (CC-CEDICT) into the binaryDisabled
embed-jiebaEmbed Chinese dictionary (Jieba) into the binaryDisabled
embed-cjkEmbed all CJK dictionaries (IPADIC, ko-dic, Jieba) into the binaryDisabled

Multiple features can be combined:

maturin develop --features "train,embed-ipadic,embed-ko-dic"

[!TIP] If you want to embed a dictionary directly into the binary (advanced usage), enable the corresponding embed-* feature flag and load it using the embedded:// scheme:

dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")

See Feature Flags for details.

Verifying the Installation

After installation, verify that lindera is available in Python:

import lindera

print(lindera.version())

Quick Start

This guide shows how to tokenize text using lindera-python.

Basic Tokenization

The recommended way to create a tokenizer is through TokenizerBuilder:

from lindera import Mode, TokenizerBuilder

builder = TokenizerBuilder()
builder.set_mode(Mode.normal())
builder.set_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
tokenizer = builder.build()

tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("関西国際空港限定トートバッグ")
for token in tokens:
    print(f"{token.surface}\t{','.join(token.details)}")

Note: Download a pre-built dictionary from GitHub Releases and specify the path to the extracted directory.

Expected output:

関西国際空港    名詞,固有名詞,組織,*,*,*,関西国際空港,カンサイコクサイクウコウ,カンサイコクサイクーコー
限定    名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,限定,ゲンテイ,ゲンテイ
トートバッグ    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,*,*,*

Method Chaining

TokenizerBuilder supports method chaining for concise configuration:

from lindera import Mode, TokenizerBuilder

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_mode(Mode.normal())
    .set_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
    .build()
)

tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("すもももももももものうち")
for token in tokens:
    print(f"{token.surface}\t{token.get_detail(0)}")

Accessing Token Properties

Each token exposes the following properties:

from lindera import TokenizerBuilder

tokenizer = TokenizerBuilder().set_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic").build()
tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("東京タワー")

for token in tokens:
    print(f"Surface: {token.surface}")
    print(f"Byte range: {token.byte_start}..{token.byte_end}")
    print(f"Position: {token.position}")
    print(f"Word ID: {token.word_id}")
    print(f"Unknown: {token.is_unknown}")
    print(f"Details: {token.details}")
    print()

N-best Tokenization

Retrieve multiple tokenization candidates ranked by cost:

from lindera import TokenizerBuilder

tokenizer = TokenizerBuilder().set_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic").build()
results = tokenizer.tokenize_nbest("すもももももももものうち", n=3)

for tokens, cost in results:
    surfaces = [t.surface for t in tokens]
    print(f"Cost {cost}: {' / '.join(surfaces)}")

Tokenizer API

TokenizerBuilder

TokenizerBuilder configures and constructs a Tokenizer instance using the builder pattern.

Constructors

TokenizerBuilder()

Creates a new builder with default configuration.

from lindera import TokenizerBuilder

builder = TokenizerBuilder()

TokenizerBuilder().from_file(file_path)

Loads configuration from a YAML file and returns a new builder. See lindera-python/resources/lindera.yml for a complete example covering segmenter, character_filters, and token_filters.

builder = TokenizerBuilder().from_file("lindera.yml")

Configuration Methods

All setter methods return self for method chaining.

set_mode(mode)

Sets the tokenization mode. mode is a Mode:

  • Mode.normal() -- Standard tokenization (default)
  • Mode.decompose(penalty=None) -- Decomposes compound words into smaller units, with the length penalties of a Penalty; None uses the default penalty

A value that is not a Mode, such as the string "normal", raises TypeError. To set a mode from its name, such as a configuration value, create it with Mode.from_str().

from lindera import Mode, Penalty

builder.set_mode(Mode.normal())
builder.set_mode(Mode.decompose(Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_penalty=0)))
builder.set_mode(Mode.from_str("decompose"))

set_dictionary(path)

Sets the system dictionary path or URI.

# Use an embedded dictionary
builder.set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")

# Use an external dictionary
builder.set_dictionary("/path/to/dictionary")

set_user_dictionary(uri)

Sets the user dictionary URI.

builder.set_user_dictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv")

set_keep_whitespace(keep)

Controls whether whitespace tokens appear in the output. Kept whitespace also stays in the lattice, so the other tokens can differ from those of the default output, which skips whitespace in the lattice as MeCab does. To keep whitespace in the lattice without outputting it, use set_skip_whitespace(False) instead.

builder.set_keep_whitespace(True)

set_skip_whitespace(skip)

Sets whether whitespace is skipped in the lattice. skip has the same meaning as segmenter.skip_whitespace in a configuration file:

  • True -- Skips whitespace, so the words on either side of it connect directly, as MeCab does.
  • False -- Keeps whitespace in the lattice as a node of its own (a whitespace dictionary entry or the SPACE unknown word), as before v7. Whitespace is still dropped from the output.
  • None -- The default of the dictionary's metadata.json: skipping, except with SudachiDict. Use it to undo an earlier call.

A value set here overrides the dictionary's default and a skip_whitespace loaded with from_file. It has no effect while whitespace tokens are kept (set_keep_whitespace(True)), because kept whitespace always stays in the lattice. Any other value raises TypeError.

With IPADIC, for example, Google が 新しい reads が as a particle (助詞) by default and as a conjunction (接続詞) with set_skip_whitespace(False). See Segmenter for details.

# Keep whitespace in the lattice, as before v7
builder.set_skip_whitespace(False)

set_break_characters(chars)

Sets the break characters. chars has the same meaning as segmenter.break_characters in a configuration file:

  • A string -- Each of its characters is a break character: no unknown word crosses a boundary between a break character and another character, and in decompose mode no system-dictionary word does either. User-dictionary words and words made of break characters only stay.
  • "" -- No break characters, which gives MeCab's segmentation.
  • None -- The default, ・. Use it to undo an earlier call.

A value set here overrides a break_characters loaded with from_file. Any other value raises TypeError.

With IPADIC, for example, レノン・ジョン, which is not in the dictionary, is レノン, ・ and ジョン by default and one unknown word with set_break_characters(""). See Segmenter for details.

# Split as MeCab does
builder.set_break_characters("")

set_space_penalty(value)

Sets the left-space penalty for Korean: a candidate that starts right after whitespace and whose part-of-speech tag normally attaches to the preceding word (particles, endings, ...) gets a cost added. value has the same meaning as segmenter.space_penalty in a configuration file:

  • None -- The default: the rules the dictionary ships in its metadata.json, if any (ko-dic ships mecab-ko-dic's rules; the other bundled dictionaries ship none). Use it to undo an earlier call.
  • False -- Turns the penalty off.
  • True -- Requires the dictionary's rules; build() raises ValueError for a dictionary that ships none.
  • A dict of the form {"rules": [{"pos": [...], "cost": n}, ...]} -- Applies these rules instead. A candidate whose first part-of-speech tag is listed in pos gets cost added; the first matching rule wins.

Any other value raises ValueError (a value with no JSON equivalent, such as an arbitrary object, raises TypeError, as in append_token_filter).

# Turn the penalty off
builder.set_space_penalty(False)

# Explicit rules
builder.set_space_penalty({
    "rules": [
        {"pos": ["EC", "EF", "EP", "ETM", "ETN", "VCP", "XSA", "XSN", "XSV"], "cost": 3000},
        {"pos": ["JC", "JKB", "JKC", "JKG", "JKO", "JKQ", "JKS", "JKV", "JX"], "cost": 6000},
    ]
})

[!NOTE] Since v6.1.0, ko-dic applies the left-space penalty by default, as mecab-ko does. For example, 검색 이 잘 된다 reads 이 as the interjection IC; without the penalty, as the subject particle JKS. Call builder.set_space_penalty(False) to turn it off. Only a ko-dic built by Lindera 6.1.0 or later ships the rules; with a ko-dic from the v6.0.0 release the penalty stays off and True fails until the dictionary is rebuilt. See Segmenter for details.

append_character_filter(kind, args=None)

Appends a character filter to the preprocessing pipeline.

builder.append_character_filter("unicode_normalize", {"kind": "nfkc"})

append_token_filter(kind, args=None)

Appends a token filter to the postprocessing pipeline.

builder.append_token_filter("lowercase", {})

The arguments of set_space_penalty, append_character_filter and append_token_filter may nest lists and dicts at most 128 levels deep. A deeper value, or one that contains itself, raises ValueError.

Build

build()

Builds and returns a Tokenizer with the configured settings.

tokenizer = builder.build()

Tokenizer

Tokenizer performs morphological analysis on text.

Creating a Tokenizer

Tokenizer(dictionary, mode=None, user_dictionary=None, space_penalty=None)

Creates a tokenizer directly from a loaded dictionary.

mode takes a Mode, as TokenizerBuilder.set_mode does; None (the default) is normal mode. Any other value, such as the string "normal", raises TypeError.

space_penalty takes the same values as TokenizerBuilder.set_space_penalty. None (the default) uses the left-space penalty rules the dictionary ships, so with ko-dic the penalty is on; pass False to turn it off. An invalid setting raises the same errors as set_space_penalty and build().

from lindera import Mode, Tokenizer, load_dictionary

dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
tokenizer = Tokenizer(dictionary, mode=Mode.normal())

# ko-dic without the left-space penalty
ko_tokenizer = Tokenizer(load_dictionary("embedded://ko-dic"), space_penalty=False)

Tokenizer Methods

tokenize(text)

Tokenizes the input text and returns a list of Token objects.

tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("形態素解析")

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
textstrText to tokenize

Returns: list[Token]

tokenize_surfaces(text)

Tokenizes the input text and returns only the token surfaces, as a list of strings. This is the fast path for wakati-style use: no Token objects are created and no morphological details are loaded, so it is significantly faster than tokenize when only the surface strings are needed. The result equals [t.surface for t in tokenizer.tokenize(text)].

surfaces = tokenizer.tokenize_surfaces("形態素解析")
# ["形態素", "解析"]

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
textstrText to tokenize

Returns: list[str]

tokenize_nbest(text, n, unique=False, cost_threshold=None)

Returns the N-best tokenization results, each paired with its total path cost.

results = tokenizer.tokenize_nbest("すもももももももものうち", n=3)
for tokens, cost in results:
    print(cost, [t.surface for t in tokens])

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
textstrText to tokenize
nintNumber of results to return
uniqueboolDeduplicate results (default: False)
cost_thresholdint or NoneMaximum cost difference from the best path (default: None)

Returns: list[tuple[list[Token], int]]

tokenize_batch(texts, max_threads=None)

Tokenizes every text of a list, each as tokenize does, on up to max_threads threads, and returns their tokens in the order of the texts. The results are the same for every number of threads. The texts are tokenized with the GIL released, so other Python threads run meanwhile; the Token objects are made afterwards.

batch = tokenizer.tokenize_batch(["形態素解析", "すもももももももものうち"])
for tokens in batch:
    print([t.surface for t in tokens])

Every text is tokenized as a call of its own: a list of the lines of a document gives the tokens of each line, not those of the whole document as one text. A short list runs on one thread (a thread needs at least 16 KiB of input), and every thread holds its own copy of the user dictionary, if any. A batch whose results are large, such as the tokens of several megabytes of text, can run faster on fewer threads than the default: when many threads make the memory of the tokens at once, much of the time goes to the kernel.

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
textslist[str]Texts to tokenize (a single str raises TypeError)
max_threadsint or NoneThe most threads, 1 or more (default: None, the number of CPUs); 0 raises ValueError

Returns: list[list[Token]]

tokenize_surfaces_batch(texts, max_threads=None)

Tokenizes every text of a list as tokenize_surfaces does, on up to max_threads threads, as tokenize_batch does.

Parameters: as tokenize_batch.

Returns: list[list[str]]

tokenize_nbest_batch(texts, n, unique=False, cost_threshold=None, max_threads=None)

Tokenizes every text of a list as tokenize_nbest does, on up to max_threads threads, as tokenize_batch does. n, unique and cost_threshold apply to each text.

Parameters: texts and max_threads as tokenize_batch; n, unique and cost_threshold as tokenize_nbest.

Returns: list[list[tuple[list[Token], int]]]

Mode

Mode is the tokenization mode that TokenizerBuilder.set_mode() and the Tokenizer constructor take. It is the counterpart of the Rust lindera::mode::Mode: normal mode, or decompose mode with its Penalty.

Creating a Mode

Mode has no constructor, so Mode() raises TypeError, and it has no Mode.Normal or Mode.Decompose attributes. Create a mode with one of the following static methods.

Mode.normal()

Returns normal mode: standard tokenization.

Mode.decompose(penalty=None)

Returns decompose mode, which adds the length penalties of penalty to the cost of long words, so that compound words are decomposed into smaller units. None (the default) uses the default penalty, Penalty(). A value that is not a Penalty raises TypeError.

Mode.from_str(name)

Returns the mode named name, as the Rust Mode parses a name: "normal" for normal mode, and "decompose" for decompose mode with the default penalty. Use it for a mode name read at run time, such as a configuration value. The name is case sensitive: any other name, such as "Normal", raises ValueError with the message Invalid mode. A value that is not a str raises TypeError.

from lindera import Mode, Penalty

normal = Mode.normal()
decompose = Mode.decompose()
whole_words = Mode.decompose(Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_penalty=0, other_penalty_length_penalty=0))
from_name = Mode.from_str("decompose")  # equal to Mode.decompose()

Mode Properties

Both properties are read-only:

PropertyTypeDescription
namestr"normal" or "decompose"
penaltyPenalty or NoneA copy of the penalty of decompose mode; None for normal mode

Methods

MethodReturnsDescription
__str__()strThe name: "normal" or "decompose"
__repr__()str"Mode.normal()", or Mode.decompose(...) with the penalty
__eq__(other)boolTrue if other is a Mode with the same name and penalty
is_normal()boolTrue for normal mode
is_decompose()boolTrue for decompose mode
mode = Mode.decompose()
mode.name              # 'decompose'
mode.penalty           # Penalty(kanji_threshold=2, kanji_penalty=3000, other_threshold=7, other_penalty=1700)
str(mode)              # 'decompose'
repr(mode)             # 'Mode.decompose(Penalty(kanji_threshold=2, kanji_penalty=3000, other_threshold=7, other_penalty=1700))'
mode.is_normal()       # False
mode.is_decompose()    # True
Mode.normal().penalty  # None
repr(Mode.normal())    # 'Mode.normal()'

Two modes are equal when their names and penalties are, as the Rust Mode compares them. A Mode is never equal to a value of another type, such as the string "normal":

Mode.from_str("decompose") == Mode.decompose()                               # True
Mode.decompose() == Mode.decompose(Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_penalty=0))  # False
Mode.normal() == "normal"                                                    # False

A Mode cannot be changed. Setting a property raises AttributeError, and penalty returns a copy, so changing the returned Penalty leaves the mode as it was; Mode.decompose() keeps a copy of the Penalty it is given as well. A Mode is not hashable, as the Rust Mode implements Eq but not Hash: hash(mode) raises TypeError, so a Mode cannot be a dict key or a set member.

mode = Mode.decompose()
penalty = mode.penalty
penalty.kanji_penalty_length_penalty = 0
mode.penalty.kanji_penalty_length_penalty  # 3000

Penalty

Penalty configures the length-based penalty thresholds used by decompose mode segmentation.

Creating a Penalty

Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_threshold=2, kanji_penalty_length_penalty=3000, other_penalty_length_threshold=7, other_penalty_length_penalty=1700)

All arguments are optional and default to the values shown above.

from lindera import Penalty

penalty = Penalty(
    kanji_penalty_length_threshold=2,
    kanji_penalty_length_penalty=3000,
    other_penalty_length_threshold=7,
    other_penalty_length_penalty=1700,
)

Penalty Properties

All four fields support both getting and setting:

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
kanji_penalty_length_thresholdint2Kanji-only surface length above which the penalty applies
kanji_penalty_length_penaltyint3000Cost penalty added for kanji-only surfaces longer than the threshold
other_penalty_length_thresholdint7Surface length above which the penalty applies for non-kanji-only surfaces
other_penalty_length_penaltyint1700Cost penalty added for non-kanji-only surfaces longer than the threshold
penalty.kanji_penalty_length_threshold = 3
print(penalty.kanji_penalty_length_threshold)  # 3

Using a Penalty

Pass a Penalty to Mode.decompose(), and the mode to TokenizerBuilder.set_mode() or to the Tokenizer constructor. Without length penalties, decompose mode keeps long words whole:

from lindera import Mode, Penalty, Tokenizer, TokenizerBuilder, load_dictionary

text = "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ"
penalty = Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_penalty=0, other_penalty_length_penalty=0)

builder = TokenizerBuilder().set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
tokenizer = builder.set_mode(Mode.decompose()).build()
print([token.surface for token in tokenizer.tokenize(text)])
# ['関西', '国際', '空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ']

tokenizer = builder.set_mode(Mode.decompose(penalty)).build()
print([token.surface for token in tokenizer.tokenize(text)])
# ['関西国際空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ']

tokenizer = Tokenizer(load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic"), mode=Mode.decompose(penalty))
print([token.surface for token in tokenizer.tokenize(text)])
# ['関西国際空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ']

Normal mode has no penalty: Mode.normal() takes no arguments.

Token

Token represents a single morphological token.

Properties

PropertyTypeDescription
surfacestrSurface form of the token
byte_startintStart byte position in the original text
byte_endintEnd byte position in the original text
positionintToken position index
word_idintDictionary word ID
is_unknownboolTrue if the word is not in the dictionary
detailslist[str] or NoneMorphological details (part of speech, reading, etc.)
dependencyTokenDependency or NoneThe bunsetsu of the token and its head; None unless the token filter japanese_dependency ran

Token Methods

get_detail(index)

Returns the detail string at the specified index, or None if the index is out of range.

token = tokenizer.tokenize("東京")[0]
pos = token.get_detail(0)        # e.g., "名詞"
subpos = token.get_detail(1)     # e.g., "固有名詞"
reading = token.get_detail(7)    # e.g., "トウキョウ"

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
indexintZero-based index into the details list

Returns: str or None

to_dict()

Returns the token as a plain dict, keeping each field's natural Python type, so it serializes without a custom encoder.

import json

data = tokenizer.tokenize("東京")[0].to_dict()
# {'surface': '東京', 'byte_start': 0, 'byte_end': 6, 'position': 0,
#  'word_id': 12345, 'is_unknown': False, 'details': [...]}

json.dumps([token.to_dict() for token in tokens])

Returns: dict with the keys surface, byte_start, byte_end, position, word_id, is_unknown, and details.

The structure of details depends on the dictionary:

  • IPADIC: [品詞, 品詞細分類1, 品詞細分類2, 品詞細分類3, 活用型, 活用形, 原形, 読み, 発音]
  • UniDic: Detailed morphological features following the UniDic specification
  • ko-dic / CC-CEDICT / Jieba: Dictionary-specific detail formats

TokenDependency

The bunsetsu of a token and the bunsetsu it depends on. The token filter japanese_dependency puts it in the dependency of every token; see Token Filter for the filter, its model, and how a text is cut into sentences.

The distributed packages have the filter, from 7.1.0 on: the dependency feature is in the default build. They have no model. The filter takes the path of a model file: the one Lindera releases for IPADIC is dependency.model in lindera-dependency-ipadic-<version>.zip, on the page of each release, which lindera download dependency-ipadic also installs (Installation). There is one for each of unidic, unidic-cwj and unidic-csj too, with the name of the dictionary in place of ipadic.

PropertyTypeDescription
sentenceintThe number of the sentence in the text, from 0
bunsetsuintThe number of the bunsetsu of the token in its sentence, from 0
