headint or NoneThe number of the bunsetsu that one depends on; None for the last bunsetsu of a sentence
rolestrWhat the token is in its bunsetsu: head (the head word), function (the function word), head_function (both) or other
scorefloatThe score of the decision that attached the bunsetsu to its head; 0 where nothing was decided
from lindera import TokenizerBuilder

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    .append_token_filter("japanese_dependency", {"model": "ipadic.model"})
    .build()
)
for token in tokenizer.tokenize("彼は赤い花を見た。"):
    dependency = token.dependency
    print(token.surface, dependency.bunsetsu, dependency.head, dependency.role)

彼 0 3 head
は 0 3 function
赤い 1 2 head_function
花 2 3 head
を 2 3 function
見 3 None head
た 3 None function
。 3 None other

TokenDependency.to_dict() returns the five fields as a dict, and Token.to_dict() has it under the key dependency (None without the filter). A TokenDependency cannot be changed.

Error Handling

Lindera Python functions raise standard Python exceptions rather than a custom exception type:

  • IOError (an alias of OSError) -- for I/O-related failures, such as a missing or unreadable file
  • ValueError -- for everything else, such as invalid configuration, parse errors, or tokenization failures
from lindera import load_dictionary

try:
    dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/that/does/not/exist")
except ValueError as e:
    print(f"Failed to load dictionary: {e}")

A LinderaError class is also registered as lindera.LinderaError, but no function in this crate currently raises it -- it can only be constructed and raised manually. Catch IOError/ValueError (or the general Exception) when handling errors from this library, not LinderaError.

Dictionary Management

Lindera Python provides functions for loading, building, and managing dictionaries used in morphological analysis.

Loading Dictionaries

System Dictionaries

Use load_dictionary(uri) to load a system dictionary. Download a pre-built dictionary from GitHub Releases and specify the path to the extracted directory:

from lindera import load_dictionary

dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")

Embedded dictionaries (advanced) -- if you built with an embed-* feature flag, you can load an embedded dictionary:

dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")

A loaded Dictionary also exposes its own metadata:

print(dictionary.metadata_name())      # e.g. "ipadic"
print(dictionary.metadata_encoding())  # e.g. "UTF-8"
metadata = dictionary.metadata()       # the full Metadata object

A user dictionary must share the metadata (schema, encoding, etc.) of the system dictionary it augments. load_user_dictionary_for takes the system dictionary and uses its metadata, as in lindera-python/examples/tokenize_with_userdict.py (see User Dictionaries).

User Dictionaries

User dictionaries add custom vocabulary on top of a system dictionary. Load one for the system dictionary it is used with:

from lindera import load_dictionary, load_user_dictionary_for

dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
user_dict = load_user_dictionary_for("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", dictionary)

A .csv is built with the system dictionary's metadata and checked against its connection matrix as it is built: a row whose context ID lies outside the matrix raises a ValueError that names its CSV line and surface (see Context IDs). A .bin is loaded as it was built.

load_user_dictionary(uri, metadata) loads a user dictionary with metadata only. A .csv loaded this way is checked when it is combined with the system dictionary, and the error names the entry by its word id:

from lindera import load_user_dictionary, Metadata

metadata = Metadata()
user_dict = load_user_dictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", metadata)

Pass the user dictionary when building a tokenizer:

from lindera import Mode, Tokenizer, load_dictionary, load_user_dictionary_for

dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
user_dict = load_user_dictionary_for("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", dictionary)

tokenizer = Tokenizer(dictionary, mode=Mode.normal(), user_dictionary=user_dict)

Or via the builder:

from lindera import TokenizerBuilder

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
    .set_user_dictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv")
    .build()
)

Building Dictionaries

System Dictionary

Build a system dictionary from source files:

from lindera import build_dictionary, Metadata

metadata = Metadata(name="custom", encoding="UTF-8")
build_dictionary("/path/to/input_dir", "/path/to/output_dir", metadata)

The input directory should contain the dictionary source files (CSV lexicon, matrix.def, etc.).

Metadata loaded with Metadata.from_json_file keeps the space_penalty rules of the metadata.json, and the built dictionary ships them. For ko-dic this means the left-space penalty stays on by default in the dictionary you build; turn it off per tokenizer with TokenizerBuilder.set_space_penalty(False) (see Tokenizer API). A Metadata created with the constructor carries no rules.

Metadata loaded with Metadata.from_json_file also keeps connection_id_mapping, which the metadata.json of ko-dic, UniDic, UniDic CWJ and UniDic CSJ enables. The build then relabels the context IDs of the connection matrix by access frequency, as lindera build does, to improve the cache locality of connection-cost lookups; the results of tokenization do not change. Pass a context-ID frequency histogram as context_id_freq, such as the context_id_freq.txt of the dictionary crate, to rank the IDs by their frequency in a corpus, as lindera build --context-id-freq does. Without one, the IDs are ranked by the count of dictionary entries, a much weaker proxy. A dictionary without connection_id_mapping does not read the histogram.

metadata = Metadata.from_json_file("/path/to/lindera-ko-dic/metadata.json")
build_dictionary(
    "/path/to/mecab-ko-dic",
    "/path/to/output_dir",
    metadata,
    context_id_freq="/path/to/lindera-ko-dic/context_id_freq.txt",
)

User Dictionary

Build a user dictionary from a CSV file for the system dictionary it is used with:

from lindera import build_user_dictionary_for, load_dictionary, load_user_dictionary_for

dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
build_user_dictionary_for("user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", dictionary)
user_dict = load_user_dictionary_for("/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", dictionary)

The CSV is built with the system dictionary's metadata and checked against its connection matrix: a row whose context ID lies outside the matrix raises a ValueError that names its CSV line and surface, and no file is written (see Context IDs). The second argument is the path of the file to write. End it with .bin, since the loaders choose how to load a user dictionary by its extension.

build_user_dictionary(kind, input_file, output_dir, metadata) builds a user dictionary with metadata only. Despite its name, output_dir is the path of the file to write too, not a directory. The rows are checked when the user dictionary is combined with the system dictionary, and the error names the entry by its word id:

from lindera import build_user_dictionary, Metadata

metadata = Metadata()
build_user_dictionary("ipadic", "user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", metadata)

The metadata parameter is optional. When omitted, default metadata values are used:

build_user_dictionary("ipadic", "user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin")

Note: the first argument ("ipadic" above) is currently unused and reserved for future use -- it does not select or configure the build in any way. The build behavior is controlled entirely by metadata (in particular metadata.user_dictionary_schema). Any string may be passed today. To build for a system dictionary, use build_user_dictionary_for.

Metadata

The Metadata class configures dictionary parameters.

Creating Metadata

from lindera import Metadata

# Default metadata
metadata = Metadata()

# Custom metadata
metadata = Metadata(
    name="my_dictionary",
    encoding="UTF-8",
    default_word_cost=-10000,
)

Loading from JSON

metadata = Metadata.from_json_file("metadata.json")

Properties

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
namestr"default"Dictionary name
encodingstr"UTF-8"Character encoding
default_word_costint-10000Default cost for unknown words
default_left_context_idint1288Default left context ID
default_right_context_idint1288Default right context ID
default_field_valuestr"*"Default value for missing fields
flexible_csvboolFalseAllow flexible CSV parsing
skip_invalid_cost_or_idboolFalseSkip entries with invalid cost or ID
dictionary_schemaSchemaIPADIC schemaSchema for the main dictionary
user_dictionary_schemaSchemaMinimal schemaSchema for user dictionaries

All properties support both getting and setting:

metadata = Metadata()
metadata.name = "custom_dict"
metadata.encoding = "EUC-JP"
print(metadata.name)  # "custom_dict"

to_dict()

Returns the metadata as a dict of strings: the properties above, with dictionary_schema_fields and user_dictionary_schema_fields (comma-separated field names) in place of the two schemas.

metadata = Metadata(name="test")
print(metadata.to_dict())

When the metadata carries left-space penalty rules, as ko-dic's does, the dict also has a space_penalty entry holding them as a JSON string; the key is absent otherwise:

metadata = Metadata.from_json_file("/path/to/ko-dic/metadata.json")
metadata.to_dict()["space_penalty"]
# '{"rules":[{"pos":["EC","EF",...],"cost":3000},{"pos":["JC","JKB",...],"cost":6000}]}'

Schema

Schema, FieldDefinition, and FieldType describe the field layout of a dictionary entry. A schema is used by Metadata.dictionary_schema and Metadata.user_dictionary_schema (see the table above).

FieldType

FieldType enumerates the category of a single field:

  • FieldType.Surface -- surface form (word text)
  • FieldType.LeftContextId -- left context ID
  • FieldType.RightContextId -- right context ID
  • FieldType.Cost -- word cost
  • FieldType.Custom -- any other, dictionary-specific field

FieldDefinition

FieldDefinition describes a single field within a schema.

FieldDefinition(index, name, field_type, description=None)

from lindera import FieldDefinition, FieldType

field = FieldDefinition(0, "surface", FieldType.Surface, "Surface form")

Properties (read-only):

PropertyTypeDescription
indexintZero-based position of the field within the schema
namestrField name
field_typeFieldTypeField type
descriptionstr or NoneOptional human-readable description

Creating a Schema

Schema holds an ordered list of field names and provides lookups between field name and index.

Schema(fields)

Creates a schema from a list of field names.

from lindera import Schema

schema = Schema([
    "surface",
    "left_context_id",
    "right_context_id",
    "cost",
    "major_pos",
    "reading",
])

Schema.create_default()

A static method that returns the built-in default schema: 13 fields matching the IPADIC-style layout (surface, left_context_id, right_context_id, cost, major_pos, pos_detail_1, pos_detail_2, pos_detail_3, conjugation_type, conjugation_form, base_form, reading, pronunciation).

schema = Schema.create_default()

Schema Methods and Properties

MemberReturnsDescription
fields (property)list[str]All field names, in order
field_count()intTotal number of fields
get_field_index(name)int or NoneIndex of the field named name
get_field_name(index)str or NoneField name at index
get_custom_fields()list[str]Field names after the four fixed fields (surface, left_context_id, right_context_id, cost)
get_field_by_name(name)FieldDefinition or NoneFull field definition for name
validate_record(record)NoneRaises ValueError if record does not match the schema
__len__()intSame as field_count()
schema = Schema.create_default()

schema.field_count()               # 13
schema.get_field_index("cost")     # 3
schema.get_field_name(0)           # "surface"
schema.get_custom_fields()         # ["major_pos", "pos_detail_1", ..., "pronunciation"]
len(schema)                        # 13

field = schema.get_field_by_name("surface")
print(field.index, field.name, field.field_type)  # 0 surface FieldType.Surface

schema.validate_record([
    "東京", "1288", "1288", "100",
    "名詞", "固有名詞", "地域", "一般", "*", "*",
    "東京", "トウキョウ", "トーキョー",
])

Text Processing Pipeline

Lindera Python supports a composable text processing pipeline that applies character filters before tokenization and token filters after tokenization. Filters are added to the TokenizerBuilder and executed in the order they are appended.

Input Text
  --> Character Filters (preprocessing)
  --> Tokenization
  --> Token Filters (postprocessing)
  --> Output Tokens

Character Filters

Character filters transform the input text before tokenization.

unicode_normalize

Applies Unicode normalization to the input text.

from lindera import TokenizerBuilder

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    .append_character_filter("unicode_normalize", {"kind": "nfkc"})
    .build()
)

Supported normalization forms: "nfc", "nfkc", "nfd", "nfkd".

mapping

Replaces characters or strings according to a mapping table.

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    .append_character_filter("mapping", {
        "mapping": {
            "\u30fc": "-",
            "\uff5e": "~",
        }
    })
    .build()
)

japanese_iteration_mark

Resolves Japanese iteration marks (odoriji) into their full forms.

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    .append_character_filter("japanese_iteration_mark", {
        "normalize_kanji": True,
        "normalize_kana": True,
    })
    .build()
)

Token Filters

Token filters transform or remove tokens after tokenization.

lowercase

Converts token surface forms to lowercase.

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    .append_token_filter("lowercase", {})
    .build()
)

japanese_base_form

Replaces inflected forms with their base (dictionary) form using the morphological details from the dictionary.

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    .append_token_filter("japanese_base_form", {})
    .build()
)

japanese_stop_tags

Removes tokens whose part-of-speech matches any of the specified tags.

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    .append_token_filter("japanese_stop_tags", {
        "tags": ["助詞,格助詞,一般", "助詞,係助詞", "助詞,連体化", "助動詞"],
    })
    .build()
)

Tags are normalized to exactly four comma-separated levels (missing levels are padded with *) and compared for exact equality against the four part-of-speech details of each token, starting at the field named part_of_speech in the dictionary schema (or at the first detail when the schema has no such field). A bare 助詞 therefore never matches IPADIC particle tokens — they always carry a subcategory such as 助詞,係助詞 — while a bare 助動詞 does match, because auxiliary verbs have no subcategory (助動詞,*,*,*).

japanese_keep_tags

Keeps only tokens whose part-of-speech matches one of the specified tags. All other tokens are removed. The following keeps only general nouns:

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    .append_token_filter("japanese_keep_tags", {
        "tags": ["名詞,一般"],
    })
    .build()
)

Complete Pipeline Example

The following example combines multiple character filters and token filters into a single pipeline:

from lindera import Mode, TokenizerBuilder

tokenizer = (
    TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_mode(Mode.normal())
    .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
    # Preprocessing
    .append_character_filter("unicode_normalize", {"kind": "nfkc"})
    .append_character_filter("japanese_iteration_mark", {
        "normalize_kanji": True,
        "normalize_kana": True,
    })
    # Postprocessing
    .append_token_filter("japanese_base_form", {})
    .append_token_filter("japanese_stop_tags", {
        "tags": ["助詞,格助詞,一般", "助詞,係助詞", "助詞,連体化", "助動詞", "記号,句点", "記号,読点"],
    })
    .append_token_filter("lowercase", {})
    .build()
)

tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("Ｌｉｎｄｅｒａは形態素解析を行うライブラリです。")
for token in tokens:
    print(f"{token.surface}\t{','.join(token.details)}")

In this pipeline:

  1. unicode_normalize converts full-width characters to half-width (NFKC normalization)
  2. japanese_iteration_mark resolves iteration marks
  3. japanese_base_form converts inflected tokens to base form
  4. japanese_stop_tags removes particles, auxiliary verbs, and punctuation
  5. lowercase normalizes alphabetic characters to lowercase

Training

Lindera Python supports training custom CRF-based morphological analysis models from annotated corpora. This functionality requires the train feature.

Prerequisites

Build lindera-python with the train feature enabled (enabled by default):

maturin develop --features train

Training a Model

Use lindera.train() to train a CRF model from a seed lexicon and annotated corpus:

import lindera

lindera.train(
    seed="resources/training/seed.csv",
    corpus="resources/training/corpus.txt",
    char_def="resources/training/char.def",
    unk_def="resources/training/unk.def",
    feature_def="resources/training/feature.def",
    rewrite_def="resources/training/rewrite.def",
    output="/tmp/model.dat",
    lambda_=1.0,
    max_iter=100,
    max_threads=4,
)

Training Parameters

ParameterTypeDefaultDescription
seedstrrequiredPath to the seed lexicon file (CSV format)
corpusstrrequiredPath to the annotated training corpus
char_defstrrequiredPath to the character definition file (char.def)
unk_defstrrequiredPath to the unknown word definition file (unk.def)
feature_defstrrequiredPath to the feature definition file (feature.def)
rewrite_defstrrequiredPath to the rewrite rule definition file (rewrite.def)
outputstrrequiredOutput path for the trained model file
lambda_float1.0Regularization coefficient, finite and >= 0; 0 disables regularization for every type; with L2, MeCab's -c C is 1 / C, so 1.0 is MeCab's -c 1.0
max_iterint100Maximum number of training iterations, 1 or more; training stops earlier once the objective converges (see eta)
max_threadsint or NoneNoneNumber of threads, 1 or more (None = auto-detect CPU cores)
regularizationstr"l2"Regularization type: "l1", "l2" or "elasticnet", in any case ("elastic_net" and "elastic-net" also select Elastic Net), as lindera train --regularization takes it
elastic_net_l1_ratiofloat0.5L1 ratio of Elastic Net regularization, between 0 and 1; 0 uses only L2, 1 uses only L1; used only with "elasticnet"
etafloat5e-5Tolerance of the convergence test, finite and >= 0: training stops before max_iter once the relative change of the objective stays below it for 3 iterations in a row; 0 disables the test

The settings are checked before any file is read: an unknown regularization, or a lambda_, elastic_net_l1_ratio or eta outside its range, raises a ValueError. To train with v6's default settings (the model still differs from v6's, since the first line search changed in #1290), pass regularization="l1" and lambda_=0.01, and eta=0 to stop only at max_iter.

Progress Output

lindera.train() writes its progress to standard output and a line per L-BFGS iteration to standard error, such as iter: 1, cost: 0.5948643217470097, best_cost: 0.5948643217470097, gamma: 0.47689090558496994, and lindera.export() writes the files it created to standard output. They are written as to a blocking stream: while a stream is full, the call waits until it takes the line, and a line that a stream can no longer take, such as a pipe whose reader has exited, is dropped while the training goes on (#1312). A program that trains in a child process must keep reading both streams of the child, or the training waits.

Exporting a Trained Model

After training, export the model to dictionary source files using lindera.export():

import lindera

lindera.export(
    model="/tmp/model.dat",
    output="/tmp/dictionary_source",
    metadata="resources/training/metadata.json",
)

Export Parameters

ParameterTypeDefaultDescription
modelstrrequiredPath to the trained model file (.dat)
outputstrrequiredOutput directory for dictionary source files
metadatastr or NoneNonePath to a base metadata.json file

The export creates the following files in the output directory, the same files that lindera export creates:

  • lex.csv -- Lexicon entries with trained costs
  • matrix.def -- Connection cost matrix
  • unk.def -- Unknown word definitions
  • char.def -- Character category definitions (copied from the trained model)
  • feature.def -- Feature template definitions (copied from the trained model)
  • rewrite.def -- Feature rewrite rules (copied from the trained model)
  • left-id.def -- Left context ID to feature string mapping
  • right-id.def -- Right context ID to feature string mapping
  • metadata.json -- Updated metadata (when metadata parameter is provided)

The model file must come from this version's training. A model file written by an earlier version, which includes every model file written before 7.0.0, is rejected: lindera.export() fails with an error that asks you to re-run training. Train such a model again with lindera.train().

Complete Workflow

The full workflow for training and using a custom dictionary:

import lindera

# Step 1: Train the CRF model
lindera.train(
    seed="resources/training/seed.csv",
    corpus="resources/training/corpus.txt",
    char_def="resources/training/char.def",
    unk_def="resources/training/unk.def",
    feature_def="resources/training/feature.def",
    rewrite_def="resources/training/rewrite.def",
    output="/tmp/model.dat",
    lambda_=1.0,
    max_iter=100,
)

# Step 2: Export to dictionary source files
lindera.export(
    model="/tmp/model.dat",
    output="/tmp/dictionary_source",
    metadata="resources/training/metadata.json",
)

# Step 3: Build the dictionary from exported source files
metadata = lindera.Metadata.from_json_file("/tmp/dictionary_source/metadata.json")
lindera.build_dictionary("/tmp/dictionary_source", "/tmp/dictionary", metadata)

# Step 4: Use the trained dictionary
tokenizer = (
    lindera.TokenizerBuilder()
    .set_dictionary("/tmp/dictionary")
    .set_mode(lindera.Mode.normal())
    .build()
)

tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("形態素解析のテスト")
for token in tokens:
    print(f"{token.surface}\t{','.join(token.details)}")

Lindera Node.js

Lindera Node.js provides Node.js bindings for the Lindera morphological analysis engine, built with NAPI-RS. It brings Lindera's high-performance tokenization capabilities to the Node.js ecosystem, on the Node.js versions ^20.17.0 || ^22.13.0 || >= 23.5.0.

Features

  • Multi-language support: Tokenize Japanese (IPADIC, IPADIC NEologd, UniDic), Korean (ko-dic), and Chinese (CC-CEDICT, Jieba) text
  • Text processing pipeline: Compose character filters and token filters for flexible preprocessing and postprocessing
  • CRF-based dictionary training: Train custom morphological analysis models from annotated corpora (requires train feature)
  • Multiple tokenization modes: Normal and decompose modes for different analysis granularity
  • N-best tokenization: Retrieve multiple tokenization candidates ranked by cost
  • User dictionaries: Extend system dictionaries with custom vocabulary
  • TypeScript support: Full type definitions included out of the box

Documentation

  • Installation -- Prerequisites, build instructions, and feature flags
  • Quick Start -- A minimal example to get started
  • Tokenizer API -- TokenizerBuilder, Tokenizer, and Token class reference
  • Dictionary Management -- Loading, building, and managing dictionaries
  • Text Processing Pipeline -- Character filters and token filters
  • Training -- Training custom CRF models and exporting dictionaries

Errors

A function or method that fails throws an Error. Its message says what went wrong, and its code tells the kind of failure:

codeFailureExample
The type expected, such as StringExpected or ArrayExpectedAn argument of another typeloadDictionary(123), new Schema("a")
InvalidArgAn argument that is not an instance of the class expected, or a number outside the range of its settingsetMode("normal"), new Metadata({ defaultLeftContextId: 2 ** 32 + 5 })
GenericFailureMost other failures, and a panic (below)loadDictionary("/nonexistent/dictionary"), Mode.fromStr("Normal")

A panic in Lindera's Rust code, which is a bug, throws an Error too, from the function or method that was called, and Node.js goes on running. Up to v6.2.0, a panic aborted Node.js with fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic, error 5, aborting (#1314). The Error of a panic has the code GenericFailure, as most other failures do, and the panic's message as its message. Rust also writes the place of the panic in its source code and the message to standard error.

An object whose method panicked may keep what the method changed before the panic, so create it again instead of using it further. Please report a panic at GitHub Issues, with its message and the input that caused it.

Installation

Installing from npm

Pre-built packages will be available on npm:

npm install lindera

[!NOTE] The npm package does not include dictionaries. See Obtaining Dictionaries below. For browser/WASM usage, see lindera-wasm.

Building from Source

Prerequisites

  • Node.js ^20.17.0 || ^22.13.0 || >= 23.5.0 -- The engines range of lindera-nodejs/package.json (LTS versions recommended)
  • Rust toolchain -- Install via rustup

The NAPI-RS CLI (@napi-rs/cli), which builds the native addon, needs no global install: it is a devDependency of lindera-nodejs, which npm install installs (see Development Build).

Obtaining Dictionaries

Lindera does not bundle dictionaries with the package. You need to obtain a pre-built dictionary separately.

Download from GitHub Releases

Pre-built dictionaries are available on the GitHub Releases page. Download and extract the dictionary archive to a local directory:

# Example: download and extract the IPADIC dictionary
curl -LO https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases/download/<version>/lindera-ipadic-<version>.zip
unzip lindera-ipadic-<version>.zip -d /path/to/ipadic

Development Build

Build lindera-nodejs in release mode. npm install also installs the NAPI-RS CLI (@napi-rs/cli) at the version package.json pins, which npm run build runs:

cd lindera-nodejs
npm install
npm run build

For a debug build, run npm run build:debug instead of npm run build.

Or use the project Makefile, which makes the same release build:

make build-lindera-nodejs

Build with Training Support

The train feature enables CRF-based dictionary training functionality. It is enabled by default:

npm run build -- --features train

Feature Flags

FeatureDescriptionDefault
trainCRF training functionalityEnabled
embed-ipadicEmbed Japanese dictionary (IPADIC) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidicEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidic-cwjEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic CWJ, 1.2 GB) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidic-csjEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic CSJ, 1.2 GB) into the binaryDisabled
embed-sudachidictEmbed Japanese dictionary (SudachiDict) into the binaryDisabled
embed-ipadic-neologdEmbed Japanese dictionary (IPADIC NEologd) into the binaryDisabled
embed-ko-dicEmbed Korean dictionary (ko-dic) into the binaryDisabled
embed-cc-cedictEmbed Chinese dictionary (CC-CEDICT) into the binaryDisabled
embed-jiebaEmbed Chinese dictionary (Jieba) into the binaryDisabled
embed-cjkEmbed all CJK dictionaries (IPADIC, ko-dic, Jieba) into the binaryDisabled

Multiple features can be combined:

npm run build -- --features "train,embed-ipadic,embed-ko-dic"

[!TIP] If you want to embed a dictionary directly into the binary (advanced usage), enable the corresponding embed-* feature flag and load it using the embedded:// scheme:

const dictionary = loadDictionary("embedded://ipadic");

See Feature Flags for details.

Verifying the Installation

After installation, verify that lindera is available in Node.js:

const lindera = require("lindera");

console.log(lindera.version());

[!NOTE] The lindera npm package's exports map declares types, import, and require conditions, so the package loads from CommonJS (const { TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera")) and ES modules (import { TokenizerBuilder } from "lindera") alike:

import { TokenizerBuilder } from "lindera";

console.log(typeof TokenizerBuilder); // "function"

Quick Start

This guide shows how to tokenize text using lindera-nodejs.

Basic Tokenization

The recommended way to create a tokenizer is through TokenizerBuilder:

const { Mode, TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setMode(Mode.normal());
builder.setDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");
const tokenizer = builder.build();

const tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("関西国際空港限定トートバッグ");
for (const token of tokens) {
  console.log(`${token.surface}\t${token.details.join(",")}`);
}

Note: Download a pre-built dictionary from GitHub Releases and specify the path to the extracted directory.

Expected output:

関西国際空港    名詞,固有名詞,組織,*,*,*,関西国際空港,カンサイコクサイクウコウ,カンサイコクサイクーコー
限定    名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,限定,ゲンテイ,ゲンテイ
トートバッグ    名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,*,*,*

Method Chaining

Every setter returns the builder itself (this), so the configuration can be chained:

const { Mode, TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const tokenizer = new TokenizerBuilder()
  .setMode(Mode.normal())
  .setDictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
  .build();

const tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("すもももももももものうち");
for (const token of tokens) {
  console.log(`${token.surface}\t${token.details[0]}`);
}

Calling the setters one statement at a time works just as well — both styles configure the same builder.

Accessing Token Properties

Each token exposes the following properties:

const { TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");
const tokenizer = builder.build();

const tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("東京タワー");
for (const token of tokens) {
  console.log(`Surface: ${token.surface}`);
  console.log(`Byte range: ${token.byteStart}..${token.byteEnd}`);
  console.log(`Position: ${token.position}`);
  console.log(`Word ID: ${token.wordId}`);
  console.log(`Unknown: ${token.isUnknown}`);
  console.log(`Details: ${token.details}`);
  console.log();
}

N-best Tokenization

Retrieve multiple tokenization candidates ranked by cost:

const { TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");
const tokenizer = builder.build();

const results = tokenizer.tokenizeNbest("すもももももももものうち", 3);
for (const { tokens, cost } of results) {
  const surfaces = tokens.map((t) => t.surface);
  console.log(`Cost ${cost}: ${surfaces.join(" / ")}`);
}

TypeScript

Lindera Node.js includes TypeScript type definitions, so all classes and functions are fully typed. The package's exports map serves both require and import, and the following sample compiles under moduleResolution: node16 with strict enabled:

import type { Token } from "lindera";
import { Mode, TokenizerBuilder } from "lindera";

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setMode(Mode.normal());
builder.setDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");
const tokenizer = builder.build();

const tokens: Token[] = tokenizer.tokenize("形態素解析");
for (const token of tokens) {
  console.log(`${token.surface}: ${token.details.join(",")}`);
}

Tokenizer API

TokenizerBuilder

TokenizerBuilder configures and constructs a Tokenizer instance using the builder pattern.

Constructors

new TokenizerBuilder()

Creates a new builder with default configuration.

const { TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();

new TokenizerBuilder().fromFile(filePath)

Loads configuration from a YAML file and returns a new builder.

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder().fromFile("lindera.yml");

See lindera-nodejs/resources/lindera.yml for a complete example configuration file, including dictionary, character filter, and token filter settings.

Configuration Methods

All setter methods return the builder itself (this), so they can be chained or called one statement at a time.

setMode(mode)

Sets the tokenization mode, a Mode:

  • Mode.normal() -- Standard tokenization (default)
  • Mode.decompose(penalty?) -- Decomposes compound words into smaller units, with the Penalty the mode holds

A value that is not a Mode, such as the mode name "normal", throws an InvalidArg error. A mode name read at run time, such as a setting, becomes a Mode with Mode.fromStr().

const { Mode } = require("lindera");

builder.setMode(Mode.normal());
builder.setMode(Mode.decompose({ kanjiPenaltyLengthPenalty: 0 }));
builder.setMode(Mode.fromStr("decompose"));

setDictionary(path)

Sets the system dictionary path or URI.

// Use an embedded dictionary
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");

// Use an external dictionary
builder.setDictionary("/path/to/dictionary");

setUserDictionary(uri)

Sets the user dictionary URI.

builder.setUserDictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv");

setKeepWhitespace(keep)

Controls whether whitespace tokens appear in the output. Kept whitespace also stays in the lattice, so the other tokens can differ from those of the default output, which skips whitespace in the lattice as MeCab does. To keep whitespace in the lattice without outputting it, use setSkipWhitespace(false) instead.

builder.setKeepWhitespace(true);

setSkipWhitespace(skip)

Sets whether whitespace is skipped in the lattice. The value means the same as segmenter.skip_whitespace in a configuration file.

ValueEffect
trueSkips whitespace, so the words on either side of it connect directly, as MeCab does
falseKeeps whitespace in the lattice as a node of its own (a whitespace dictionary entry or the SPACE unknown word), as before v7; whitespace is still dropped from the output
null or undefinedDefault: the setting of the dictionary's metadata.json (skipping, except with SudachiDict)

A value set here overrides the dictionary's default and a skip_whitespace loaded with fromFile. It has no effect while whitespace tokens are kept (setKeepWhitespace(true)), because kept whitespace always stays in the lattice. The argument is required; any other value throws an Error.

With IPADIC, for example, Google が 新しい reads が as a particle (助詞) by default and as a conjunction (接続詞) with setSkipWhitespace(false). See Segmenter for details.

// Keep whitespace in the lattice, as before v7
builder.setSkipWhitespace(false);

// Back to the dictionary's default
builder.setSkipWhitespace(null);

setBreakCharacters(chars)

Sets the break characters. chars has the same meaning as segmenter.break_characters in a configuration file:

  • A string -- Each of its characters is a break character: no unknown word crosses a boundary between a break character and another character, and in decompose mode no system-dictionary word does either. User-dictionary words and words made of break characters only stay.
  • "" -- No break characters, which gives MeCab's segmentation.
  • null or undefined -- The default, ・. Use it to undo an earlier call.

The argument is required. A value set here overrides a break_characters loaded with fromFile. Any other value throws.

With IPADIC, for example, レノン・ジョン, which is not in the dictionary, is レノン, ・ and ジョン by default and one unknown word with setBreakCharacters(""). See Segmenter for details.

// Split as MeCab does
builder.setBreakCharacters("");

setSpacePenalty(value)

Sets the left-space penalty for Korean (mecab-ko's left-space-penalty-factor): a candidate that starts right after whitespace and whose first part-of-speech tag is listed in a rule gets that rule's cost added. The value means the same as segmenter.space_penalty in a configuration file.

ValueEffect
null or undefinedDefault: the rules the dictionary ships in its metadata.json, if any
falseTurns the penalty off
trueRequires the dictionary's rules; build() throws if the dictionary ships none
{ rules: [{ pos: [...], cost: n }, ...] }Applies these rules instead of the dictionary's

Any other value throws an Error.

// Turn the penalty off
builder.setSpacePenalty(false);

// Explicit rules (these are the ones ko-dic ships)
builder.setSpacePenalty({
  rules: [
    { pos: ["EC", "EF", "EP", "ETM", "ETN", "VCP", "XSA", "XSN", "XSV"], cost: 3000 },
    { pos: ["JC", "JKB", "JKC", "JKG", "JKO", "JKQ", "JKS", "JKV", "JX"], cost: 6000 },
  ],
});

// Back to the dictionary's default
builder.setSpacePenalty(null);

[!NOTE] Since v6.1.0, ko-dic applies the left-space penalty by default, because its metadata.json ships mecab-ko-dic's rules. This changes the Korean output (for example, 이 in 검색 이 잘 된다 is the interjection IC with the penalty and the subject particle JKS without it). Call setSpacePenalty(false) to turn it off. For a Tokenizer created directly, pass false as the fourth argument: new Tokenizer(dictionary, Mode.normal(), null, false). A ko-dic downloaded from the v6.0.0 release ships no rules, so with it the penalty stays off and setSpacePenalty(true) makes build() throw. See Segmenter for details.

appendCharacterFilter(kind, args?)

Appends a character filter to the preprocessing pipeline.

builder.appendCharacterFilter("unicode_normalize", { kind: "nfkc" });

appendTokenFilter(kind, args?)

Appends a token filter to the postprocessing pipeline.

builder.appendTokenFilter("lowercase", {});

The arguments of setSpacePenalty, appendCharacterFilter and appendTokenFilter may nest arrays and objects at most 128 levels deep. A deeper value, or one that contains itself, throws an Error.

Build

build()

Builds and returns a Tokenizer with the configured settings.

const tokenizer = builder.build();

Tokenizer

Tokenizer performs morphological analysis on text.

Creating a Tokenizer

new Tokenizer(dictionary, mode?, userDictionary?, spacePenalty?)

Creates a tokenizer directly from a loaded dictionary.

mode takes a Mode, as setMode does, with the same errors. null or undefined (the default) is normal mode. For decompose mode with a custom penalty, pass Mode.decompose(penalty).

spacePenalty takes the same values as setSpacePenalty. null or undefined (the default) uses the left-space penalty rules the dictionary ships. An invalid setting throws, as setSpacePenalty and build() do.

const { Mode, Tokenizer, loadDictionary } = require("lindera");

const dictionary = loadDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
const tokenizer = new Tokenizer(dictionary, Mode.normal());

// ko-dic without the left-space penalty
const koTokenizer = new Tokenizer(loadDictionary("embedded://ko-dic"), Mode.normal(), null, false);

Tokenizer Methods

tokenize(text)

Tokenizes the input text and returns an array of plain token objects.

const tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("形態素解析");

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
textstringText to tokenize

Returns: Token[]

Tokens are plain JavaScript objects, not class instances, so they are reclaimed by ordinary garbage collection and pass through JSON.stringify, structuredClone, and worker transfer without conversion. See Token.

tokenizeSurfaces(text)

Tokenizes the input text and returns only the token surfaces, as an array of strings. This is the fast path for wakati-style use: no token objects are built and no morphological details are loaded, so it is significantly faster than tokenize when only the surface strings are needed. The result equals tokenizer.tokenize(text).map((t) => t.surface).

const surfaces = tokenizer.tokenizeSurfaces("形態素解析");
// ["形態素", "解析"]

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
textstringText to tokenize

Returns: string[]

tokenizeNbest(text, n, unique?, costThreshold?)

Returns the N-best tokenization results, each containing tokens and total path cost.

const results = tokenizer.tokenizeNbest("すもももももももものうち", 3);
for (const { tokens, cost } of results) {
  console.log(cost, tokens.map((t) => t.surface));
}

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
textstringText to tokenize
nnumberNumber of results to return, an integer of 0 or more
uniquebooleanDeduplicate results (default: false)
costThresholdnumber | undefinedMaximum cost difference from the best path (default: undefined)

Returns: NbestResult[], where each NbestResult is { tokens: Token[], cost: number }

tokenizeBatch(texts, maxThreads?)

Tokenizes every text of an array, each as tokenize does, on up to maxThreads threads, and returns their tokens in the order of the texts. The results are the same for every number of threads. The call is synchronous: the JavaScript thread waits until every text is tokenized, while the tokenization runs on several threads.

const batch = tokenizer.tokenizeBatch(["形態素解析", "すもももももももものうち"]);
for (const tokens of batch) {
  console.log(tokens.map((t) => t.surface));
}

Every text is tokenized as a call of its own: an array of the lines of a document gives the tokens of each line, not those of the whole document as one text. A short array runs on one thread (a thread needs at least 16 KiB of input), and every thread holds its own copy of the user dictionary, if any. A batch whose results are large, such as the tokens of several megabytes of text, can run faster on fewer threads than the default: when many threads make the memory of the tokens at once, much of the time goes to the kernel.

Parameters:

NameTypeDescription
textsstring[]Texts to tokenize
maxThreadsnumber | undefinedThe most threads, an integer of 1 or more (default: the number of CPUs); any other number throws an InvalidArg error

Returns: Token[][]

tokenizeSurfacesBatch(texts, maxThreads?)

Tokenizes every text of an array as tokenizeSurfaces does, on up to maxThreads threads, as tokenizeBatch does.

Parameters: as tokenizeBatch.

Returns: string[][]

tokenizeNbestBatch(texts, n, unique?, costThreshold?, maxThreads?)

Tokenizes every text of an array as tokenizeNbest does, on up to maxThreads threads, as tokenizeBatch does. n, unique and costThreshold apply to each text.

Parameters: texts and maxThreads as tokenizeBatch; n, unique and costThreshold as tokenizeNbest.

Returns: NbestResult[][]

tokenizeBatchAsync(texts, maxThreads?)

Tokenizes every text of an array as tokenizeBatch does, and returns a Promise of the same results. The texts are tokenized on a thread of libuv's pool, on up to maxThreads threads, while the event loop runs; the token objects are then made on the JavaScript thread.

const batch = await tokenizer.tokenizeBatchAsync(["形態素解析", "すもももももももものうち"]);
for (const tokens of batch) {
  console.log(tokens.map((t) => t.surface));
}
  • A maxThreads that is not an integer of 1 or more rejects the Promise with the InvalidArg error that tokenizeBatch throws. An argument of the wrong type, such as a string instead of an array, throws when the method is called, as for every method.
  • The token objects are made on the JavaScript thread. A batch with few results is made at once, as tokenizeBatch makes it; a larger one is made in parts, with a turn of the event loop between two parts (through setImmediate), so that timers and I/O run while the objects are made, and the parts take no thread of libuv's pool. With IPADIC on a Linux x86_64 machine, on bocchan.txt 20 times (10,760 lines, 1.39 million tokens) on 8 threads, the event loop's largest delay was about 15 ms during tokenizeBatchAsync and about 8 ms during tokenizeSurfacesBatchAsync, most of it a garbage collection of the young generation; tokenizeBatchAsync took about 1.6 s, and the synchronous tokenizeBatch, which holds the event loop for its whole time, about 1.5 s.
  • Fake timers that replace setImmediate, as those of Jest or Sinon can, hold the Promise of a batch made in parts until they run the immediates. When setImmediate is not a function, the parts left are made at once.
  • A batch takes one thread of libuv's pool while it runs (the pool has 4 by default, UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE), which file system and DNS calls share. Batches on the same tokenizer run one after the other; single-text calls on it do not wait for them.

Parameters: as tokenizeBatch.

Returns: Promise<Token[][]>

tokenizeSurfacesBatchAsync(texts, maxThreads?)

Tokenizes every text of an array as tokenizeSurfacesBatch does, and returns a Promise of the same results, as tokenizeBatchAsync does.

Parameters: as tokenizeBatch.

Returns: Promise<string[][]>

tokenizeNbestBatchAsync(texts, n, unique?, costThreshold?, maxThreads?)

Tokenizes every text of an array as tokenizeNbestBatch does, and returns a Promise of the same results, as tokenizeBatchAsync does. An n, costThreshold or maxThreads outside its range rejects the Promise.

Parameters: as tokenizeNbestBatch.

Returns: Promise<NbestResult[][]>

Token

Token is a plain object describing a single morphological token. It is a TypeScript interface, not a class: it has no methods and no prototype, and every field is read directly.

Properties

PropertyTypeDescription
surfacestringSurface form of the token
byteStartnumberStart byte position in the original text
byteEndnumberEnd byte position in the original text
positionnumberToken position index
wordIdnumberDictionary word ID
isUnknownbooleantrue if the word is not in the dictionary
detailsstring[]Morphological details (part of speech, reading, etc.)
dependencyTokenDependency (optional)The bunsetsu of the token and its head; the property is there only when the token filter japanese_dependency ran

Reading Details

Index details directly. Out-of-range indexes yield undefined.

const token = tokenizer.tokenize("東京")[0];
const pos = token.details[0];      // e.g., "名詞"
const subpos = token.details[1];   // e.g., "固有名詞"
const reading = token.details[7];  // e.g., "トウキョウ"

The structure of details depends on the dictionary:

  • IPADIC: [品詞, 品詞細分類1, 品詞細分類2, 品詞細分類3, 活用型, 活用形, 原形, 読み, 発音]
  • UniDic: Detailed morphological features following the UniDic specification
  • ko-dic / CC-CEDICT / Jieba: Dictionary-specific detail formats

TokenDependency

The bunsetsu of a token and the bunsetsu it depends on. The token filter japanese_dependency puts it in the dependency of every token; see Token Filter for the filter, its model, and how a text is cut into sentences.

The distributed packages have the filter, from 7.1.0 on: the dependency feature is in the default build. They have no model. The filter takes the path of a model file: the one Lindera releases for IPADIC is dependency.model in lindera-dependency-ipadic-<version>.zip, on the page of each release, which lindera download dependency-ipadic also installs (Installation). There is one for each of unidic, unidic-cwj and unidic-csj too, with the name of the dictionary in place of ipadic.

PropertyTypeDescription
sentencenumberThe number of the sentence in the text, from 0
bunsetsunumberThe number of the bunsetsu of the token in its sentence, from 0
headnumber | nullThe number of the bunsetsu that one depends on; null for the last bunsetsu of a sentence
rolestringWhat the token is in its bunsetsu: head (the head word), function (the function word), head_function (both) or other
scorenumberThe score of the decision that attached the bunsetsu to its head; 0 where nothing was decided
const { TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const tokenizer = new TokenizerBuilder()
  .setDictionary("embedded://ipadic")
  .appendTokenFilter("japanese_dependency", { model: "ipadic.model" })
  .build();
for (const token of tokenizer.tokenize("彼は赤い花を見た。")) {
  const { bunsetsu, head, role } = token.dependency;
  console.log(token.surface, bunsetsu, head, role);
}

彼 0 3 head
は 0 3 function
赤い 1 2 head_function
花 2 3 head
を 2 3 function
見 3 null head
た 3 null function
。 3 null other

TokenDependency is a plain object, a TypeScript interface as Token is, and JSON.stringify of a token keeps it. A token without the filter has no dependency property, and is the object it was before.

Mode and Penalty

TokenizerBuilder.setMode() and the Tokenizer constructor take the mode as a Mode, which holds the penalty of decompose mode as a Penalty.

Mode

The tokenization mode: normal, or decompose with a Penalty. It is the counterpart of the Rust lindera::mode::Mode (see Segmenter), and setMode() and the Tokenizer constructor take it:

  • Normal mode -- standard dictionary-cost-based tokenization
  • Decompose mode -- penalty-based decomposition of compound words

Mode has no constructor, so new Mode() throws; the static factories below create a mode. A mode cannot be changed.

Mode.normal()

Creates normal mode.

const { Mode } = require("lindera");

const mode = Mode.normal();

Mode.decompose(penalty?)

Creates decompose mode with penalty, a Penalty object. null or undefined (the default) uses the default penalty, and a field left out keeps its default. A value that is not an object, or a field that is not an integer in its range, throws an InvalidArg error.

const decompose = Mode.decompose(); // the default penalty
const custom = Mode.decompose({ kanjiPenaltyLengthPenalty: 0 });

Mode.fromStr(name)

Creates a mode from its name, as the Rust Mode parses one: "normal" is normal mode, and "decompose" is decompose mode with the default penalty. The name is case sensitive; any other name, including "Normal" and "Decompose", throws an Error whose message contains Invalid mode. Use it for a mode name read at run time, such as a setting:

const mode = Mode.fromStr("decompose");
console.log(mode.equals(Mode.decompose()));
// true

Properties and Methods

MemberTypeDescription
namestringThe name of the mode, "normal" or "decompose" (a read-only property)
penaltyPenalty | nullThe penalty of decompose mode, as a copy with every field set, or null for normal mode (a read-only property). Changing the copy does not change the mode
isNormal()booleanWhether this is normal mode
isDecompose()booleanWhether this is decompose mode
equals(other)booleanWhether other has the same name and penalty. A value that is not a Mode throws an InvalidArg error
toString()stringThe name of the mode, as name

=== compares objects, not modes: each call of Mode.normal() returns a new object, so compare modes with equals.

const { Mode } = require("lindera");

const mode = Mode.decompose({ kanjiPenaltyLengthPenalty: 0 });
console.log(mode.name, mode.isNormal(), mode.isDecompose());
// decompose false true

// A copy with every field set: the field left out has its default
const penalty = mode.penalty;
console.log(penalty.kanjiPenaltyLengthPenalty, penalty.otherPenaltyLengthPenalty);
// 0 1700

// Changing the copy does not change the mode
penalty.otherPenaltyLengthPenalty = 0;
console.log(mode.penalty.otherPenaltyLengthPenalty);
// 1700

console.log(Mode.normal().penalty);
// null

console.log(Mode.decompose().equals(Mode.fromStr("decompose")));
// true
console.log(mode.equals(Mode.decompose()));
// false
console.log(`${Mode.normal()}`);
// normal

Penalty

A plain object (the TypeScript type Penalty) with the penalty parameters of decompose mode. Every field is optional, and a field left out keeps its default:

PropertyTypeDescription
kanjiPenaltyLengthThresholdnumberLength threshold for kanji sequences before a penalty is applied, an integer 0 or more (default: 2)
kanjiPenaltyLengthPenaltynumberPenalty value for long kanji sequences, a 32-bit signed integer (default: 3000)
otherPenaltyLengthThresholdnumberLength threshold for other character sequences before a penalty is applied, an integer 0 or more (default: 7)
otherPenaltyLengthPenaltynumberPenalty value for long other-character sequences, a 32-bit signed integer (default: 1700)

Pass it to Mode.decompose(), and the mode to setMode() or to the Tokenizer constructor. Without length penalties, decompose mode keeps long words whole, as normal mode does:

const { Mode, Tokenizer, TokenizerBuilder, loadDictionary } = require("lindera");

const text = "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ";
const penalty = { kanjiPenaltyLengthPenalty: 0, otherPenaltyLengthPenalty: 0 };
const surfaces = (tokenizer) => tokenizer.tokenize(text).map((token) => token.surface);

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder().setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
console.log(surfaces(builder.setMode(Mode.normal()).build()));
// [ '関西国際空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ' ]

console.log(surfaces(builder.setMode(Mode.decompose()).build()));
// [ '関西', '国際', '空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ' ]

console.log(surfaces(builder.setMode(Mode.decompose(penalty)).build()));
// [ '関西国際空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ' ]

const tokenizer = new Tokenizer(loadDictionary("embedded://ipadic"), Mode.decompose(penalty));
console.log(surfaces(tokenizer));
// [ '関西国際空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ' ]

Dictionary Management

Lindera Node.js provides functions for loading, building, and managing dictionaries used in morphological analysis.

Loading Dictionaries

System Dictionaries

Use loadDictionary(uri) to load a system dictionary. Download a pre-built dictionary from GitHub Releases and specify the path to the extracted directory:

const { loadDictionary } = require("lindera");

const dictionary = loadDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");

Embedded dictionaries (advanced) -- if you built with an embed-* feature flag, you can load an embedded dictionary:

const dictionary = loadDictionary("embedded://ipadic");

Dictionary exposes a few read-only accessors for inspecting the loaded dictionary's metadata:

console.log(dictionary.metadataName());     // e.g. "ipadic"
console.log(dictionary.metadataEncoding()); // e.g. "UTF-8"

const metadata = dictionary.metadata(); // full Metadata object
console.log(metadata.defaultWordCost);

User Dictionaries

User dictionaries add custom vocabulary on top of a system dictionary. Load one for the system dictionary it is used with:

const { loadDictionary, loadUserDictionaryFor } = require("lindera");

const dictionary = loadDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");
const userDict = loadUserDictionaryFor("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", dictionary);

A .csv is built with the system dictionary's metadata and checked against its connection matrix as it is built: a row whose context ID lies outside the matrix throws an error that names its CSV line and surface (see Context IDs). A .bin is loaded as it was built.

loadUserDictionary(uri, metadata) loads a user dictionary with metadata only. A .csv loaded this way is checked when it is combined with the system dictionary, and the error names the entry by its word id:

const { loadUserDictionary, Metadata } = require("lindera");

const metadata = new Metadata();
const userDict = loadUserDictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", metadata);

Pass the user dictionary when building a tokenizer:

const { Mode, Tokenizer, loadDictionary, loadUserDictionaryFor } = require("lindera");

const dictionary = loadDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");
const userDict = loadUserDictionaryFor("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", dictionary);

const tokenizer = new Tokenizer(dictionary, Mode.normal(), userDict);

Or via the builder:

const { TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");
builder.setUserDictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv");
const tokenizer = builder.build();

Building Dictionaries

System Dictionary

Build a system dictionary from source files:

const { buildDictionary, Metadata } = require("lindera");

const metadata = new Metadata({ name: "custom", encoding: "UTF-8" });
buildDictionary("/path/to/input_dir", "/path/to/output_dir", metadata);

The input directory should contain the dictionary source files (CSV lexicon, matrix.def, etc.).

To build a dictionary with the settings its metadata.json ships, load the file with Metadata.fromJsonFile() and pass the result. The file's space_penalty rules are kept, so a ko-dic built this way applies the left-space penalty by default (see setSpacePenalty). A Metadata created with new Metadata(...) carries no rules.

const metadata = Metadata.fromJsonFile("/path/to/lindera-ko-dic/metadata.json");
buildDictionary("/path/to/mecab-ko-dic", "/path/to/output_dir", metadata);

Metadata.fromJsonFile() also keeps connection_id_mapping, which the metadata.json of ko-dic, UniDic, UniDic CWJ and UniDic CSJ enables. The build then relabels the context IDs of the connection matrix by access frequency, as lindera build does, to improve the cache locality of connection-cost lookups; the results of tokenization do not change. Pass a context-ID frequency histogram as the fourth argument, contextIdFreq, such as the context_id_freq.txt of the dictionary crate, to rank the IDs by their frequency in a corpus, as lindera build --context-id-freq does. Without one, the IDs are ranked by the count of dictionary entries, a much weaker proxy. A dictionary without connection_id_mapping does not read the histogram.

buildDictionary(
  "/path/to/mecab-ko-dic",
  "/path/to/output_dir",
  metadata,
  "/path/to/lindera-ko-dic/context_id_freq.txt",
);

User Dictionary

Build a user dictionary from a CSV file for the system dictionary it is used with:

const { buildUserDictionaryFor, loadDictionary, loadUserDictionaryFor } = require("lindera");

const dictionary = loadDictionary("/path/to/ipadic");
buildUserDictionaryFor("user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", dictionary);
const userDict = loadUserDictionaryFor("/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", dictionary);

The CSV is built with the system dictionary's metadata and checked against its connection matrix: a row whose context ID lies outside the matrix throws an error that names its CSV line and surface, and no file is written (see Context IDs). The second argument is the path of the file to write. End it with .bin, since the loaders choose how to load a user dictionary by its extension.

buildUserDictionary(kind, inputFile, outputDir, metadata) builds a user dictionary with metadata only. Despite its name, outputDir is the path of the file to write too, not a directory. The rows are checked when the user dictionary is combined with the system dictionary, and the error names the entry by its word id:

const { buildUserDictionary, Metadata } = require("lindera");

const metadata = new Metadata();
buildUserDictionary("ipadic", "user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", metadata);

The metadata parameter is optional. When omitted, default metadata values are used:

buildUserDictionary("ipadic", "user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin");

[!NOTE] The first argument (kind) is currently unused -- it is reserved for future use and has no effect on the build. Any string value can be passed for it today. To build for a system dictionary, use buildUserDictionaryFor.

Metadata

The Metadata class configures dictionary parameters.

Creating Metadata

const { Metadata } = require("lindera");

// Default metadata
const metadata = new Metadata();

// Custom metadata
const metadata = new Metadata({
  name: "my_dictionary",
  encoding: "UTF-8",
  defaultWordCost: -10000,
});

Loading from JSON

const metadata = Metadata.fromJsonFile("metadata.json");

Properties

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
namestring"default"Dictionary name
encodingstring"UTF-8"Character encoding
defaultWordCostnumber-10000Default cost for unknown words, an integer from -32768 to 32767
defaultLeftContextIdnumber1288Default left context ID, an integer from 0 to 65535
defaultRightContextIdnumber1288Default right context ID, an integer from 0 to 65535
defaultFieldValuestring"*"Default value for missing fields
flexibleCsvbooleanfalseAllow flexible CSV parsing
skipInvalidCostOrIdbooleanfalseSkip entries with invalid cost or ID

[!NOTE] Schema information (dictionary/user-dictionary field layout) is not exposed on this binding's Metadata object -- there are no dictionarySchema / userDictionarySchema properties. Use the standalone Schema class instead.

All properties support both getting and setting:

const metadata = new Metadata();
metadata.name = "custom_dict";
metadata.encoding = "EUC-JP";
console.log(metadata.name); // "custom_dict"

toObject()

Returns a plain object representation of the metadata, with every value as a string:

const metadata = new Metadata({ name: "test" });
console.log(metadata.toObject());

When the metadata carries left-space penalty rules (for example, when it was loaded from ko-dic's metadata.json), the object also has a spacePenalty entry holding the rules as a JSON string. Otherwise the key is absent.

const koDic = Metadata.fromJsonFile("/path/to/lindera-ko-dic/metadata.json");
const { rules } = JSON.parse(koDic.toObject().spacePenalty);
console.log(rules[1].pos); // ["JC", "JKB", "JKC", "JKG", "JKO", "JKQ", "JKS", "JKV", "JX"]

Schema

The Schema class defines the field structure of dictionary entries.

Creating a Schema

const { Schema } = require("lindera");

// Default IPADIC-compatible schema
const schema = Schema.createDefault();

// Custom schema
const custom = new Schema(["surface", "left_id", "right_id", "cost", "pos", "reading"]);

Schema Methods

MethodReturnsDescription
getFieldIndex(name)number | nullGet field index by name
fieldCount()numberTotal number of fields
getFieldName(index)string | nullGet field name by index
getCustomFields()string[]Fields from index 4 onward (morphological features)
getAllFields()string[]All field names
getFieldByName(name)FieldDefinition | nullGet full field definition
validateRecord(record)voidValidate a CSV record against the schema
const schema = Schema.createDefault();

console.log(schema.fieldCount());           // 13 (IPADIC format)
console.log(schema.getFieldIndex("pos1"));  // e.g., 4
console.log(schema.getAllFields());          // ["surface", "left_id", ...]
console.log(schema.getCustomFields());      // Fields from index 4 onward

FieldDefinition

PropertyTypeDescription
indexnumberField position index
namestringField name
fieldTypeFieldTypeField type enum
descriptionstring | undefinedOptional description

FieldType

ValueDescription
FieldType.SurfaceWord surface text
FieldType.LeftContextIdLeft context ID
FieldType.RightContextIdRight context ID
FieldType.CostWord cost
FieldType.CustomMorphological feature field

Text Processing Pipeline

Lindera Node.js supports a composable text processing pipeline that applies character filters before tokenization and token filters after tokenization. Filters are added to the TokenizerBuilder and executed in the order they are appended.

Input Text
  --> Character Filters (preprocessing)
  --> Tokenization
  --> Token Filters (postprocessing)
  --> Output Tokens

[!NOTE] This page shows a few commonly used filters as examples -- it is not the complete list. See Filters for the full, authoritative catalogue of every character and token filter that lindera-analysis ships, including parameters and examples.

Character Filters

Character filters transform the input text before tokenization.

unicode_normalize

Applies Unicode normalization to the input text.

const { TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
builder.appendCharacterFilter("unicode_normalize", { kind: "nfkc" });
const tokenizer = builder.build();

Supported normalization forms: "nfc", "nfkc", "nfd", "nfkd".

mapping

Replaces characters or strings according to a mapping table.

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
builder.appendCharacterFilter("mapping", {
  mapping: {
    "\u30fc": "-",
    "\uff5e": "~",
  },
});
const tokenizer = builder.build();

japanese_iteration_mark

Resolves Japanese iteration marks (odoriji) into their full forms.

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
builder.appendCharacterFilter("japanese_iteration_mark", {
  normalize_kanji: true,
  normalize_kana: true,
});
const tokenizer = builder.build();

Token Filters

Token filters transform or remove tokens after tokenization.

lowercase

Converts token surface forms to lowercase.

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
builder.appendTokenFilter("lowercase", {});
const tokenizer = builder.build();

japanese_base_form

Replaces inflected forms with their base (dictionary) form using the morphological details from the dictionary.

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
builder.appendTokenFilter("japanese_base_form", {});
const tokenizer = builder.build();

japanese_stop_tags

Removes tokens whose part-of-speech matches any of the specified tags.

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
builder.appendTokenFilter("japanese_stop_tags", {
  tags: ["助詞,格助詞,一般", "助詞,係助詞", "助詞,連体化", "助動詞"],
});
const tokenizer = builder.build();

[!NOTE] Tags are normalized to exactly four comma-separated levels (missing levels are padded with *) and compared for exact equality against the four part-of-speech details of each token, starting at the field named part_of_speech in the dictionary schema (or at the first detail when the schema has no such field). A bare 助詞 therefore never matches IPADIC particle tokens — they always carry a subcategory such as 助詞,係助詞 — while a bare 助動詞 does match, because auxiliary verbs have no subcategory (助動詞,*,*,*).

japanese_keep_tags

Keeps only tokens whose part-of-speech matches one of the specified tags. All other tokens are removed. The following keeps only general nouns:

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
builder.appendTokenFilter("japanese_keep_tags", {
  tags: ["名詞,一般"],
});
const tokenizer = builder.build();

Complete Pipeline Example

The following example combines multiple character filters and token filters into a single pipeline:

const { Mode, TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera");

const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setMode(Mode.normal());
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic");
// Preprocessing
builder.appendCharacterFilter("unicode_normalize", { kind: "nfkc" });
builder.appendCharacterFilter("japanese_iteration_mark", {
  normalize_kanji: true,
  normalize_kana: true,
});
// Postprocessing
builder.appendTokenFilter("japanese_base_form", {});
builder.appendTokenFilter("japanese_stop_tags", {
  tags: ["助詞,格助詞,一般", "助詞,係助詞", "助詞,連体化", "助動詞", "記号,句点", "記号,読点"],
});
builder.appendTokenFilter("lowercase", {});
const tokenizer = builder.build();

const tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("Ｌｉｎｄｅｒａは形態素解析を行うライブラリです。");
for (const token of tokens) {
  console.log(`${token.surface}\t${token.details.join(",")}`);
}

In this pipeline:

  1. unicode_normalize converts full-width characters to half-width (NFKC normalization)
  2. japanese_iteration_mark resolves iteration marks
  3. japanese_base_form converts inflected tokens to base form
  4. japanese_stop_tags removes particles, auxiliary verbs, and punctuation
  5. lowercase normalizes alphabetic characters to lowercase

Training

Lindera Node.js supports training custom CRF-based morphological analysis models from annotated corpora. This functionality requires the train feature.

Prerequisites

Build lindera-nodejs with the train feature enabled (enabled by default):

npm run build -- --features train

Training a Model

[!NOTE] The file paths below (resources/training/*.csv, *.def) are illustrative placeholders — this repository does not ship those exact files. For a complete, runnable example that generates a seed lexicon, corpus, and definition files on the fly and then trains/exports/builds a real dictionary, see lindera-nodejs/examples/train_and_export.js.

Use train() to train a CRF model from a seed lexicon and annotated corpus:

const { train } = require("lindera");

train({
  seed: "resources/training/seed.csv",
  corpus: "resources/training/corpus.txt",
  charDef: "resources/training/char.def",
  unkDef: "resources/training/unk.def",
  featureDef: "resources/training/feature.def",
  rewriteDef: "resources/training/rewrite.def",
  output: "/tmp/model.dat",
  lambda: 1.0,
  maxIter: 100,
  maxThreads: 4,
});

Training Parameters

ParameterTypeDefaultDescription
seedstringrequiredPath to the seed lexicon file (CSV format)
corpusstringrequiredPath to the annotated training corpus
charDefstringrequiredPath to the character definition file (char.def)
unkDefstringrequiredPath to the unknown word definition file (unk.def)
featureDefstringrequiredPath to the feature definition file (feature.def)
rewriteDefstringrequiredPath to the rewrite rule definition file (rewrite.def)
outputstringrequiredOutput path for the trained model file
lambdanumber1.0Regularization coefficient, finite and >= 0; 0 disables regularization for every type; with L2, MeCab's -c C is 1 / C, so 1.0 is MeCab's -c 1.0
maxIternumber100Maximum number of training iterations, 1 or more; training stops earlier once the objective converges (see eta)
maxThreadsnumber | undefinedundefinedNumber of threads, 1 or more (undefined = auto-detect CPU cores)
regularizationstring"l2"Regularization type: "l1", "l2" or "elasticnet", in any case ("elastic_net" and "elastic-net" also select Elastic Net), as lindera train --regularization takes it
elasticNetL1Rationumber0.5L1 ratio of Elastic Net regularization, between 0 and 1; 0 uses only L2, 1 uses only L1; used only with "elasticnet"
etanumber5e-5Tolerance of the convergence test, finite and >= 0: training stops before maxIter once the relative change of the objective stays below it for 3 iterations in a row; 0 disables the test

The settings are checked before any file is read: an unknown regularization, or a lambda, elasticNetL1Ratio or eta outside its range, throws an InvalidArg error. To train with v6's default settings (the model still differs from v6's, since the first line search changed in #1290), pass regularization: "l1" and lambda: 0.01, and eta: 0 to stop only at maxIter.

Progress Output

train() writes its progress to standard output and a line per L-BFGS iteration to standard error, such as iter: 1, cost: 0.5948643217470097, best_cost: 0.5948643217470097, gamma: 0.47689090558496994, and exportModel() writes the files it created to standard output. They are written as to a blocking stream, also when Node.js makes the streams non-blocking, as node --test does: while a stream is full, the call waits until it takes the line, and a line that a stream can no longer take, such as a pipe whose reader has exited, is dropped while the training goes on (#1312). A program that trains in a child process must keep reading both streams of the child, or the training waits.

Exporting a Trained Model

After training, export the model to dictionary source files using exportModel():

const { exportModel } = require("lindera");

exportModel({
  model: "/tmp/model.dat",
  output: "/tmp/dictionary_source",
  metadata: "resources/training/metadata.json",
});

Export Parameters

ParameterTypeDefaultDescription
modelstringrequiredPath to the trained model file (.dat)
outputstringrequiredOutput directory for dictionary source files
metadatastring | undefinedundefinedPath to a base metadata.json file

The export creates the following files in the output directory, the same files that lindera export creates:

  • lex.csv -- Lexicon entries with trained costs
  • matrix.def -- Connection cost matrix
  • unk.def -- Unknown word definitions
  • char.def -- Character category definitions (copied from the trained model)
  • feature.def -- Feature template definitions (copied from the trained model)
  • rewrite.def -- Feature rewrite rules (copied from the trained model)
  • left-id.def -- Left context ID to feature string mapping
  • right-id.def -- Right context ID to feature string mapping
  • metadata.json -- Updated metadata (when metadata parameter is provided)

The model file must come from this version's training. A model file written by an earlier version, which includes every model file written before 7.0.0, is rejected: exportModel() fails with an error that asks you to re-run training. Train such a model again with train().

Complete Workflow

The full workflow for training and using a custom dictionary:

const {
  train,
  exportModel,
  buildDictionary,
  Metadata,
  Mode,
  TokenizerBuilder,
} = require("lindera");

// Step 1: Train the CRF model
train({
  seed: "resources/training/seed.csv",
  corpus: "resources/training/corpus.txt",
  charDef: "resources/training/char.def",
  unkDef: "resources/training/unk.def",
  featureDef: "resources/training/feature.def",
  rewriteDef: "resources/training/rewrite.def",
  output: "/tmp/model.dat",
  lambda: 1.0,
  maxIter: 100,
});

// Step 2: Export to dictionary source files
exportModel({
  model: "/tmp/model.dat",
  output: "/tmp/dictionary_source",
  metadata: "resources/training/metadata.json",
});

// Step 3: Build the dictionary from exported source files
const metadata = Metadata.fromJsonFile("/tmp/dictionary_source/metadata.json");
buildDictionary("/tmp/dictionary_source", "/tmp/dictionary", metadata);

// Step 4: Use the trained dictionary
const builder = new TokenizerBuilder();
builder.setDictionary("/tmp/dictionary");
builder.setMode(Mode.normal());
const tokenizer = builder.build();

const tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("形態素解析のテスト");
for (const token of tokens) {
  console.log(`${token.surface}\t${token.details.join(",")}`);
}

Lindera Ruby

Lindera Ruby provides Ruby bindings for the Lindera morphological analysis engine, built with Magnus and rb-sys. It brings Lindera's high-performance tokenization capabilities to the Ruby ecosystem with support for Ruby 3.1 and later.

Features

  • Multi-language support: Tokenize Japanese (IPADIC, IPADIC NEologd, UniDic), Korean (ko-dic), and Chinese (CC-CEDICT, Jieba) text
  • Text processing pipeline: Compose character filters and token filters for flexible preprocessing and postprocessing
  • CRF-based dictionary training: Train custom morphological analysis models from annotated corpora (requires train feature)
  • Multiple tokenization modes: Normal and decompose modes for different analysis granularity
  • N-best tokenization: Retrieve multiple tokenization candidates ranked by cost
  • User dictionaries: Extend system dictionaries with custom vocabulary

Integer arguments

An integer parameter takes only the values its setting can hold. default_word_cost of Lindera::Metadata.new takes -32768 to 32767, the context IDs 0 to 65535, and the penalties of Lindera::Penalty.new a 32-bit integer. A count or an index takes 0 or more: the thresholds of Lindera::Penalty.new, index of Schema#get_field_name and Token#get_detail, and n of Tokenizer#tokenize_nbest. max_iter and max_threads of Lindera.train take 1 or more. cost_threshold of Tokenizer#tokenize_nbest takes a 64-bit integer. A value outside the range raises a RangeError that names the parameter and the range; an index past the end still returns nil:

require 'lindera'

begin
  Lindera::Metadata.new(nil, nil, 100_000, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil)
rescue RangeError => e
  puts "#{e.class}: #{e.message}"
  # RangeError: default_word_cost must be an integer between -32768 and 32767, got 100000
end

tokenizer = Lindera::Tokenizer.new(Lindera.load_dictionary('embedded://ipadic'))

begin
  tokenizer.tokenize_nbest('東京都', -1, nil, nil)
rescue RangeError => e
  puts "#{e.class}: #{e.message}"
  # RangeError: n must be an integer between 0 and 18446744073709551615, got -1
end

The float settings of Lindera.train are checked the same way, before any file is read: lambda and eta: take a finite number of 0 or more, and elastic_net_l1_ratio: a number between 0 and 1 (see Training).

Documentation

  • Installation -- Prerequisites, build instructions, and feature flags
  • Quick Start -- A minimal example to get started
  • Tokenizer API -- TokenizerBuilder, Tokenizer, and Token class reference
  • Dictionary Management -- Loading, building, and managing dictionaries
  • Text Processing Pipeline -- Character filters and token filters
  • Training -- Training custom CRF models and exporting dictionaries

Installation

From v6.1.0, lindera-ruby installs from RubyGems as lindera. It is a source gem: gem install compiles the native extension from the bundled Rust source, which takes a few minutes.

Prerequisites

  • Ruby 3.1 or later, with the tools needed to build native gems (a C compiler and make)
  • Rust toolchain 1.89 or later -- Install via rustup
  • libclang -- libclang-dev on Debian/Ubuntu; the Xcode command line tools on macOS
  • Bundler -- only to build from source (gem install bundler)

Install from RubyGems

gem install lindera

Or add it to your Gemfile:

gem "lindera"

[!NOTE] Use lindera v6.1.0 or later. The lindera gems published before v6.1.0 fail to compile during installation; for those versions, build from source as described below.

The gem compiles against the crates.io releases of lindera and lindera-binding of the same version, which it pins exactly. It ships no Cargo.lock, so their dependencies, including the other lindera-* crates, resolve to the latest compatible releases at install time. It builds with the default features (train) and no embedded dictionary; see Obtaining Dictionaries. To enable other feature flags, set LINDERA_FEATURES when installing:

LINDERA_FEATURES="embed-ipadic" gem install lindera

Obtaining Dictionaries

Lindera does not bundle dictionaries with the package. You need to obtain a pre-built dictionary separately.

Download from GitHub Releases

Pre-built dictionaries are available on the GitHub Releases page. Download and extract the dictionary archive to a local directory:

# Example: download and extract the IPADIC dictionary
curl -LO https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases/download/<version>/lindera-ipadic-<version>.zip
unzip lindera-ipadic-<version>.zip -d /path/to/ipadic

Development Build

Build the native extension of lindera-ruby in release mode. Rake puts it in lindera-ruby/lib/lindera/ and does not install the gem; Ruby run with bundle exec from lindera-ruby/ loads it from there:

cd lindera-ruby
bundle install
bundle exec rake compile

For a debug build, run bundle exec rake compile:dev instead of bundle exec rake compile.

Or use the project Makefile, which makes the same release build with the embed-ipadic and train features:

make build-lindera-ruby

Run make test-lindera-ruby to run both the Rust unit tests and the Ruby minitest suite.

Building the Gem

bundle exec rake build (or make package-lindera-ruby) writes the source gem to lindera-ruby/pkg/. It packages the crate as cargo package normalizes it, so the gem compiles outside this repository, against the crates.io releases of lindera and lindera-binding of the same version. Do not run gem build directly: the crate's own Cargo.toml only resolves inside the Cargo workspace.

make test-lindera-ruby-gem (requires Docker) builds the gem, installs it with gem install in a clean ruby container and tokenizes text with it. The test compiles the lindera crates from the checkout, so it also works for versions not yet released on crates.io.

Build with Training Support

The train feature enables CRF-based dictionary training functionality. It is enabled by default:

LINDERA_FEATURES="train" bundle exec rake compile

Feature Flags

Features are specified through the LINDERA_FEATURES environment variable as a comma-separated list, both for bundle exec rake compile and for gem install.

FeatureDescriptionDefault
trainCRF training functionalityEnabled
embed-ipadicEmbed Japanese dictionary (IPADIC) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidicEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidic-cwjEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic CWJ, 1.2 GB) into the binaryDisabled
embed-unidic-csjEmbed Japanese dictionary (UniDic CSJ, 1.2 GB) into the binaryDisabled
embed-sudachidictEmbed Japanese dictionary (SudachiDict) into the binaryDisabled
