API reference

The API reference is available. Please see following URL:

  • lindera-ipadic

Build

This page describes how to build the IPADIC dictionary from source files.

Build system dictionary

Download the IPADIC source files and build the dictionary:

# Download and extract IPADIC source files
% curl -L -o /tmp/mecab-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920.tar.gz "https://Lindera.dev/mecab-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920.tar.gz"
% tar zxvf /tmp/mecab-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920.tar.gz -C /tmp

# Build the dictionary
% lindera build \
  --src /tmp/mecab-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920 \
  --dest /tmp/lindera-ipadic-2.7.0-20250920 \
  --metadata ./lindera-ipadic/metadata.json

Build user dictionary

Build a user dictionary from a CSV file:

% lindera build \
  --src ./resources/user_dict/ipadic_simple_userdic.csv \
  --dest ./resources/user_dict \
  --metadata ./lindera-ipadic/metadata.json \
  --user

For more details about user dictionary format, see Dictionary Format.

Embedding in binary

To embed the IPADIC dictionary directly into the binary:

cargo build --features=embed-ipadic

This allows using embedded://ipadic as the dictionary path without external dictionary files.

Rust API example

use lindera::dictionary::load_dictionary;
use lindera::mode::Mode;
use lindera::segmenter::Segmenter;
use lindera::analysis::tokenizer::Tokenizer;
use lindera::LinderaResult;

fn main() -> LinderaResult<()> {
    let dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")?;
    let segmenter = Segmenter::new(Mode::Normal, dictionary, None);
    let tokenizer = Tokenizer::new(segmenter);

    let text = "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。";
    let mut tokens = tokenizer.tokenize(text)?;
    for token in tokens.iter_mut() {
        let details = token.details().join(",");
        println!("{}\t{}", token.surface.as_ref(), details);
    }
    Ok(())
}

Notice that NEologd treats "形態素解析" (morphological analysis) as a single compound noun, whereas standard IPADIC splits it into "形態素" and "解析".

Tokenize with embedded IPADIC NEologd

% echo "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。" | lindera tokenize \

Rust API example

use lindera::dictionary::load_dictionary;
use lindera::mode::Mode;
use lindera::segmenter::Segmenter;
use lindera::analysis::tokenizer::Tokenizer;
use lindera::LinderaResult;

fn main() -> LinderaResult<()> {
    let dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic-neologd")?;
    let segmenter = Segmenter::new(Mode::Normal, dictionary, None);
    let tokenizer = Tokenizer::new(segmenter);

    let text = "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。";
    let mut tokens = tokenizer.tokenize(text)?;
    for token in tokens.iter_mut() {
        let details = token.details().join(",");
        println!("{}\t{}", token.surface.as_ref(), details);
    }
    Ok(())
}

Lindera UniDic

Lindera UniDic is a Japanese dictionary crate based on UniDic, which uses uniform word unit definitions. UniDic provides more detailed morphological information than IPADIC, with 21 fields per entry.

Contents

  • Dictionary Format -- Field definitions for system and user dictionaries
  • Build -- How to build the dictionary from source
  • Examples -- Tokenization examples

API Reference

  • lindera-unidic

Lindera UniDic

Dictionary version

This repository contains unidic-mecab.

Dictionary format

Refer to the manual for details on the unidic-mecab dictionary format and part-of-speech tags.

IndexName (Japanese)Name (English)Notes
0表層形Surface
1左文脈IDLeft context ID
2右文脈IDRight context ID
3コストCost
4品詞大分類Part-of-speech
5品詞中分類Part-of-speech subcategory 1

7品詞細分類Part-of-speech subcategory 3
8活用型Conjugation type

10語彙素読みReading
11語彙素（語彙素表記 + 語彙素細分類）Lexeme
12書字形出現形Orthographic surface form

14書字形基本形Orthographic base form
15発音形基本形Phonological base form

API reference

The API reference is available. Please see following URL:

  • lindera-unidic

Build

This page describes how to build the UniDic dictionary from source files.

Build system dictionary

Download NINJAL's source package of UniDic 2.1.2 and build the dictionary:

% curl -L -o /tmp/unidic-mecab-2.1.2_src.zip "https://clrd.ninjal.ac.jp/unidic_archive/cwj/2.1.2/unidic-mecab-2.1.2_src.zip"
% shasum -a 256 /tmp/unidic-mecab-2.1.2_src.zip
6cce98269214ce7de6159f61a25ffc5b436375c098cc86d6aa98c0605cbf90d4  /tmp/unidic-mecab-2.1.2_src.zip
% unzip /tmp/unidic-mecab-2.1.2_src.zip -d /tmp

% lindera build \
  --src /tmp/unidic-mecab-2.1.2_src \
  --dest /tmp/lindera-unidic-2.1.2 \
  --metadata ./lindera-unidic/metadata.json \
  --context-id-freq ./lindera-unidic/context_id_freq.txt

[!TIP] lindera-unidic/metadata.json sets connection_id_mapping: true, so the builder relabels the connection-cost matrix's context IDs by access frequency to improve cache locality when looking up connection costs. Passing --context-id-freq / -f with the bundled context_id_freq.txt histogram gives this remapping real corpus frequency data to rank IDs by. Without the flag, the build still succeeds, but falls back to a much weaker entry-count-based proxy and writes this warning to standard error:

[WARN  lindera_dictionary::builder::context_id_remap] connection_id_mapping is enabled but no context-id frequency file was found; falling back to the entry-count proxy, which measured ~0% improvement. Bundle a corpus-derived histogram (see the ctxfreq_dump example) for the real gain.

Either way, tokenization output is unaffected -- the remap is a bijective relabeling that only changes a build-time optimization, never correctness.

Build user dictionary

Build a user dictionary from a CSV file:

% lindera build \
  --src ./resources/user_dict/unidic_simple_userdic.csv \
  --dest ./resources/user_dict \
  --metadata ./lindera-unidic/metadata.json \
  --user

For more details about user dictionary format, see Dictionary Format.

Embedding in binary

To embed the UniDic dictionary directly into the binary:

cargo build --features=embed-unidic

This allows using embedded://unidic as the dictionary path without external dictionary files.

use lindera::dictionary::load_dictionary;

Lindera UniDic CWJ

Lindera UniDic CWJ is a Japanese dictionary crate based on UniDic for contemporary written Japanese (現代書き言葉UniDic) ver.2025.12, the successor of UniDic 3.1, distributed by the National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics (NINJAL). It has 33 fields per entry, 12 more than UniDic 2.1.2, among them the kana forms, the accent and the lexicon and lemma IDs.

Its source is downloaded from NINJAL's official URL, not from lindera.dev, and checked against the SHA-256 that the crate pins. lindera-unidic keeps providing UniDic 2.1.2.

[!NOTE] UniDic CWJ is much larger than the other dictionaries. The built dictionary takes 1.2 GB, 982 MiB of it the connection matrix (24,082 × 21,375). With embed-unidic-cwj, every binary carries those 1.2 GB, and compiling the crate takes about 11 GiB of memory (measured on macOS). The WASM binding does not provide embed-unidic-cwj. To keep binaries small, download the dictionary with lindera download unidic-cwj and load it from its directory.

Contents

  • Dictionary Format -- Field definitions for system and user dictionaries
  • Build -- How to build the dictionary from source
  • Examples -- Tokenization examples

API Reference

  • lindera-unidic-cwj

Lindera UniDic CWJ

Dictionary version

This crate builds UniDic for contemporary written Japanese (現代書き言葉UniDic) ver.2025.12, from NINJAL's full package unidic-cwj-202512_full.zip.

Dictionary format

Refer to the UniDic FAQ for the fields and their values. Fields 0 to 20 are those of UniDic 2.1.2, with the same names.

IndexName (Japanese)Name (English)Notes
0表層形Surface
1左文脈IDLeft context ID
2右文脈IDRight context ID
3コストCost
4品詞大分類Part-of-speech
5品詞中分類Part-of-speech subcategory 1
6品詞小分類Part-of-speech subcategory 2
7品詞細分類Part-of-speech subcategory 3
8活用型Conjugation type
9活用形Conjugation form
10語彙素読みReading
11語彙素（語彙素表記 + 語彙素細分類）Lexeme
12書字形出現形Orthographic surface form
13発音形出現形Phonological surface form
14書字形基本形Orthographic base form
15発音形基本形Phonological base form
16語種Word type
17語頭変化型Initial mutation type
18語頭変化形Initial mutation form
19語末変化型Final mutation type
20語末変化形Final mutation form
21語頭変化結合型Initial connection type
22語末変化結合型Final connection type
23語彙素類Lexeme class
24仮名形出現形Kana
25仮名形基本形Kana base
26語形出現形Form
27語形基本形Form base
28アクセント型Accent type
29アクセント結合型Accent connection typeCan contain commas, such as 動詞%F2@0,名詞%F1
30アクセント修飾型Accent modification type
31語彙表IDLexicon ID
32語彙素IDLemma ID

The JSON output of lindera tokenize writes these fields as strings, with the dictionary's text, as it writes every field of the schema. lexicon_id goes above 2^53, the largest integer a JavaScript number holds exactly, so convert it to a number only with a type that keeps big integers, such as JavaScript's BigInt.

User dictionary format (CSV)

Simple version

IndexName (Japanese)Name (English)Notes
0表層形Surface
1品詞大分類Part-of-speech
2語彙素読みReading

Detailed version

The 33 fields of the dictionary format above, in the same order. After index 32, it can be freely expanded.

API reference

The API reference is available. Please see following URL:

  • lindera-unidic-cwj

Build

This page describes how to build the UniDic CWJ dictionary from source files.

Build system dictionary

Download NINJAL's full package, extract the four files the builder reads, and build the dictionary. The lighter package, unidic-cwj-202512.zip, holds only MeCab's compiled files and cannot be built from.

% curl -L -o /tmp/unidic-cwj-202512_full.zip "https://clrd.ninjal.ac.jp/unidic_archive/2512/unidic-cwj-202512_full.zip"
% shasum -a 256 /tmp/unidic-cwj-202512_full.zip
ca02ad51c8ae238373dcb150eec014f1ad9f05f54c7416a16c2fe444fd4921b3  /tmp/unidic-cwj-202512_full.zip
% unzip /tmp/unidic-cwj-202512_full.zip lex.csv matrix.def char.def unk.def -d /tmp/unidic-cwj-202512

% lindera build \
  --src /tmp/unidic-cwj-202512 \
  --dest /tmp/lindera-unidic-cwj-202512 \
  --metadata ./lindera-unidic-cwj/metadata.json \
  --context-id-freq ./lindera-unidic-cwj/context_id_freq.txt

The package is 2.77 GiB, and the four files take 7.95 GiB, matrix.def 7.70 GiB of them. The builder reads matrix.def in blocks of 64 MiB, so it holds the 982 MiB matrix and one block rather than the whole file: building the dictionary allocated at most 2.48 GiB on macOS.

lindera-unidic-cwj/metadata.json sets connection_id_mapping: true, so the builder relabels the context IDs of the connection-cost matrix by how often tokenization reads them, which keeps the cells it reads close together in memory. Pass the crate's context_id_freq.txt with --context-id-freq / -f: it was counted over resources/bocchan.txt with the ctxfreq_dump example. Without it, the build still succeeds, but ranks the IDs by a much weaker entry-count proxy and warns, as for UniDic. Either way the tokens are the same: the relabeling keeps every cost.

Build user dictionary

Build a user dictionary from a CSV file. The simple format is the same as UniDic 2.1.2's:

% lindera build \
  --src ./resources/user_dict/unidic_simple_userdic.csv \
  --dest ./resources/user_dict \
  --metadata ./lindera-unidic-cwj/metadata.json \
  --user

For more details about user dictionary format, see Dictionary Format.

Embedding in binary

To embed the UniDic CWJ dictionary directly into the binary:

cargo build --features=embed-unidic-cwj

This allows using embedded://unidic-cwj as the dictionary path without external dictionary files. The binary then carries the 1.2 GB dictionary, and compiling it takes about 11 GiB of memory.

の	助詞,格助詞,*,*,*,*,ノ,の,の,ノ,の,ノ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,格助,ノ,ノ,ノ,ノ,*,名詞%F1,*,7968444268028416,28989
形態	名詞,普通名詞,一般,*,*,*,ケイタイ,形態,形態,ケータイ,形態,ケータイ,漢,*,*,*,*,*,*,体,ケイタイ,ケイタイ,ケイタイ,ケイタイ,0,C2,*,3024215389381120,11002

を	助詞,格助詞,*,*,*,*,ヲ,を,を,オ,を,オ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,格助,ヲ,ヲ,ヲ,ヲ,*,動詞%F2@0,名詞%F1,形容詞%F2@-1,*,11381878116459008,41407
行う	動詞,一般,*,*,五段-ワア行,連体形-一般,オコナウ,行う,行う,オコナウ,行う,オコナウ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,用,オコナウ,オコナウ,オコナウ,オコナウ,0,C2,*,1340038453535425,4875
こと	名詞,普通名詞,一般,*,*,*,コト,事,こと,コト,こと,コト,和,コ濁,基本形,*,*,*,B1WS2WB3WB6SjShS,体,コト,コト,コト,コト,2,C3,*,3528350027096576,12836
が	助詞,格助詞,*,*,*,*,ガ,が,が,ガ,が,ガ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,格助,ガ,ガ,ガ,ガ,*,動詞%F2@0,名詞%F1,*,2168520431510016,7889
でき	動詞,非自立可能,*,*,上一段-カ行,連用形-一般,デキル,出来る,でき,デキ,できる,デキル,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,用,デキ,デキル,デキ,デキル,2,C1,M4@1,7043480111161985,25624
ます	助動詞,*,*,*,助動詞-マス,終止形-一般,マス,ます,ます,マス,ます,マス,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,助動,マス,マス,マス,マス,*,動詞%F4@1,*,9812325267808939,35697
。	補助記号,句点,*,*,*,*,*,。,。,*,。,*,記号,*,*,*,*,*,*,補助,*,*,*,*,*,*,*,6880571302400,25

The segmentation follows UniDic's short units, as UniDic 2.1.2's does ("日本" and "語", "形態" and "素"), and each token carries the 33 fields. The accent connection type of "を" holds commas (動詞%F2@0,名詞%F1,形容詞%F2@-1): it is one field, quoted in lex.csv.

Tokenize with embedded UniDic CWJ

% echo "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://unidic-cwj

The embedded dictionary is built from the same files, so the output is the same as above.

NOTE: To include the UniDic CWJ dictionary in the binary, build with the --features=embed-unidic-cwj option. The binary then carries the 1.2 GB dictionary.

Rust API example

use lindera::dictionary::load_dictionary;
use lindera::mode::Mode;
use lindera::segmenter::Segmenter;
use lindera::analysis::tokenizer::Tokenizer;
use lindera::LinderaResult;

fn main() -> LinderaResult<()> {
    let dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://unidic-cwj")?;
    let segmenter = Segmenter::new(Mode::Normal, dictionary, None);
    let tokenizer = Tokenizer::new(segmenter);

    let text = "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。";
    let mut tokens = tokenizer.tokenize(text)?;
    for token in tokens.iter_mut() {
        let details = token.details().join(",");
        println!("{}\t{}", token.surface.as_ref(), details);
    }
    Ok(())
}

Lindera UniDic CSJ

Lindera UniDic CSJ is a Japanese dictionary crate based on UniDic for contemporary spoken Japanese (現代話し言葉UniDic) ver.2025.12, distributed by the National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics (NINJAL). It is made for transcriptions of speech: NINJAL trained it on the Corpus of Everyday Japanese Conversation (CEJC).

It has the same words and the same 33 fields per entry as UniDic CWJ, the UniDic for contemporary written Japanese, with other word costs and another connection matrix, so the two split some text differently. Use UniDic CSJ for transcribed speech and UniDic CWJ for written text.

Its source is downloaded from NINJAL's official URL, not from lindera.dev, and checked against the SHA-256 that the crate pins.

[!NOTE] UniDic CSJ is as large as UniDic CWJ. The built dictionary takes 1.2 GB, 1,002 MiB of it the connection matrix (24,314 × 21,609). With embed-unidic-csj, every binary carries those 1.2 GB, and compiling the crate takes as much memory as for UniDic CWJ: 8 to 11 GiB in the builds measured on macOS. The WASM binding does not provide embed-unidic-csj. To keep binaries small, download the dictionary with lindera download unidic-csj and load it from its directory.

Contents

  • Dictionary Format -- Field definitions for system and user dictionaries
  • Build -- How to build the dictionary from source
  • Examples -- Tokenization examples

API Reference

  • lindera-unidic-csj

Lindera UniDic CSJ

Dictionary version

This crate builds UniDic for contemporary spoken Japanese (現代話し言葉UniDic) ver.2025.12, from NINJAL's full package unidic-csj-202512_full.zip.

Dictionary format

Refer to the UniDic FAQ for the fields and their values. Fields 0 to 20 are those of UniDic 2.1.2, with the same names, and all 33 are those of UniDic CWJ.

IndexName (Japanese)Name (English)Notes
0表層形Surface
1左文脈IDLeft context ID
2右文脈IDRight context ID
3コストCost
4品詞大分類Part-of-speech
5品詞中分類Part-of-speech subcategory 1
6品詞小分類Part-of-speech subcategory 2
7品詞細分類Part-of-speech subcategory 3
8活用型Conjugation type
9活用形Conjugation form
10語彙素読みReading
11語彙素（語彙素表記 + 語彙素細分類）Lexeme
12書字形出現形Orthographic surface form
13発音形出現形Phonological surface form
14書字形基本形Orthographic base form
15発音形基本形Phonological base form
16語種Word type
17語頭変化型Initial mutation type
18語頭変化形Initial mutation form
19語末変化型Final mutation type
20語末変化形Final mutation form
21語頭変化結合型Initial connection type
22語末変化結合型Final connection type
23語彙素類Lexeme class
24仮名形出現形Kana
25仮名形基本形Kana base
26語形出現形Form
27語形基本形Form base
28アクセント型Accent type
29アクセント結合型Accent connection typeCan contain commas, such as 動詞%F2@0,名詞%F1
30アクセント修飾型Accent modification type
31語彙表IDLexicon ID
32語彙素IDLemma ID

The JSON output of lindera tokenize writes these fields as strings, with the dictionary's text, as it writes every field of the schema. lexicon_id goes above 2^53, the largest integer a JavaScript number holds exactly, so convert it to a number only with a type that keeps big integers, such as JavaScript's BigInt.

User dictionary format (CSV)

Simple version

IndexName (Japanese)Name (English)Notes
0表層形Surface
1品詞大分類Part-of-speech
2語彙素読みReading

Detailed version

The 33 fields of the dictionary format above, in the same order. After index 32, it can be freely expanded.

API reference

The API reference is available. Please see following URL:

  • lindera-unidic-csj

Build

This page describes how to build the UniDic CSJ dictionary from source files.

Build system dictionary

Download NINJAL's full package, extract the four files the builder reads, and build the dictionary. The lighter package, unidic-csj-202512.zip, holds only MeCab's compiled files and cannot be built from.

% curl -L -o /tmp/unidic-csj-202512_full.zip "https://clrd.ninjal.ac.jp/unidic_archive/2512/unidic-csj-202512_full.zip"
% shasum -a 256 /tmp/unidic-csj-202512_full.zip
f737d26ce9daf96347e1ccaf34896a36651ffb7ceff91d4d8041591ff7a387e4  /tmp/unidic-csj-202512_full.zip
% unzip /tmp/unidic-csj-202512_full.zip lex.csv matrix.def char.def unk.def -d /tmp/unidic-csj-202512

% lindera build \
  --src /tmp/unidic-csj-202512 \
  --dest /tmp/lindera-unidic-csj-202512 \
  --metadata ./lindera-unidic-csj/metadata.json \
  --context-id-freq ./lindera-unidic-csj/context_id_freq.txt

The package is 2.81 GiB, and the four files take 8.18 GiB, matrix.def 7.92 GiB of them. The builder reads matrix.def in blocks of 64 MiB, so it holds the 1,002 MiB matrix and one block rather than the whole file: building the dictionary allocated at most 2.50 GiB on macOS.

lindera-unidic-csj/metadata.json is UniDic CWJ's with another name: the two packages have the same fields. It sets connection_id_mapping: true, and the crate ships its own context_id_freq.txt, counted over resources/bocchan.txt as UniDic CWJ's is: pass it with --context-id-freq / -f. See UniDic CWJ for what the relabeling does.

Build user dictionary

Build a user dictionary from a CSV file. The simple format is the same as UniDic 2.1.2's:

% lindera build \
  --src ./resources/user_dict/unidic_simple_userdic.csv \
  --dest ./resources/user_dict \
  --metadata ./lindera-unidic-csj/metadata.json \
  --user

For more details about user dictionary format, see Dictionary Format.

Embedding in binary

To embed the UniDic CSJ dictionary directly into the binary:

cargo build --features=embed-unidic-csj

This allows using embedded://unidic-csj as the dictionary path without external dictionary files. The binary then carries the 1.2 GB dictionary, and compiling it takes 8 to 11 GiB of memory, as for UniDic CWJ.

Examples

This page shows tokenization examples using the UniDic CSJ dictionary.

Tokenize with external UniDic CSJ

Download the dictionary with lindera download unidic-csj, or build it, and pass its directory:

% echo "そんなら君の指を切ってみろ。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict /tmp/lindera-unidic-csj-202512

そんな	形状詞,一般,*,*,*,*,ソンナ,そんな,そんな,ソンナ,そんな,ソンナ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,相,ソンナ,ソンナ,ソンナ,ソンナ,0,C2,*,5912632401994240,21510
ら	接尾辞,名詞的,一般,*,*,*,ラ,等,ら,ラ,ら,ラ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,接尾体,ラ,ラ,ラ,ラ,*,C3,*,10877477157216768,39572
君	接尾辞,名詞的,一般,*,*,*,クン,君,君,クン,君,クン,漢,*,*,*,*,*,*,接尾体,クン,クン,クン,クン,*,C4,*,2928557877764608,10654
の	助詞,格助詞,*,*,*,*,ノ,の,の,ノ,の,ノ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,格助,ノ,ノ,ノ,ノ,*,名詞%F1,*,7968444268028416,28989
指	名詞,普通名詞,一般,*,*,*,ユビ,指,指,ユビ,指,ユビ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,体,ユビ,ユビ,ユビ,ユビ,2,C3,*,10688361157239296,38884
を	助詞,格助詞,*,*,*,*,ヲ,を,を,オ,を,オ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,格助,ヲ,ヲ,ヲ,ヲ,*,動詞%F2@0,名詞%F1,形容詞%F2@-1,*,11381878116459008,41407
切っ	動詞,非自立可能,*,*,五段-ラ行,連用形-促音便,キル,切る,切っ,キッ,切る,キル,和,キ濁,基本形,*,*,*,*,用,キッ,キル,キッ,キル,1,C1,*,2626192180126340,9554
て	助詞,接続助詞,*,*,*,*,テ,て,て,テ,て,テ,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,接助,テ,テ,テ,テ,*,動詞%F1,形容詞%F2@-1,*,6837321680953856,24874
みろ	動詞,非自立可能,*,*,上一段-マ行,命令形,ミル,見る,みろ,ミロ,みる,ミル,和,*,*,*,*,*,*,用,ミロ,ミル,ミロ,ミル,1,C1,*,10148500948001573,36920
。	補助記号,句点,*,*,*,*,*,。,。,*,。,*,記号,*,*,*,*,*,*,補助,*,*,*,*,*,*,*,6880571302400,25
EOS

The fields are those of UniDic CWJ, but the costs are not, so the two can split a text differently: UniDic CSJ splits "そんなら" as "そんな" and "ら", where UniDic CWJ splits it as "そん" and "なら".

Tokenize with embedded UniDic CSJ

% echo "そんなら君の指を切ってみろ。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://unidic-csj

The embedded dictionary is built from the same files, so the output is the same as above.

NOTE: To include the UniDic CSJ dictionary in the binary, build with the --features=embed-unidic-csj option. The binary then carries the 1.2 GB dictionary.

Rust API example

use lindera::dictionary::load_dictionary;
use lindera::mode::Mode;
use lindera::segmenter::Segmenter;
use lindera::analysis::tokenizer::Tokenizer;
use lindera::LinderaResult;

fn main() -> LinderaResult<()> {
    let dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://unidic-csj")?;
    let segmenter = Segmenter::new(Mode::Normal, dictionary, None);
    let tokenizer = Tokenizer::new(segmenter);

    let text = "そんなら君の指を切ってみろ。";
    let mut tokens = tokenizer.tokenize(text)?;
    for token in tokens.iter_mut() {
        let details = token.details().join(",");
        println!("{}\t{}", token.surface.as_ref(), details);
    }
    Ok(())
}

Lindera SudachiDict

Lindera SudachiDict is a Japanese dictionary crate based on SudachiDict, the actively maintained dictionary used by the Sudachi morphological analyzer. It is updated several times a year upstream, so recent vocabulary (令和, スマホ, 推し活, ...) is in-vocabulary. Each entry has 19 fields, including SudachiDict-specific columns such as the normalized form, split references, and synonym group IDs.

The dictionary source files are mirrored at lindera/sudachidict. The bundled version is 20260723 (small + core + notcore lexicons), from the mirror's tag 0.1.0-20260723, which adds Sudachi's own char.def (sudachi.rs v0.7.0).

[!NOTE] This dictionary reproduces SudachiDict's vocabulary and lattice behavior, and reads Sudachi's own char.def as Sudachi does, but not the Sudachi engine plugins (katakana/numeric joining, input normalization, A/B/C split modes) or a few engine rules. See Behavioral differences from Sudachi for details.

Contents

  • Dictionary Format -- Field definitions for system and user dictionaries
  • Build -- How to build the dictionary from source
  • Examples -- Tokenization examples

API Reference

  • lindera-sudachidict

Lindera SudachiDict

Dictionary version

This repository contains SudachiDict 20260723 (small + core + notcore lexicons), from the mirror's tag 0.1.0-20260723, with Sudachi's own char.def (sudachi.rs v0.7.0), which "char_def_format": "sudachi" in metadata.json reads as Sudachi does. "lexicon_format": "sudachi" decodes the escapes of the lexicons (a backslash, u and hex digits, which they write for (, ), /, ,, | and ") in every field, as Sudachi does, in user dictionaries too.

Dictionary format

Refer to the SudachiDict documentation for details on the dictionary format and part-of-speech tags.

IndexName (Japanese)Name (English)Notes
0表層形Surface
1左文脈IDLeft context ID
2右文脈IDRight context ID
3コストCost
4見出し（解析結果表示用）Display surface
5品詞大分類Part-of-speech
6品詞中分類Part-of-speech subcategory 1
7品詞小分類Part-of-speech subcategory 2
8品詞細分類Part-of-speech subcategory 3
9活用型Conjugation type
10活用形Conjugation form
11読みReading
12正規化表記Normalized form
13辞書形IDDictionary form word ID
14分割タイプSplit modeA/B/C
15A単位分割情報Split references (A)
16B単位分割情報Split references (B)
17語構成Word structure
18同義語グループIDSynonym group IDs

[!NOTE] Because the display surface sits at index 4 (before the part-of-speech columns), the first token detail is the display surface -- not the part-of-speech as in IPADIC or UniDic. Code that reads the details positionally must account for this; schema-aware access such as token.get("part_of_speech") returns the part-of-speech directly. The part-of-speech token filters (japanese_stop_tags, japanese_keep_tags, japanese_compound_word, and japanese_number with tags) resolve the part-of-speech columns through the dictionary schema, so they match this dictionary the same way they match IPADIC or UniDic (see lindera/lindera#997).

User dictionary format (CSV)

Simple version

IndexName (Japanese)Name (English)Notes
0表層形Surface
1品詞大分類Part-of-speech
2読みReading

Detailed version

The detailed version follows the dictionary format above (19 columns).

IndexName (Japanese)Name (English)Notes
0-18-Same as the dictionary format
19--After 19, it can be freely expanded.

API reference

The API reference is available. Please see following URL:

  • lindera-sudachidict

Build

This page describes how to build the SudachiDict dictionary from source files.

Build system dictionary

Download the SudachiDict source archive and build the dictionary:

% curl -L -o /tmp/sudachidict-0.1.0-20260723.tar.gz "https://lindera.dev/sudachidict-0.1.0-20260723.tar.gz"
% tar zxvf /tmp/sudachidict-0.1.0-20260723.tar.gz -C /tmp

% lindera build \
  --src /tmp/sudachidict-0.1.0-20260723 \
  --dest /tmp/lindera-sudachidict \
  --metadata ./lindera-sudachidict/metadata.json

The archive bundles the raw lexicons (small + core + notcore, whose escapes "lexicon_format": "sudachi" in metadata.json decodes as Sudachi does), the connection matrix, Sudachi's own char.def (from sudachi.rs v0.7.0, which "char_def_format": "sudachi" in metadata.json reads as Sudachi does) and the pre-aligned unk.def, so no manual preprocessing is needed. The built dictionary is about 570MB.

[!TIP] To build from a newer upstream SudachiDict release than the bundled one, see SudachiDict (Custom Build), which builds directly from the upstream raw distribution.

Build user dictionary

Build a user dictionary from a CSV file:

% lindera build \
  --src ./resources/user_dict/sudachidict_simple_userdic.csv \
  --dest ./resources/user_dict \
  --metadata ./lindera-sudachidict/metadata.json \
  --user

For more details about user dictionary format, see Dictionary Format.

Embedding in binary

To embed the SudachiDict dictionary directly into the binary:

cargo build --features=embed-sudachidict

This allows using embedded://sudachidict as the dictionary path without external dictionary files.

[!NOTE] The embedded dictionary adds roughly 570MB to the binary. If binary size matters, prefer building the dictionary to a directory as shown above and loading it by path.

Examples

This page shows tokenization examples using the SudachiDict dictionary.

Tokenize with external SudachiDict

% echo "令和五年に始まった。推し活が楽しい。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict /tmp/lindera-sudachidict

令和	令和,名詞,固有名詞,一般,*,*,*,レイワ,令和,*,A,*,*,*,*
五	五,名詞,数詞,*,*,*,*,ゴ,五,*,A,*,*,*,017040
年	年,名詞,普通名詞,助数詞可能,*,*,*,ネン,年,*,A,*,*,*,*
に	に,助詞,格助詞,*,*,*,*,ニ,に,*,A,*,*,*,*
始まっ	始まっ,動詞,一般,*,*,五段-ラ行,連用形-促音便,ハジマッ,始まる,380965,A,*,*,*,000378
た	た,助動詞,*,*,*,助動詞-タ,終止形-一般,タ,た,83558,A,*,*,*,*
。	。,補助記号,句点,*,*,*,*,。,。,*,A,*,*,*,*
推し活	推し活,名詞,普通名詞,一般,*,*,*,オシカツ,推し活,*,A,*,*,*,*
が	が,助詞,格助詞,*,*,*,*,ガ,が,*,A,*,*,*,*
楽しい	楽しい,形容詞,一般,*,*,形容詞,終止形-一般,タノシイ,楽しい,519727,A,*,*,*,*
。	。,補助記号,句点,*,*,*,*,。,。,*,A,*,*,*,*
EOS

Notice that 令和 is a single proper noun (IPADIC and UniDic 2.1.2 split it into 令 and 和) and 推し活 is in-vocabulary. The first detail column is the display surface, followed by the part-of-speech columns and SudachiDict-specific columns (normalized form, split mode, synonym group IDs).

Tokenize with embedded SudachiDict

% echo "令和五年に始まった。推し活が楽しい。" | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://sudachidict

The output is the same as above.

NOTE: To include SudachiDict dictionary in the binary, you must build with the --features=embed-sudachidict option.

Rust API example

use lindera::dictionary::load_dictionary;
use lindera::mode::Mode;
use lindera::segmenter::Segmenter;
use lindera::analysis::tokenizer::Tokenizer;
use lindera::LinderaResult;

fn main() -> LinderaResult<()> {
    let dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://sudachidict")?;
    let segmenter = Segmenter::new(Mode::Normal, dictionary, None);
    let tokenizer = Tokenizer::new(segmenter);

    let text = "令和五年に始まった。推し活が楽しい。";
    let mut tokens = tokenizer.tokenize(text)?;
    for token in tokens.iter_mut() {
        // Schema-aware access: works regardless of column positions
        let pos = token.get("part_of_speech").unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        let details = token.details().join(",");
        println!("{}\t{}\t{}", token.surface.as_ref(), pos, details);
    }
    Ok(())
}

Lindera ko-dic

Lindera ko-dic is a Korean dictionary crate based on mecab-ko-dic.

Contents

  • Dictionary Format -- Field definitions for system and user dictionaries
  • Build -- How to build the dictionary from source
  • Examples -- Tokenization examples

API Reference

  • lindera-ko-dic

Lindera ko-dic

Dictionary version

This repository contains mecab-ko-dic.

Dictionary format

Information about the dictionary format and part-of-speech tags used by mecab-ko-dic id documented in this Google Spreadsheet, linked to from mecab-ko-dic's repository readme.

Note how ko-dic has one less feature column than NAIST JDIC, and has an altogether different set of information (e.g. doesn't provide the "original form" of the word).

The tags are a slight modification of those specified by 세종 (Sejong), whatever that is. The mappings from Sejong to mecab-ko-dic's tag names are given in tab 태그 v2.0 on the above-linked spreadsheet.

The dictionary format is specified fully (in Korean) in tab 사전 형식 v2.0 of the spreadsheet. Any blank values default to *.

IndexName (Korean)Name (English)Notes
0표면Surface
1왼쪽 문맥 IDLeft context ID
2오른쪽 문맥 IDRight context ID
3비용Cost
4품사 태그Part-of-speech tagSee 태그 v2.0 tab on spreadsheet
5의미 부류Meaning(too few examples for me to be sure)
6종성 유무Presence or absenceT for true; F for false; else *
7읽기Readingusually matches surface, but may differ for foreign words e.g. Chinese character words
8타입TypeOne of: Inflect (활용); Compound (복합명사); or Preanalysis (기분석)
9첫번째 품사First part-of-speeche.g. given a part-of-speech tag of "VV+EM+VX+EP", would return VV
10마지막 품사Last part-of-speeche.g. given a part-of-speech tag of "VV+EM+VX+EP", would return EP
11표현Expression활용, 복합명사, 기분석이 어떻게 구성되는지 알려주는 필드 -- Field that tells how inflected forms, compound nouns, and pre-analyzed entries are composed

Left-space penalty

mecab-ko (the MeCab fork mecab-ko-dic is built for) raises the connection cost of a word whose left side is preceded by skipped whitespace (whitespace that the previous word's surface does not end with) when its pos-id.def id is listed in dicrc:

left-space-penalty-factor = 100,3000,120,6000,172,3000,183,3000,184,3000,185,3000,200,3000,210,6000,220,3000,221,3000,222,3000,230,3000

Lindera does not store pos-id.def ids, but every listed id corresponds to the entry's first part-of-speech tag (for Inflect rows, the First part-of-speech column), so the same rules are written by tag. ko-dic ships them in its metadata.json (space_penalty), and Segmenter::new applies them by default. Opt out with Segmenter::space_penalty(None), "space_penalty": false in the segmenter config, or lindera tokenize --disable-space-penalty; explicit rules go through Segmenter::space_penalty, a space_penalty object, or --space-penalty-rules. The shipped rules are present only in a ko-dic built by Lindera 6.1.0 or later; with a ko-dic from the v6.0.0 release the penalty silently stays off until the dictionary is rebuilt, while --space-penalty-rules works regardless.

pos-id.def idsFirst part-of-speech tagsCost
100, 200 (Inflect)EC, EF, EP, ETM, ETN3000
172, 230 (Inflect)VCP3000
183, 184, 185, 220, 221, 222 (Inflect)XSA, XSN, XSV3000
120, 210 (Inflect)JC, JKB, JKC, JKG, JKO, JKQ, JKS, JKV, JX6000
{
  "rules": [
    { "pos": ["EC", "EF", "EP", "ETM", "ETN", "VCP", "XSA", "XSN", "XSV"], "cost": 3000 },
    { "pos": ["JC", "JKB", "JKC", "JKG", "JKO", "JKQ", "JKS", "JKV", "JX"], "cost": 6000 }
  ]
}

echo "검색 이 잘 된다" | lindera tokenize --dict embedded://ko-dic

이 after the space is read as the interjection IC (as mecab-ko does) instead of the subject particle JKS; with --disable-space-penalty it reads as JKS. See the Segmenter documentation for the semantics.

Whitespace

mecab-ko skips whitespace when it builds the lattice, so a word after a space connects to the word before it. The SPACE unknown-word entry (unk.def: SPACE,1798,3563,996) is therefore never connected to anything during training, and its row and column of matrix.def are all zero. Lindera skips whitespace the same way by default. With --disable-skip-whitespace (Segmenter::skip_whitespace(false), "skip_whitespace": false) whitespace stays in the lattice as that entry, which resets the context at every space: 2년 전 대회 then reads 전 as 저/NP + ㄴ/JX instead of the noun NNG, and 하고 있다 reads 있 as a main verb instead of the auxiliary VX.

9첫번째 품사first part-of-speeche.g. given a part-of-speech tag of "VV+EM+VX+EP", would return VV
10마지막 품사last part-of-speeche.g. given a part-of-speech tag of "VV+EM+VX+EP", would return EP
11표현expression활용, 복합명사, 기분석이 어떻게 구성되는지 알려주는 필드 -- Field that tells how inflected forms, compound nouns, and pre-analyzed entries are composed
12--After 12, it can be freely expanded.

API reference

The API reference is available. Please see following URL:

  • lindera-ko-dic

Build

Build system dictionary

Download the official release of mecab-ko-dic from the Downloads of its upstream repository on Bitbucket, extract it, and build the dictionary:

% curl -L -o /tmp/mecab-ko-dic-2.1.1-20180720.tar.gz "https://bitbucket.org/eunjeon/mecab-ko-dic/downloads/mecab-ko-dic-2.1.1-20180720.tar.gz"
% shasum -a 256 /tmp/mecab-ko-dic-2.1.1-20180720.tar.gz
fd62d3d6d8fa85145528065fabad4d7cb20f6b2201e71be4081a4e9701a5b330  /tmp/mecab-ko-dic-2.1.1-20180720.tar.gz
% tar zxvf /tmp/mecab-ko-dic-2.1.1-20180720.tar.gz -C /tmp
% lindera build \
  --src /tmp/mecab-ko-dic-2.1.1-20180720 \
  --dest /tmp/lindera-ko-dic-2.1.1-20180720 \
  --metadata ./lindera-ko-dic/metadata.json \
  --context-id-freq ./lindera-ko-dic/context_id_freq.txt

[!TIP] lindera-ko-dic/metadata.json sets connection_id_mapping: true, so the builder relabels the connection-cost matrix's context IDs by access frequency to improve cache locality when looking up connection costs. Passing --context-id-freq / -f with the bundled context_id_freq.txt histogram gives this remapping real corpus frequency data to rank IDs by. Without the flag, the build still succeeds, but falls back to a much weaker entry-count-based proxy and writes this warning to standard error:

[WARN  lindera_dictionary::builder::context_id_remap] connection_id_mapping is enabled but no context-id frequency file was found; falling back to the entry-count proxy, which measured ~0% improvement. Bundle a corpus-derived histogram (see the ctxfreq_dump example) for the real gain.

Either way, tokenization output is unaffected -- the remap is a bijective relabeling that only changes a build-time optimization, never correctness.

Build user dictionary

% lindera build \
  --src ./resources/user_dict/ko-dic_simple_userdic.csv \
  --dest ./resources/user_dict \
  --metadata ./lindera-ko-dic/metadata.json \
  --user

Embedding the dictionary

To embed the ko-dic dictionary directly into the binary, build with the following feature flag:

% cargo build --features=embed-ko-dic

Examples

Tokenize with external ko-dic

% echo "한국어의형태해석을실시할수있습니다." | lindera tokenize \
  --dict /tmp/lindera-ko-dic-2.1.1-20180720

한국어  NNG,*,F,한국어,Compound,*,*,한국/NNG/*+어/NNG/*
의      JKG,*,F,의,*,*,*,*
형태    NNG,*,F,형태,*,*,*,*
해석    NNG,행위,T,해석,*,*,*,*
을      JKO,*,T,을,*,*,*,*
실시    NNG,행위,F,실시,*,*,*,*
할      XSV+ETM,*,T,할,Inflect,XSV,ETM,하/XSV/*+ᆯ/ETM/*
수      NNB,*,F,수,*,*,*,*
있      VV,*,T,있,*,*,*,*
습니다  EF,*,F,습니다,*,*,*,*
.       SF,*,*,*,*,*,*,*
EOS

Tokenize with embedded ko-dic

% echo "한국어의형태해석을실시할수있습니다." | lindera tokenize \
  --dict embedded://ko-dic

한국어  NNG,*,F,한국어,Compound,*,*,한국/NNG/*+어/NNG/*
의      JKG,*,F,의,*,*,*,*
형태    NNG,*,F,형태,*,*,*,*
해석    NNG,행위,T,해석,*,*,*,*
을      JKO,*,T,을,*,*,*,*
실시    NNG,행위,F,실시,*,*,*,*

수      NNB,*,F,수,*,*,*,*

NOTE: To include ko-dic dictionary in the binary, you must build with the --features=embed-ko-dic option.

Rust API example

use lindera::dictionary::load_dictionary;
use lindera::mode::Mode;
use lindera::segmenter::Segmenter;
use lindera::analysis::tokenizer::Tokenizer;
use lindera::LinderaResult;

fn main() -> LinderaResult<()> {
    let dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://ko-dic")?;
    let segmenter = Segmenter::new(Mode::Normal, dictionary, None);
    let tokenizer = Tokenizer::new(segmenter);

    let text = "한국어의형태해석을실시할수있습니다.";
    let mut tokens = tokenizer.tokenize(text)?;
    for token in tokens.iter_mut() {
        let details = token.details().join(",");
        println!("{}\t{}", token.surface.as_ref(), details);
    }
    Ok(())
}
