With keep_whitespace false (the default), v7.0.0 skips whitespace in the Viterbi lattice, as MeCab does: the word after a space connects directly to the word before it. v6 dropped whitespace from the output but kept it in the lattice as the SPACE unknown word, so the words around a space connected to that node instead of to each other. How much that changed depends on the dictionary's connection costs for the node: in ko-dic they are all zero, so every space cut the context between the words around it; in IPADIC and UniDic they are not zero, and the node's costs stood in for the connection between the words.

The output changes only for sentences that contain whitespace. That includes a sentence that ends with the \n or \t it was split at, such as a line that does not end with 。: its last word now connects to the end of the sentence directly.

DictionaryEffectExample
ko-dicSpaced Korean text now follows mecab-ko2년 전 대회: 전 is NNG, not 저/NP + ㄴ/JX; 하고 있다: 있 is VX, not VV
IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd, UniDicA word after a half-width space connects to the word before it, as in MeCabIPADIC Google が 新しい: が is a case particle, not a conjunction; 東京 都: 都 is a suffix, as in MeCab
SudachiDictNo change: its metadata.json sets skip_whitespace to false, because Sudachi keeps whitespace in the lattice and the costs assume it—
CC-CEDICTNo change in the best path (the dictionary has no connection costs); N-best costs no longer include the whitespace nodes—
JiebaNo change in the best path on the 247 sentences with a space of UD Chinese GSD and of the GSDSimp dev and test splits; N-best costs no longer include the whitespace nodes—

The default comes from the dictionary's metadata.json; a dictionary that does not set skip_whitespace skips. A SudachiDict built by Lindera 6.x has no such setting, but it no longer loads anyway; the rebuilt one has it.

Token surfaces and offsets never include the skipped whitespace; whitespace that belongs to a dictionary entry, inside it or at its end, stays in that entry's token, as in MeCab (see the previous section). Skipping does not change the segmentation of text without whitespace. keep_whitespace(true) keeps whitespace in the lattice, so its output is the same as in v6; beyond the whitespace tokens, it can differ from the default v7 output, which skips whitespace.

To get the v6 handling of whitespace back, turn skipping off; whitespace is still dropped from the output. This does not undo the other output changes in this guide, such as Unknown words start at every position, as in MeCab. Leaving skip_whitespace out of the configuration, or setting it to null, keeps the dictionary's default:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
// Segmenter
let segmenter = Segmenter::new(Mode::Normal, dictionary, None).skip_whitespace(false);
// SegmentWorker
worker.set_skip_whitespace(false);
}
# Configuration file / TokenizerBuilder::set_segmenter_skip_whitespace(false)
segmenter:
  skip_whitespace: false

lindera tokenize --disable-skip-whitespace

The language bindings set it on TokenizerBuilder: set_skip_whitespace(False) in Python, set_skip_whitespace(false) in Ruby, and setSkipWhitespace(false) in Node.js, PHP and WASM. null (None in Python, nil in Ruby) goes back to the dictionary's default.

Overlapping char.def lines are resolved as in MeCab

A dictionary's char.def can list the same code point on several lines. Up to v6.2.0, the dictionary builder gave such a code point the categories of every line that covers it. v7.0.0 uses only the last line, as MeCab, vibrato and Kuromoji do. In the bundled dictionaries, three characters change (ko-dic calls the kanji categories HANJA and HANJANUMERIC, and CC-CEDICT and Jieba call them CHINESE and CHINESENUMERIC):

Characterv6 categoriesv7 categoriesEffect
Ð (U+00D0)SPACE, ALPHAALPHAEvery dictionary except ko-dic and SudachiDict maps U+00D0 to SPACE (a typo for U+000D inherited from mecab-ipadic) before the ALPHA range (SudachiDict did too up to v6.2.0; from v7.0.0 it has Sudachi's own char.def, which does not, see SudachiDict reads Sudachi's own char.def), so Ð was dropped as whitespace and split the word around it. GUÐMUNDUR さん now gives GUÐMUNDUR and さん instead of GU, MUNDUR and さん
々 (U+3005)KANJI, SYMBOLSYMBOLDictionary words such as 人々 and 佐々木 are unchanged. After a kanji that the dictionary does not know, 々 is a token of its own, as in MeCab: 龘々 gives 龘 and 々 instead of one unknown word. With ko-dic, 々 is tagged SY instead of SH
〇 (U+3007)KANJI, SYMBOL, KANJINUMERICSYMBOL, KANJINUMERICRuns of numerals can be grouped differently. With ko-dic, 二〇二六年 is one unknown word (SH) instead of 二, 〇, 二六 and 年 (see also Unknown words come from the default category, as in MeCab)

The kanji numerals 一 to 九, 十, 百, 千, 万, 億 and 兆 are also listed on two lines, but keep their categories.

lindera train now reads char.def with the dictionary builder. It used to keep only the first category of each line, skip lines that name a single code point (such as 0x0020 SPACE), and resolve overlaps by start position. The %t feature template now gives the first category of the last line that covers the character, which is MeCab's default type. The bundled training files have neither kind of line, so the models trained from them do not change.

A range line without a category is now an error in lindera build and lindera train, as in MeCab; it would otherwise reset the earlier lines to DEFAULT.

The change is in the dictionary builder. The embedded dictionaries and the dictionaries that the 7.0.0 CLI fetches with lindera download have the new categories; a dictionary directory built or downloaded with v6.2.0 or earlier no longer loads (see Dictionary directories must be rebuilt).

The context is carried across 、 and 。

The segmenter cuts the input into sentences at \n, \t, 。 and 、, and after 32 KiB without any of them, to keep each lattice small. Up to v6, every sentence started from the beginning-of-sentence context (BOS) and ended with the connection to the end of the sentence (EOS), so the word after 、 or 。 was read as if it began a text. MeCab does not cut inside a line. v7.0.0 carries the context across the cuts at 、 and 。 and across the forced cuts: the next sentence starts from the words that end the previous one, and EOS is paid only at a \n, a \t or the end of the input. The sentences up to that point form a segment, and segments stay independent. The best path of a segment, and its cost, are those of one lattice over the whole segment, which is what MeCab gives for a line:

Input (dictionary)v6v7 (as MeCab)
彼は、ああ言った (IPADIC)ああ is an interjection (感動詞)ああ is an adverb (副詞)
だから、こんなに答える (IPADIC)こんな (連体詞) and にこんなに (副詞)
選手が泳ぎ、さらにカヌーで進んだ (UniDic)さらに is a conjunction (接続詞)さらに is an adverb (副詞)
言語としては、Javaのオブジェクト (UniDic)J, a, v and a, each 記号,文字Java (名詞,普通名詞)

On the sentences of UD Japanese GSD that contain 、, the change alters 50 lines with UniDic: 27 come closer to the gold segmentation and part-of-speech tags, 7 move away (sign test p = 0.0008), and 16 are ties. Of 505 paragraphs of Botchan, the number that Lindera segments and tags exactly as MeCab does went from 352 to 438 with IPADIC and from 428 to 503 with UniDic. Text without 、, 。 and forced cuts, such as text cut only at \n and \t, is not affected. Carrying the context costs the 1-best segmentation about 1% more instructions.

The result can still differ from one lattice over the segment:

  • No word spans a cut. A dictionary entry that contains 、 or 。 never matches: MeCab reads UniDic's 一、二塁 as one noun, Lindera as 一, 、 and 二塁. An unknown word is not grouped across a cut, and a word that would span a forced cut is split there.
  • The left-space penalty (ko-dic) does not apply to a word that starts right at a forced cut, even when whitespace precedes the cut.

The N-best results follow the same model. Within a segment, they are exactly the N best paths of one lattice over the segment: unique compares the word boundaries of the whole segment, and the cost threshold is measured from the first result. Across segments, the results are the cheapest combinations of one path per segment (see the next section). The first result is the 1-best segmentation. The costs of a line with 、 or 。 change, the first result's included, because they now include the connections across the cuts and the EOS connection only once.

There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior.

N-best results cover the whole input

The N-best methods (Segmenter::segment_nbest, Tokenizer::tokenize_nbest, their _with_lattice and worker forms, lindera tokenize -N and the bindings' N-best methods) cut the input into sentences as the 1-best segmentation does. Up to v6, they searched each sentence on its own, and the k-th result joined the k-th path of every sentence. From the second result on, that changed every sentence at once, so the results were not the cheapest segmentations of the input and their costs could go down, and a sentence with fewer than k paths was missing from the k-th result. v7.0.0 searches the input segment by segment (see the previous section) and returns the N cheapest combinations of one path per segment, in ascending order of total cost, and every result covers the whole input:

Input (IPADIC, -N 3)v6v7
東京、です3079 東京 、 です; 23850 東 京 、 で す; 24249 東 京 、 で す3357 東京 、 です; 12059 東京 、 です (、 as 名詞,数); 13633 東京 、 で す
。東京13 。 東京; 30433 。 東 京; 13520 東 京 (no 。)852 。 東京; 13569 。 東 京; 13636 。 東 京

Each of these lines is one segment, so its v7 results are the three best paths of one lattice over the line, the ones MeCab returns. The first result is the 1-best segmentation, and the output for input with a single sentence does not change. The cost threshold (cost_threshold, --nbest-cost-threshold) is now measured over the whole input: a result is kept when its total cost is within the threshold of the first result's. v6 applied the threshold to each sentence separately. With unique, the results still have distinct word boundaries.

An empty input now gets one result without tokens, with the connection cost from BOS to EOS, as in MeCab and as an input of only whitespace already did; v6 gave no result, because an empty input has no sentence. This applies to segment_nbest, tokenize_nbest, their worker forms, the bindings' N-best methods and lindera tokenize -N, which now writes a result for an empty line.

Unknown words start at every position, as in MeCab

A word that is not in the dictionary is read as an unknown word, built from the character categories of the dictionary's char.def (katakana, Latin letters, digits, symbols and so on). Most categories are set to group: a run of characters that share a category, such as a run of katakana, becomes one candidate, a grouped unknown word. Up to v6, normal mode created no unknown words at the positions inside the last grouped unknown word, a shortcut inherited from Kuromoji that MeCab does not have. After a dictionary word that ends inside such a run, no unknown word could continue the path, so the grouped unknown word that swallowed the dictionary word was often the only way through. v7.0.0 creates unknown-word candidates at every position that a path reaches, in every mode, under MeCab's condition: the category that creates them is set to always create them (INVOKE in char.def), or no dictionary word starts at that position. Decompose mode already did this, and its output does not change.

Input (dictionary)v6v7 (as MeCab)
それが「⁂⁂第一だ (IPADIC)「⁂⁂, one unknown noun that swallows the dictionary symbol 「「 (記号,括弧開) and ⁂⁂
ジョン・レノンが歌う (IPADIC)ジョン・レノン, one unknown nounジョン, ・ and レノン
ホテル・コルテシアに泊まる (UniDic)ホテル・コルテシア, one unknown nounホテル, ・ and コルテシア
"좋아." (ko-dic)아 (EC) and ." (SY)아 (EF), . (SF) and " (SY)
  • Japanese: IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd and UniDic put ・ in the katakana range of their char.def. After a dictionary word and ・, an unknown katakana word could not start, so ジョン・レノン became one unknown word. Now the unknown word starts after them, as in MeCab. A run that starts with an unknown word, such as レノン・ジョン, stays one unknown word in MeCab; v7.0.0 splits it too, as ・ is a break character by default (see Middle dots break unknown words by default). In the same way, a dictionary symbol is no longer merged into the unknown symbols after it.
  • Korean: a sentence-final .", ?", !" or .' was one symbol (SY). Now ., ? and ! are sentence-final punctuation (SF), as in MeCab, and the ending before them can change with it, as in "좋아.".
  • Chinese: Jieba was not affected with the mecab-jieba-0.1.2 dictionary (not measured with 0.1.3, see Jieba: costs retrained on UD Chinese GSD), and CC-CEDICT keeps Latin words and runs of kana in one word, as in v6. With the costs of the CC-CEDICT dictionary of v6 (CC-CEDICT-MeCab-0.1.0-20200409), the change would split them, as MeCab does with that dictionary: every unknown word costs −3,200 whatever its length, so a path with more words costs less, and T (an entry, −400) followed by the unknown word he (−3,200) beats the unknown word The. The shortcut hid this. v7.0.0 builds CC-CEDICT with new costs (see CC-CEDICT: unknown words no longer cost less than dictionary words).
  • SudachiDict output can change in the same kinds of runs.
  • N-best: the first result changes as the 1-best segmentation does, and the other results can now include splits such as G and oogle for Google (UniDic).

With dictionaries built from the same sources, the number of lines that Lindera segments and tags exactly as MeCab does rises, on top of the other changes in this guide, from 589 to 596 of 600 Japanese sentences and from 438 to 459 of 505 paragraphs of Botchan with IPADIC, from 590 to 596 and from 441 to 459 with IPADIC-NEologd, and from 877 to 1,498 of 1,500 Korean sentences with ko-dic (with the left-space penalty off, as MeCab has none). No line that matched before stops matching, and UniDic is unchanged on these texts. On UD Japanese GSD with UniDic, 64 sentences change: 53 come closer to the gold segmentation and part-of-speech tags, 10 move away (sign test p = 3.4 × 10⁻⁸), and 1 is a tie. The 10 all match MeCab's output; GSD keeps some names joined by ・ and some numbers as one word.

Text with many runs of katakana or Latin letters costs more, because every position inside a run now gets candidates, as in MeCab. Against the same release without this change, counting the speedups made with it, the instruction count rises by 13% on UD Japanese GSD (Wikipedia text; 14% to 17% for N-best), and falls by 0.8% on Botchan and on Korean and by 14% to 16% in Decompose mode. A line of 10,240 katakana without a delimiter costs 3 to 5 times as much in 1-best and 3 to 15 times in N-best, and the peak memory of lindera tokenize -N 3 on it grows from 12 to 56 MiB with IPADIC and from 18 to 127 MiB with UniDic.

There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior. unknown_word_ladder(false) (--disable-unknown-word-ladder) still turns off the shorter unknown-word candidates, but no longer reproduces the output of Lindera before v6.

Middle dots break unknown words by default

The char.def of IPADIC, UniDic, ko-dic, CC-CEDICT and Jieba puts ・ (U+30FB) in the katakana category (SudachiDict's no longer does, see SudachiDict reads Sudachi's own char.def), so a run of katakana joined by ・ is one unknown word when its first word is not in the dictionary, as in MeCab, while a dictionary word before ・ ends there (see Unknown words start at every position, as in MeCab). Whether text was split at ・ thus depended on whether its first word was in the dictionary. v7.0.0 makes ・ a break character by default (#1353): no unknown word crosses a boundary between a break character and another character, in every mode, and in decompose mode no system-dictionary word does either.

Input (IPADIC)MeCab, and v7 with no break charactersv7
レノン・ジョンレノン・ジョン, one unknown wordレノン, ・ and ジョン
ザ・サイレント・フォレストザ・サイレント・フォレスト, one unknown wordザ, ・, サイレント, ・ and フォレスト
リベラル・アーツ・カレッジリベラル, ・ and アーツ・カレッジリベラル, ・, アーツ, ・ and カレッジ
インフォームド・コンセント, in decompose modeOne dictionary wordインフォームド, ・ and コンセント
  • In decompose mode, a system-dictionary word with a boundary inside it does not enter the lattice, and comes out as its parts, without its own part of speech and reading: IPADIC has 658 such entries, IPADIC-NEologd 302,023, SudachiDict 175,744 and UniDic 1,094, mostly emoticons such as Φ（・∀・＊）. Normal mode keeps them, and every mode keeps user-dictionary words and words made of ・ only.
  • ･ (U+FF65) is not a break character by default: every bundled dictionary puts it in the symbol category, so no unknown word runs through it.
  • For MeCab's segmentation, set no break characters: break_characters: "" under segmenter in the configuration, --disable-break-characters for lindera tokenize, Segmenter::break_characters(""), or set_break_characters("") (setBreakCharacters("")) in the bindings. A string sets other break characters.
  • lindera train and Trainer create the unknown-word candidates with the same rule, ・ by default; train with the break characters the dictionary will be used with (--break-characters, --disable-break-characters, Trainer::break_characters).
  • Lattice::unknown_word_candidates takes the break characters as a new argument, before out: pass None for the candidates of before. LatticeOptions has a new field, break_characters, None by default, so the lattice itself keeps MeCab's segmentation unless told otherwise.
  • Segmenting takes up to about 1.3% more instructions (0.5% on Botchan and 1.0% on UD Japanese GSD with IPADIC, measured on macOS), and less in decompose mode on long runs of katakana joined by ・.

Unknown words come from the default category, as in MeCab

A character can have more than one category in char.def: the kanji numerals are KANJINUMERIC KANJI in IPADIC and UniDic, HANJANUMERIC HANJA in ko-dic and CHINESENUMERIC CHINESE in CC-CEDICT and Jieba, and 〇 (U+3007) is SYMBOL plus the numeral category in all of them but Jieba (see Jieba: 〇 is a numeral entry). The first category of the line that decides a character's categories is its default category. Up to v6.2.0, Lindera created unknown-word candidates for every category of a character, and went on with a grouped unknown word only while the next character had the same category at the same position of its category list. v7.0.0 follows MeCab:

  • Unknown words come from the default category only, with its INVOKE, GROUP and LENGTH settings and its unk.def entries.
  • A grouped unknown word goes on while each character shares a category with the one before it.
  • The shorter candidates of the length ladder go on while each character shares a category with the first one.
Input (dictionary)v6v7 (as MeCab)
三國史記 (ko-dic)三 (SH), 國史 (NNG) and 記 (NNG)三國史記 (SH)
十人十色 (ko-dic)十 (SH), 人 (NNG), 十 (SH) and 色 (NNG)十人十色 (SH)
二十歲 (ko-dic)二十 (SH) and 歲 (SH)二十歲 (SH)
〇〇〇 (ko-dic)〇〇〇 (SH)〇〇〇 (SY)
  • Korean: many ko-dic numerals, such as 三 and 十, are not dictionary words, and their default category HANJANUMERIC groups, so a numeral and the hanja after it become one SH word, as in MeCab.
  • 〇: its default category is SYMBOL, which creates unknown words even where a dictionary word starts, so it is a symbol with ko-dic (SY). CC-CEDICT has 〇 as an entry, which beats such a group with the costs of the v7.0.0 dictionary, so 二〇二六年 stays 二, 〇, 二, 六 and 年 (see CC-CEDICT: unknown words no longer cost less than dictionary words). With Jieba, whose group ran on through the numerals and the Chinese characters after them, 〇 is now a numeral entry (see Jieba: 〇 is a numeral entry).
  • Japanese: IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd and UniDic have the kanji numerals and 〇 as dictionary words, and no line of the texts compared changes. SudachiDict was not compared.

With dictionaries built from the same sources, the number of lines that Lindera segments and tags exactly as MeCab does rises, on top of the other changes in this guide, from 3,913 to 3,917 of the 3,919 non-empty lines of Sangnoksu with ko-dic (with the left-space penalty off, as MeCab has none); every generated sentence that combines the characters with several categories with other characters now matches MeCab with IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd, UniDic, ko-dic, CC-CEDICT and Jieba. No line that matched before stops matching. The instruction count falls by 0.3% to 4.8%.

CharacterDefinition::lookup_categories (in lindera_dictionary::dictionary::character_definition) returns the default category first, then the other categories in category id order. The 7.0.0 char_def.bin stores them in this order, which is why the dictionary format version changes (see Dictionary directories must be rebuilt).

There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior.

SudachiDict reads Sudachi's own char.def

SudachiDict used to be built with UniDic 2.1.2's char.def, as SudachiDict ships none. v7.0.0 builds it with Sudachi's own char.def (sudachi.rs v0.7.0) and reads it as Sudachi does (#1388), which its metadata.json selects with "char_def_format": "sudachi":

  • A code point gets the categories of every line that covers it, ALL stands for every category, and the flags NOOOVBOW and NOOOVEOW keep unknown words from starting at a character and right after it: small katakana, ー, ヽ, ヾ, 々, combining marks, variation selectors, skin tone modifiers, ZWNJ and ZWJ.
  • Unknown words come from every category of a character, over runs cut as Sudachi cuts them, and a position where nothing else starts gets a one-character unknown word of DEFAULT, as in Sudachi.
  • The file maps × and ÷ to SYMBOL, CR to SPACE and U+9FA6..U+9FFF to KANJI, and leaves ・ out of the katakana category.
Input (SudachiDict)v7.0.0 before #1388v7.0.0 and Sudachi
時々｜図抜けた時 / 々｜ / 図抜け / た時々 / ｜ / 図抜け / た
résumé (with combining accents)re / ́ / su / me / ́résumé
ァィゥェォを並べるァィゥェォ / を / 並べるァ / ィ / ゥ / ェ / ォ / を / 並べる

On Botchan (resources/bocchan.txt), 5 of its 505 lines change, all of them at 々 before ｜, and Lindera now gives the same tokens as sudachi.rs v0.7.0 (with its input-text and path-rewrite plugins disabled) on 502 of the lines, up from 497. Of the other three, one is the URL of the next section, and SudachiDict (Custom Build) explains the last two. To build SudachiDict yourself, use Sudachi's char.def with "char_def_format": "sudachi"; MeCab's format, the default, stops at the first NOOOVBOW of the file.

SudachiDict decodes the escapes of its lexicons

SudachiDict's lexicons write (, ), /, ,, | and " as escapes: a backslash, u and four hex digits. The word http:// is written http:\u002f\u002f, and 1,2塁 is written 1\u002c2塁. Sudachi's dictionary builder decodes them, and Lindera's builder did not, so 3,723 entries of the 2026-07-23 lexicons kept their escapes and never matched text. v7.0.0 decodes them in every field, as Sudachi does (#1389), which SudachiDict's metadata.json selects with "lexicon_format": "sudachi". The tokens below are in code spans, and ␣ is a space:

Input (SudachiDict)v7.0.0 before #1389v7.0.0 and Sudachi
http://lindera.devhttp :// lindera . devhttp:// lindera . dev
1,2塁1 , 2塁1,2塁
b/sb / sb/s
co.,ltd.co ., ltd .co.,ltd.
\( ^o^ )/\( ␣ ^o^ ␣ )/\( ^o^ )/

The details are decoded too: the display surface of 1,2塁 is 1,2塁, and its normalized form 一二塁. So are the rows of a user dictionary built for SudachiDict, as in Sudachi's user dictionaries. The mecab output of lindera tokenize joins the details with commas and does not quote them, so a detail with a comma, such as that display surface, is ambiguous there, as some details of CC-CEDICT and Jieba already are; the JSON output is not.

On Botchan, 1 of its 505 lines changes, the one with a URL, and Lindera now gives the same tokens as sudachi.rs v0.7.0 (with its input-text and path-rewrite plugins disabled) on 503 of the lines, up from 502. To build SudachiDict yourself, set "lexicon_format": "sudachi"; without it, the words with escapes keep them.

CC-CEDICT: unknown words no longer cost less than dictionary words

v7.0.0 builds the CC-CEDICT dictionary from CC-CEDICT-MeCab-0.1.0-20261021 instead of CC-CEDICT-MeCab-0.1.0-20200409 (#1128). The CC-CEDICT data (2020-04-09), char.def and the other entries are the same, and two kinds of cost change:

  • Every unknown word costs 400 instead of −3,200.
  • The 20 entries made only of Latin letters (such as T, PK, TA, cos and Tony) and the 2 made only of digits (88 and 996) cost 399, one less than an unknown word, instead of −400 to −3,200.

CC-CEDICT has no connection costs, so a path costs the sum of the costs of its words, and with the old costs a path with more unknown words cost less. Unknown words start at every position would then split Latin words and runs of kana: T (−400) and the unknown word he (−3,200) beat the unknown word The (−3,200). With the new costs, more unknown words cost more, and an entry made only of Latin letters or of digits wins only for exactly its own characters (399 against 400), never as the start of a longer run (399 + 400 against 400). Latin words, runs of kana and numbers stay one word, as in v6, and MeCab segments them the same way with the new dictionary.

What changes from v6 is that dictionary words now beat the unknown words that cover the same characters:

Inputv6v7
他穿着一件T恤。T and 恤T恤
我们去卡拉OK唱歌。卡拉 and OK卡拉OK
请把文件存到U盘里。U and 盘U盘
二〇〇八年北京奧運會二, 〇〇 (unknown), 八, 年, 北京 and 奧運會二, 〇, 〇, 八, 年, 北京 and 奧運會
两个队PK了一场。PK, an unknown wordPK, the entry (P K, "(slang) to take on/to challenge/…")
  • An entry that mixes Latin letters or digits with Chinese characters, such as T恤, B超, AA制, 卡拉OK, 阿Q, 3C, U盘 or X光, used to lose to unknown words over its Latin letters or digits.
  • 〇 and the entries made only of Latin letters or of digits come with their pinyin and definition, where an unknown word over the same characters used to win.

Against v7.0.0 with the 0.1.0-20200409 dictionary, 167 of the 4,997 sentences of UD Chinese GSD change: 163 come closer to the gold segmentation and 4 move away (sign test p = 3.4 × 10⁻⁴³). The 4 are CC-CEDICT words that GSD writes as two words (X光, T恤 and K書) or splits at · (喬治·華盛頓). The simplified UD Chinese GSDSimp gives the same counts. Lindera and MeCab agree on the same 4,951 GSD sentences with either dictionary (the other 46 differ where Lindera cuts the sentence after 。 or 、), and on every one of 8,064 generated sentences around the characters with several categories with the new one. The instruction count on GSD falls by 0.1%.

The costs of paths change with the costs of unknown words, so N-best costs and the cost threshold of N-best results are on a different scale. Entries of a user dictionary keep their own costs (−10,000 for the simple format, the default_word_cost of the metadata), so they still cost less than an unknown word.

A CC-CEDICT dictionary directory built from the 0.1.0-20200409 archive keeps the old costs (and has to be rebuilt anyway, see Dictionary directories must be rebuilt): build it from the 0.1.0-20261021 archive, as lindera-cc-cedict and the 7.0.0 release assets do. There is no setting to restore the old costs.

Jieba: 〇 is a numeral entry

v7.0.0 builds the Jieba dictionary from mecab-jieba-0.1.3 instead of mecab-jieba-0.1.1. Since 0.1.2 (#1162), it reads 〇 (U+3007 IDEOGRAPHIC NUMBER ZERO) as a numeral, like 一 to 兆; 0.1.3 trains the costs again (see Jieba: costs retrained on UD Chinese GSD):

  • In char.def, 〇 is CHINESENUMERIC CHINESE, the categories of the other numerals, instead of SYMBOL CHINESENUMERIC.
  • 〇 is an entry like 零: part of speech m, pinyin ling2 and definition zero.

With the 0.1.1 dictionary, 〇 was an unknown word. Since unknown words come from the default category, its SYMBOL group went on through the numerals, which are CHINESE too, and the Chinese characters after them, as in MeCab: 二〇〇八年北京奧運會 was 二 and 〇〇八年北京奧運會 (w). An entry alone would not stop the group: SYMBOL makes unknown words even where an entry starts, and with the connection costs of 0.1.1 one unknown word over 〇〇八年北京奧運會 costs less than the path through 北京奧運 and 會, because entering or leaving their context ID costs 32,767. With the numeral categories, which make no unknown word where an entry starts, and the entry, no unknown word starts at 〇:

Inputv6v7
二〇〇八年北京奧運會二, 〇〇 (unknown), 八, 年, 北京奧運 and 會二, 〇, 〇, 八, 年, 北京, 奧運 and 會
编号〇〇七的特工编号, 〇〇 (unknown), 七, 的 and 特工编号, 〇, 〇, 七, 的 and 特工
第二〇章第二 and 〇章 (unknown)第二, 〇 and 章

With 0.1.2, only text with 〇 changed: none of the 4,997 sentences of UD Chinese GSD has 〇. Lindera and MeCab segment the same way with the 0.1.3 dictionary: 28 hand-written lines, 2,160 generated lines around the numerals and 〇, the 8,064 generated sentences around the characters with several categories, and 4,951 of the 4,997 GSD sentences, as many as with the older dictionaries. As with the other numerals, a character that starts no entry and the 〇 after it can make one unknown word, as in MeCab: 両〇頻 is 両〇 and 頻.

A Jieba dictionary directory built from the 0.1.1 archive keeps 〇 as a symbol (and has to be rebuilt anyway, see Dictionary directories must be rebuilt): build it from the 0.1.3 archive, as lindera-jieba and the 7.0.0 release assets do.

Jieba: costs retrained on UD Chinese GSD

v7.0.0 builds the Jieba dictionary from mecab-jieba-0.1.3, whose word and connection costs are trained again (#1250). Up to 0.1.2, every connection into or out of context ID 2, which 52 of the 55 parts of speech shared (362,085 of the 584,430 entries, such as every v, nr and ns), cost 32,767. Three defects added up: the training corpus never made a gold word a dictionary word, the trainer of lindera 2.3.3 put no dictionary words in its lattices, and its export wrote 32,767 for a connection without a trained weight. The best path was the one with the fewest such connections, close to longest match, and the word costs had never been trained against each other. 0.1.3 is trained with the trainer of v7.0.0 on the training splits of UD Chinese GSD and of the same sentences in simplified script (GSDSimp), with each gold word that is in the dictionary given the features of a dictionary entry. Every part of speech has its own context ID (a 56 × 56 matrix), and no connection costs 32,767.

Jieba now segments text as UD Chinese GSD does, which is finer than jieba and than 0.1.2. Both columns are v7.0.0; MeCab segments every line the same way with the same dictionary:

Input0.1.20.1.3 (as MeCab)
北京是中华人民共和国的首都。北京 / 是 / 中华人民共和国 / 的 / 首都 / 。北京 / 是 / 中华 / 人民 / 共和 / 国 / 的 / 首都 / 。
可以进行中文形态学分析。可以 / 进行 / 中文 / 形态 / 学分 / 析 / 。可以 / 进行 / 中文 / 形态 / 学 / 分析 / 。
这个问题很重要。这个 / 问题 / 很重 / 要 / 。这 / 个 / 问题 / 很 / 重要 / 。
武汉市解除离汉离鄂通道管控措施武汉市 / 解除 / 离 / 汉 / 离 / 鄂 / 通道 / 管控 / 措施武汉 / 市 / 解除 / 离 / 汉 / 离 / 鄂 / 通道 / 管控 / 措施

GSD's gold segmentation has 中華 / 人民 / 共和 / 國 (54 times) and 這 / 個 (69 times, never 這個). Segmentation F1 over word spans, with models trained on the training splits only:

DictionaryGSD devGSD testGSDSimp devGSDSimp test
0.1.277.0977.3177.0777.70
0.1.388.8487.7189.5988.75

MeCab 0.996 with the same dictionaries gives the same F1 within 0.09, and segments 4,951 of the 4,997 GSD sentences as Lindera does, with either dictionary. The parts of speech are jieba's, as before.

A simple user dictionary row (a surface, a part of speech and a pinyin) costs the default_word_cost of metadata.json. The trained word costs go down to −25,149, so lindera-jieba sets it to −32768 instead of 1625: with 1625, or with the −10000 of the other dictionaries, the user word 羽田机场 lost to 羽田 and 机场. Of user words made of two adjacent GSD words that are not in the dictionary, one per sentence of the test splits, −32768 keeps 99.4% as one word, −10000 53% to 58% and 1625 4%. A detailed row gives its own context IDs and cost: the IDs of 0.1.2 (0 to 6) name other parts of speech in 0.1.3, so take them from the left-id.def and right-id.def of the 0.1.3 archive.

A Jieba dictionary directory built from an older archive has to be rebuilt from mecab-jieba-0.1.3, as lindera-jieba and the 7.0.0 release assets are. There is no setting to restore the old costs.

Dash and tilde spellings are kept as written

Japanese text spells the dash and the tilde in two ways each: the dash as ― (U+2015, HORIZONTAL BAR) or — (U+2014, EM DASH), the tilde as ～ (U+FF5E, FULLWIDTH TILDE) or 〜 (U+301C, WAVE DASH). Up to v6.2.0, the dictionary builder rewrote ― to — and ～ to 〜 in every entry of IPADIC and IPADIC-NEologd, whose metadata.json turned the rewrite on with normalize_details. It rewrote the surface, the spelling under which the segmenter finds the entry in the text, and the detail fields, such as the base form and the reading. The text to segment was not rewritten, so an entry that the dictionary source spells with ― or ～ matched only text that spelled it with — or 〜. The rewrite was a workaround for an old EUC-JP conversion. The dictionary sources are UTF-8 now, and ― is the dash that the common Shift_JIS and EUC-JP converters produce and that Aozora Bunko texts use. v7.0.0 keeps every entry as written in the dictionary's CSV files, as MeCab does:

Input (dictionary)v6v7 (as MeCab)
ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ (IPADIC)ＣＤ, ― and ＲＯＭＣＤ―ＲＯＭ (名詞,一般)
―― (IPADIC)An unknown noun (名詞,サ変接続)記号,一般
あいいれなぁ～い (IPADIC-NEologd)あいいれなぁ, ～ and いあいいれなぁ～い (形容詞,自立)
CD―ROM (IPADIC-NEologd)CD, ― and ROMCD―ROM (名詞,一般)
ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ (IPADIC)ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ (名詞,一般)ＣＤ, — and ＲＯＭ
—— (IPADIC)記号,一般An unknown noun (名詞,サ変接続)

The detail fields keep the CSV spelling as well: the entry ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ gives the base form ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ, where v6 gave ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ.

With dictionaries built from the same sources, the number of lines that Lindera segments and tags exactly as MeCab does rises, on top of the other changes in this guide, from 459 to 503 of 505 paragraphs of Botchan (from 2,690 to 2,744 of its 2,746 sentences) and from 3,377 to 3,581 of 3,587 paragraphs of Kokoro and I Am a Cat, two other novels from Aozora Bunko. The figures are the same with IPADIC and IPADIC-NEologd, and no line that matched before stops matching.

Text that writes these characters as — or 〜 no longer finds the entries that it found only through the rewrite: 12 in IPADIC, all spelled with ―, and 1,085 in IPADIC-NEologd, most of them spelled with ～. In the table above, ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ is split and —— is an unknown noun, as in MeCab. IPADIC-NEologd has most of its words with a tilde in both spellings, so text with either tilde still finds them.

To have both spellings find the entries, map the text to the dictionary's spelling with the mapping character filter. IPADIC spells all its entries with a dash with ― and all those with a tilde with 〜, so map — to ― and ～ to 〜:

lindera tokenize --dict embedded://ipadic --char-filter 'mapping:{"mapping":{"—":"―","～":"〜"}}'

# Configuration file
character_filters:
  - kind: mapping
    args:
      mapping:
        "—": "―"
        "～": "〜"

With this filter, ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ is one word and —— is 記号,一般 again, and text with ～ also finds IPADIC's entries with 〜, which it did not in v6 either. The token's surface is the mapped text, such as ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ; its byte offsets point into the original text. Mapping the tilde the other way, 〜 to ～, would hide IPADIC's entries with 〜. With IPADIC-NEologd, a mapping trades words: some of its words exist in only one spelling, 129 only with ― and 85 only with —, 957 only with ～ and 1,813 only with 〜, so mapping one spelling to the other makes text find the words of one and miss those of the other. NFKC normalization (the unicode_normalize character filter) does not fold these characters: it turns ～ into ~ and leaves ―, — and 〜 as they are.

User dictionaries were never rewritten and do not change. The change is in the dictionary builder. The embedded dictionaries and the dictionaries that the 7.0.0 CLI fetches with lindera download keep the spellings; a dictionary directory built or downloaded with v6.2.0 or earlier no longer loads (see Dictionary directories must be rebuilt). UniDic, ko-dic, CC-CEDICT, Jieba and SudachiDict never turned the rewrite on.

The normalize_details setting is removed

normalize_details turned this rewrite on and did nothing else, so v7.0.0 removes it from the bundled metadata.json files and from the APIs that create or expose dictionary metadata:

APIChange
RustMetadata::new takes 10 arguments instead of 11 (normalize_details was the ninth), and the Metadata::normalize_details field and the PrefixDictionaryBuilderOptions::normalize_details method are gone. For binding authors, lindera_binding::CoreMetadata and CoreMetadata::new change the same way. See Rust API changes in lindera_dictionary
PythonThe normalize_details keyword argument of Metadata, the property and the to_dict() key are gone; passing the keyword raises TypeError
RubyMetadata.new takes 8 positional arguments instead of 9, so passing 9 raises ArgumentError; the normalize_details reader and the to_h key are gone
PHPThe last argument of the Metadata constructor, normalize_details, the property and the toArray() key are gone; passing the argument raises Error (by name) or ArgumentCountError (as a ninth argument)
Node.jsThe normalizeDetails option of Metadata, the property and the toObject() key are gone; TypeScript rejects the option, and at run time it is ignored
WASMNo change: its Metadata never exposed the setting

A metadata.json that still contains normalize_details, such as one written by v6, loads as before, whether it comes with a built dictionary, is passed to lindera build or is read by a binding; the key is ignored and is not written back.

Tied entries resolve to the first CSV row, as in MeCab

A dictionary can have several entries with the same surface, the same left and right context IDs and the same cost, which differ only in their details, such as the reading or the base form. Such entries are tied: a path costs the same with any of them, so the order in which the segmenter considers them decides which one it outputs. Up to v6.2.0, Lindera added the dictionary entries that start at a position in reverse order, and the search keeps the earlier of two candidates with equal cost, so the last CSV row of a tied group won. The reverse order came in with v2.1.0, apparently by accident. v7.0.0 outputs the first row, as MeCab does:

Input (dictionary)v6v7 (as MeCab)
あいつは狡い (IPADIC)狡い reads コスイ狡い reads ズルイ

IPADIC's Adj.csv has the two rows in this order:

狡い,19,19,4682,形容詞,自立,*,*,形容詞・アウオ段,基本形,狡い,ズルイ,ズルイ
狡い,19,19,4682,形容詞,自立,*,*,形容詞・アウオ段,基本形,狡い,コスイ,コスイ

Tied entries exist for 5,637 surfaces in IPADIC, 90,991 in IPADIC-NEologd, 3,324 in UniDic and 175 in ko-dic. In the Japanese dictionaries, the rows of a tied group never differ in the part of speech, only in fields such as the reading and the base form; in ko-dic, 5 groups also differ in the part of speech. With each tied surface on its own line, the number of surfaces whose full details equal those of MeCab 0.996 rises from 1,607 to 5,637 of 5,637 with IPADIC, from 524 to 3,324 of 3,324 with UniDic, and from 8,205 to 86,319 of 86,464 with IPADIC-NEologd (surfaces with whitespace or control characters left out). The other 145 IPADIC-NEologd surfaces contain 、, which no word spans (see The context is carried across 、 and 。), or belong to groups whose rows MeCab reads in another order (see below). With ko-dic, all 175 agree when MeCab's dictionary is built from the CSV files in name order.

On running text, the number of lines whose full details equal MeCab's rises, on top of the other changes in this guide, from 7,989 to 8,096 of the 8,100 sentences of UD Japanese GSD and from 3,278 to 3,583 of the 3,587 paragraphs of Kokoro and I Am a Cat with IPADIC, and from 3,394 to 3,571 of the same 3,587 paragraphs with UniDic. No line is segmented differently. In all the texts compared, 15 tokens change their part of speech, all to MeCab's. Most of them are entries of the same surface with different context IDs and costs whose paths happen to cost the same in that sentence, and the same order decides between them: UniDic, for example, now reads 御前 as a pronoun (代名詞) instead of a common noun (名詞,普通名詞,一般), as MeCab does.

User dictionaries follow the same rule: among tied user entries, the first row is now chosen instead of the last. A user entry that ties with a system entry is still chosen over it, as in v6. This is the one intended difference from MeCab, which chooses the system entry. Such a tie needs a user entry in the detailed format that copies the context IDs and the cost of a system entry, for example to give a word another reading. An entry in the simple three-column format gets the cost and the context IDs of the dictionary's metadata.json (default_word_cost, default_left_context_id and default_right_context_id: -10000, 0 and 0 for IPADIC), so it practically never ties with a system entry.

N-best search uses the same order. In addition, the first N-best result is now always the 1-best segmentation, the output of segment; up to v6 it could be another path when several paths had exactly the same cost. The costs of the N-best results do not change: only results with the same cost can change places, which can also change which of them is cut off at the n-th result. N-best search takes about 3% to 4% more instructions (-N 3); the speed of the 1-best segmentation does not change (within 0.2%).

With unique (--nbest-unique), every result is the cheapest path of its word boundaries, and of tied entries it now holds the first CSV row in every result, as the 1-best segmentation does. Up to v6, unique N-best went through the paths in order of cost and kept the first path of each segmentation, which could hold either row of a tied pair, and it went through every path of a segmentation before it reached the next one: a short line whose words have many entries could take tens of seconds and gigabytes. The search now goes over word boundaries, so it does not depend on the number of paths. Again, only results with the same cost can change.

MeCab's mecab-dict-index reads the CSV files in the order the file system lists them (readdir order), so for tied groups whose rows are in different files (in IPADIC-NEologd and ko-dic), MeCab's choice depends on the file system, while Lindera reads the files in name order.

The change is in the segmenter, not in the dictionary files. There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior.

Equal-cost segmentations keep the later-starting word, as in MeCab

Two segmentations can reach the same position with exactly the same cost while their last words start at different positions. MeCab keeps the one whose last word starts later: it puts every word at the head of the list of words that end where it ends, so the words that start later come first in that list, and of words of equal cost it keeps the first. Up to v6.2.0, Lindera kept the one whose last word starts earlier. v7.0.0 chooses as MeCab does:

Input (dictionary)v6v7 (as MeCab)
腸窒扶斯 (IPADIC)腸 / 窒 / 扶斯腸 / 窒扶 / 斯
にフリーホイールダイオードや (IPADIC)フリーホイールダイオード (one unknown word)フリー / ホイール / ダイオード
家系譜 (UniDic)家 / 系譜家系 / 譜
차나 마셔 (ko-dic)차나 / 마셔차 / 나 / 마셔
電視台上班 (CC-CEDICT)電視 / 台 / 上班電視 / 台上 / 班
二十二年 (Jieba)二 / 十二 / 年二十 / 二 / 年

Both segmentations of 腸窒扶斯 cost 28,382. With the Japanese and Korean dictionaries, such ties are rare. The texts compared are Botchan (as one file, as paragraphs and as sentences), the 3,587 paragraphs of Kokoro and I Am a Cat and the 8,100 sentences of UD Japanese GSD, each with IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd and UniDic, and the 7,759 lines of Sangnoksu with ko-dic: about 54,000 lines in all. 9 of them change, all to MeCab's segmentation, and none moves away from it. In Decompose mode, which MeCab does not have, 0 to 2 lines per text change in the same way.

With CC-CEDICT, ties are common, because its costs take few values. CC-CEDICT has no connection costs, and an entry of len characters costs max(-36000, -400 * len ** 1.5) (except the 22 entries made only of Latin letters or only of digits, see CC-CEDICT: unknown words no longer cost less than dictionary words), so two segmentations into entries of the same lengths cost the same, such as 電視 / 台 / 上班 and 電視 / 台上 / 班. Jieba's costs are trained (see Jieba: costs retrained on UD Chinese GSD), so ties are rare with it; with the mecab-jieba-0.1.2 dictionary, whose 584,430 entries had 12 distinct costs and 4 context IDs, 1,186 sentences changed. Compared with v7.0.0 changed to keep the earlier-starting word on ties, about a quarter of the 4,997 sentences of UD Chinese GSD change with CC-CEDICT:

DictionarySentences that changeCloser to / farther from the gold segmentationSentences segmented as MeCab, before → after
CC-CEDICT1,267634 / 455 (sign test p = 6.5 × 10⁻⁸)3,694 → 4,951
Jieba31 / 14,948 → 4,951

The other sentences that change come neither closer to the gold segmentation nor farther from it, and segmentation F1 rises from 77.94 to 78.30 with CC-CEDICT and stays 88.79 with Jieba. Every sentence that changes costs the same either way.

When whitespace is skipped (see Whitespace is skipped in the lattice), the word that ends later wins first, as in MeCab, which looks the next word up from every position a word ends at: an entry that ends with the space wins over a word that ends before it. One difference from MeCab remains in theory: after skipped whitespace, MeCab keeps a node for every position the previous word can end at, while Lindera keeps one, so two words that start right after the same whitespace and tie through previous words that end at different positions can be chosen differently. This needs an entry that ends with whitespace and an exact tie, and it does not occur in the texts compared.

Among words that start at the same position, the order of Tied entries resolve to the first CSV row, as in MeCab still applies, and the first N-best result is still the 1-best segmentation. When the context is carried across 、 or 。, a tie between the words that end the previous sentence resolves the same way, as in one lattice over the line: the word that starts later wins (see The context is carried across 、 and 。).

The 1-best segmentation takes 0.6% to 0.9% more instructions with IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd and UniDic, with no measurable change in time, and about 2% more instructions and 2% to 5% more time with ko-dic. N-best search (-N 3) takes about 1% more instructions.

The change is in the segmenter, not in the dictionary files. There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior.

lindera tokenize removes only the line terminator and writes every line

lindera tokenize reads its input line by line. Up to v6.2.0, it removed all the whitespace at both ends of each line before tokenizing it: spaces, tabs, U+3000, U+00A0 and the other Unicode whitespace (str::trim). The library, the language bindings and MeCab do not. v7.0.0 removes only the line terminator (\n, or \r\n) and tokenizes the rest of the line as the library does:

Input line (IPADIC)v6v7 (as MeCab)
Two spaces, 東京, a space東京 at bytes 0-6東京 at bytes 2-8
U+3000, 東京東京 at 0-6U+3000 (記号,空白) at 0-3, 東京 at 3-9
東京, U+3000東京 at 0-6東京 at 0-6, U+3000 (記号,空白) at 6-9
U+00A0, 東京, U+00A0東京 at 0-6U+00A0 (unknown, 記号,一般) at 0-2, 東京 at 2-8, U+00A0 at 8-10
  • Spaces and tabs are SPACE characters, which the segmenter skips and drops from the output, so they still give no tokens; only the byte offsets of the tokens after them change, and now index the input line, as the library's offsets do.
  • U+3000 at the start or end of a line is a token, as in the middle of a line, with IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd (記号,空白) and UniDic (空白) (see Dictionary entries with whitespace are kept). In the 538 lines of Botchan as one file, where 202 lines start with an indent of U+3000, 206 such tokens appear and no other token changes. Text without whitespace at the ends of its lines, such as the 8,100 sentences of UD Japanese GSD and the 3,587 paragraphs of Kokoro and I Am a Cat, gives the same output as before.
  • With --keep-whitespace, the spaces at the start and end of a line are tokens too: two spaces, 東京 and a space give three tokens.
  • With -N, a line of spaces or tabs and an empty line give one result without tokens (NBEST 1 and EOS), as in MeCab, instead of no result (see N-best results cover the whole input for the empty input). The costs of a line with U+3000 at an end include that token.
  • The wakati format writes a line for every input line, or for every result with -N: a line without tokens, such as an empty line or a line of spaces, gives an empty line, as in MeCab. v6 wrote nothing for it, so the output had fewer lines than the input (Botchan as one file: 505 output lines for its 538 input lines, 33 of them empty).
  • The \r of a line that ends with \r\n is removed, and only that one \r. MeCab removes only the \n and outputs the \r as an unknown word; Lindera removes it so that text with Windows line endings does not end every line with a \r token.

The library and the language bindings never trimmed their input, so they do not change, except for the N-best result of an empty input. The change is in the CLI, not in the dictionary files. No option restores the v6 behavior; to get the v6 offsets and tokens, remove the whitespace at the ends of each line before passing the text to lindera tokenize.

lindera tokenize --output json writes the dictionary's fields as strings

Up to v6.2.0, the JSON output of lindera tokenize, which Token::as_value builds, wrote each field of the dictionary's schema as an integer when its text read as one, as a floating-point number when it read as one, and as a string otherwise. A field could be a number in one token and a string in the next, and some texts did not come back as they are in the dictionary. v7.0.0 writes every field of the schema as a string, with the dictionary's text, as the mecab output and the bindings' details do. byte_start, byte_end and word_id are still numbers (#1365).

A user dictionary entry for IPADIC whose fields hold these texts:

Text in the dictionaryv6v7
0077"007"
NaN, infnull"NaN", "inf"
1e31000.0"1e3"
-1, 0.5-1, 0.5"-1", "0.5"
97260136050285239726013605028523, which JavaScript's JSON.parse reads as 9726013605028524"9726013605028523"

The fields this changes in the official dictionaries are those whose text is a number in some entries:

  • UniDic CWJ and UniDic CSJ: lexicon_id, lemma_id and accent_type. lexicon_id goes beyond 2^53: with the v6 conversion, 2,023 of the values that UniDic CWJ gives over Botchan came back as other values when read as doubles. The fields that change in the first token of 見せた with UniDic CWJ, which the v6 conversion wrote as 2, 36480 and 10027554702500481 (read by JSON.parse as 10027554702500480):

    [
  {
    ...
    "accent_type": "2",
    ...
    "lemma_id": "36480",
    ...
    "lexicon_id": "10027554702500481",
    ...
    "surface": "見せ",
    "word_id": 880831,
    ...
  },
  ...
]

  • SudachiDict: dictionary_form_id and synonym_group_ids, which lost its leading zeros (001453 was written as 1453).

  • UniDic, UniDic CWJ, UniDic CSJ and SudachiDict: the surface forms of words written in digits, such as 1.

  • Jieba: char_count, which is 4+ for longer words.

In the other official dictionaries, a field changes only in an entry whose text there is a number, such as a word written in digits; over Botchan, IPADIC and IPADIC-NEologd gave the same output as before. Read the fields of the schema as strings, and convert those you need as numbers; a reader that compared a field with a number now compares it with a string.

WASM: the builder settings apply whichever way the dictionary is set

Up to v6.2.0, TokenizerBuilder.build() in the WASM binding ignored part of the builder's configuration, depending on how the dictionary was set:

Dictionary set withIgnored up to v6.2.0
setDictionaryInstance(), such as a dictionary loaded from OPFS with loadDictionaryFromBytes()setKeepWhitespace(), appendCharacterFilter() and appendTokenFilter()
setDictionary(), such as an embedded:// dictionaryThe user dictionary set with setUserDictionaryInstance()

v7.0.0 applies every setting and the user dictionary either way, as the Tokenizer API page describes. For example, with IPADIC loaded from bytes, setKeepWhitespace(true) and the unicode_normalize (NFKC) and lowercase filters turn Ｌｉｎｄｅｒａ 東京 into lindera, a space and 東京; v6 gave Ｌｉｎｄｅｒａ and 東京.

With a dictionary instance, build() now also checks what it checks for a dictionary set by URI: unless whitespace is kept, the dictionary's char.def must define the SPACE category. Every bundled dictionary does; a custom dictionary without it now needs setKeepWhitespace(true).

The other bindings, the CLI and the library do not change, and neither do the dictionary files. No option restores the v6 behavior; to get it, leave out the settings that v6 ignored.

PHP: optional arguments reject a value of the wrong type

Up to v6.2.0, the PHP binding read a value of the wrong type for an optional parameter as null, so the call silently used the default, with or without strict_types. For example, $tokenizer->tokenizeNbest('東京都', 2, 'yes') returned results that were not deduplicated, and Lindera\Trainer::train(..., max_iter: $argv[1]) trained for the default 100 iterations whatever the command line said. A required parameter already rejected such a value.

v7.0.0 rejects it for the optional parameters too: those of the Penalty, Metadata, FieldDefinition and Tokenizer constructors, of Mode::decompose(), Tokenizer::tokenizeNbest(), Trainer::train(), Trainer::export() and Dictionary::buildUser(). The call throws a TypeError, Invalid value given for argument followed by the parameter's name. A required parameter now throws the same TypeError for such a value; v6 threw an Exception with the same message. null and leaving the argument out still select the default. $lambda of Trainer::train() now takes an int as well as a float, as a PHP float parameter does; v6 read an int there as null too.

Pass each argument its declared type, and cast values that arrive as strings, such as (int) $argv[1] (see Argument types). Code that catches such a value with catch (Exception $e) must catch TypeError instead: a TypeError is an Error, not an Exception. The parameters declared mixed, the other bindings, the CLI and the library do not change. No option restores the v6 behavior.

Bindings: integer arguments outside their range are rejected

Up to v6.2.0, the PHP, Node.js and WASM bindings converted an integer argument to the type of its setting by wrapping, so a value outside the range silently became another value. The PHP binding took every int as a 64-bit integer and cast it to the narrower type. In Node.js and WASM, the conversion from a JS number to a 32-bit integer (ECMAScript's ToUint32 or ToInt32) wrapped it before the binding saw it, and a WASM BigInt was taken modulo 2^64.

Callv6.2.0v7.0.0
PHP new Lindera\Metadata(default_word_cost: 100000)cost -31072ValueError
Node.js new Metadata({ defaultLeftContextId: 2 ** 32 + 5 })context ID 5Error with the code InvalidArg
Node.js schema.getFieldName(2 ** 32)"surface", the first fieldnull
WASM new Penalty(-1)threshold 4294967295a thrown string
tokenizeNbest('東京', -1) in PHP, Node.js and WASMall 33 segmentationsthe binding's error

v7.0.0 rejects such a value. The PHP binding throws a ValueError, the Node.js binding an Error with the code InvalidArg, and the WASM binding a string, as for its other errors. The message names the parameter and the range, such as default_word_cost must be an integer between -32768 and 32767, got 100000. The parameters are the integer settings of Metadata (the default word cost and context IDs) and Penalty, the index of FieldDefinition, getFieldName and PHP's Token::getDetail, the number of N-best results and, in Node.js and WASM, the N-best cost threshold, and the iteration and thread counts of the training functions. The checks apply to the constructors and to the property setters (Node.js Metadata, WASM Penalty and FieldDefinition).

With them, some values that v6 accepted now throw:

  • A negative index, for which v6 returned null (PHP, Node.js) or undefined (WASM). An index past the end still returns null or undefined.
  • In Node.js and WASM, a number that is not an integer, such as 1.5, NaN or Infinity, which v6 truncated or turned into 0.
  • In WASM, a BigInt cost threshold outside the 64-bit range, and a cost threshold that is not a BigInt.
  • An iteration or thread count of 0 for the training functions, which v6 passed to the trainer: training then failed only after the corpus was read and every lattice was built. The counts take 1 or more, and the Python and Ruby bindings reject 0 too, with a ValueError and a RangeError (#1275).

Pass an integer in the range. The TypeScript declarations of the Node.js and WASM bindings do not change. The Python and Ruby bindings already rejected these values, with OverflowError and RangeError, and still do. The RangeError of the Ruby binding now has the message above, which names the parameter and the range, where v6 named only the Rust type (fixnum too big to convert into `i16` ); this covers the N-best cost threshold too, for an Integer outside the 64-bit range. The OverflowError of a Python property setter now names the property in its note (while processing 'default_word_cost' instead of 'cost'). No option restores the v6 behavior.

Bindings: a mode is a Mode

Up to v6.2.0, every binding exported a Mode, but no function or constructor took one: set_mode / setMode and the Tokenizer constructors took a mode name, and decompose mode always used the default penalty. Node.js exported a string enum JsMode, whose values 'Normal' and 'Decompose' setMode rejected, and WASM a numeric enum. A custom penalty reached the segmenter only through a configuration file loaded with from_file / fromFile. In Rust, TokenizerBuilder::set_segmenter_mode lost the penalty of a Mode::Decompose the same way, because it wrote only the name of the mode into the configuration.

In v7.0.0, the Mode of each binding is a copy of the Rust lindera::mode::Mode: normal mode, or decompose mode with a Penalty. set_mode / setMode and the Tokenizer constructors take a Mode, as set_segmenter_mode and Segmenter::new do in Rust, and no longer take a mode name. Leaving the mode of a constructor out, or passing null / None / nil, still means normal mode, and set_segmenter_mode keeps the penalty:

Bindingv6v7
Pythonbuilder.set_mode("decompose")builder.set_mode(Mode.decompose(penalty))
Rubybuilder.set_mode('decompose')builder.set_mode(Lindera::Mode.decompose(penalty))
PHP$builder->setMode('decompose')$builder->setMode(Lindera\Mode::decompose($penalty))
Node.jsbuilder.setMode("decompose")builder.setMode(Mode.decompose(penalty))
WASMbuilder.setMode("decompose")builder.setMode(Mode.decompose(penalty))

The Tokenizer constructors take the same Mode as their second argument, for example Tokenizer(dictionary, Mode.normal()) in Python. The penalty is optional: Mode.decompose() uses the default one. With IPADIC and both length penalties 0, decompose mode segments 関西国際空港限定トートバッグ as 関西国際空港 / 限定 / トートバッグ instead of 関西 / 国際 / 空港 / 限定 / トートバッグ.

A mode name read at run time, such as a setting, becomes a Mode with Mode.from_str(name) (Mode.fromStr in PHP, Node.js and WASM). It parses the name as the Rust Mode does: "normal" or "decompose", case sensitive, the latter with the default penalty; another name throws the error that set_mode threw for it in v6. A mode name, or any other value that is not a Mode, passed to set_mode / setMode or a constructor now throws a type error: TypeError in Python, Ruby and PHP, an InvalidArg error in Node.js and expected instance of Mode in WASM.

The other changes:

  • The Mode classes: a Mode has no constructor; Mode.normal(), Mode.decompose() and Mode.from_str() create one. It has a name, a penalty (a copy, or none for normal mode), the normal and decompose checks, and equality of the name and the penalty (==, or equals() in Node.js and WASM). Python's Mode(mode_str) and its attributes Mode.Normal / Mode.Decompose, Ruby's Lindera::Mode.new, PHP's new Lindera\Mode(), Node.js's JsMode and WASM's Mode.Normal / Mode.Decompose are gone. The Python and Ruby constructors accepted "Normal" and "Decompose", and PHP's any case; from_str does not. A Python Mode is not hashable, as the Rust Mode is not Hash.
  • Node.js: the TypeScript type JsPenalty is renamed Penalty, and its fields become optional; a field left out keeps its default. TypeScript code that names JsPenalty uses Penalty. The package exports no value for the type, so JavaScript code does not change.
  • Rust: TokenizerBuilder::set_segmenter_mode with a Mode::Decompose whose penalty is not the default now applies that penalty, so the output changes. A mode parsed from "decompose", such as the one the CLI's --mode gives, carries the default penalty and is not affected.
  • Binding authors: CoreTokenizerBuilder::set_mode, CoreTokenizer::from_segmenter and CoreTokenizer::from_segmenter_with_space_penalty take a lindera::mode::Mode instead of the &str that v6.2.0's lindera-binding-core took. set_mode no longer returns a Result. lindera_binding::parse_mode parses a mode name, as the bindings' from_str do.

Node.js: a panic throws an Error instead of aborting

Up to v6.2.0, a panic in the Rust code of the Node.js binding, which is a bug of Lindera, unwound into napi-rs's callback and aborted Node.js with fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic, error 5, aborting. v7.0.0 catches the panic at every function and method of the binding (#1314): the call throws an Error whose code is GenericFailure, as for most other failures, and whose message is the panic's message, and Node.js goes on running. Rust still writes the place of the panic and its message to standard error. An object whose method panicked may keep what the method changed before the panic, so create it again. See Errors of the Node.js binding.

lindera train builds its lattices as MeCab's learner does

Up to v6.2.0, lindera train built training lattices that differ from those of MeCab's learner:

  • The seed lexicon was not in the lattice, so a gold token competed only with unknown words, never with the other seed words.
  • The unknown-word candidates ignored char.def. A fixed classifier (ASCII digit, ASCII letter, kanji, katakana, hiragana, other) gave the class of the first character, every candidate was one to three characters long, and the class number served as the unk.def entry, so only an unk.def with one entry per class, in the order DEFAULT, HIRAGANA, KATAKANA, KANJI, ALPHA, NUMERIC, worked.
  • Each char.def category got one label, with the feature string of its last unk.def line, and lindera export wrote one unk.def line per category. mecab-ipadic's unk.def has 40 lines for 11 categories; they became 11 lines, and the unknown ALPHA, HIRAGANA and KATAKANA words all became 感動詞, the feature of the last line of each of these categories.
  • A gold token that was not a seed word got an unknown-word label through a check written for IPADIC features (名詞,一般 and the like), or a label without features. An unk.def line with fewer than five fields was silently skipped.
  • When regularization left no bigram weight for some context IDs, lindera export wrote a matrix.def smaller than the IDs of the entries (0 0 when no weight was left at all), and the built dictionary panicked at tokenization. model_info.connection_matrix_size in metadata.json was a square of the larger ID.
  • lindera export wrote 32767 (i16::MAX) to matrix.def for a connection without a trained weight, whose bigram features never met in training or whose weights regularization zeroed. Training gives such a connection the cost 0, and so does MeCab's mecab-dict-gen, so the built dictionary avoided transitions that the model had learned to be neutral. In a five-fold cross-validation with mecab-ipadic's files and v6's default regularization, L1 with --lambda 0.01, writing 0 raised the boundary F1 from 0.9552 to 0.9572 in every fold (#1168).
  • model_info.training_iterations in metadata.json was the --max-iterations value, not the number of iterations that ran.
  • Training stopped at --max-iterations unless one of argmin's own tests held: a gradient norm below the square root of the machine epsilon, or an iteration that left the objective unchanged. With an objective in the hundreds or thousands the first practically never holds, so training ran to the cap. An L2 run whose line search failed panicked (#1167).
  • The export functions of the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP bindings wrote lex.csv, matrix.def, unk.def, metadata.json and a fixed char.def with the categories DEFAULT, HIRAGANA, KATAKANA, KANJI, ALPHA and NUMERIC, not the char.def the model was trained with, and no feature.def, rewrite.def, left-id.def or right-id.def.
  • The seed lexicon was read line by line and split on ,, and a line that starts with # was skipped as a comment. mecab-ko-dic's quoted comma surface "," became the surface ", and lindera export wrote it unquoted, so lindera build read the rest of lex.csv as one field and dropped every row after it without an error. The # rows of UniDic, SudachiDict and IPADIC NEologd were not trained.
  • A feature was split on , for the rewrite rules, the feature templates, unknown-word matching and the context IDs of user lexicon entries. A quoted column with a comma in it became several columns and shifted the columns after it: in 19,955 rows of mecab-jieba's training seed, whose quoted English definition is followed by four more columns, %F[6] to %F[9] were pieces of the definition.
  • A %F[n], %L[n] or %R[n] without ? that read past the last column of a feature read * there, so the template still gave a feature, such as U09:*, which every feature with fewer columns shared. MeCab's learner skips the template. The unk.def features of mecab-jieba have five columns, and its feature.def reads %F[6] to %F[9], so its 11 unknown-word labels had four features, U06:* to U09:*, that no seed row had.
  • Model::write_dictionary gave an entry of the user lexicon that Model::read_user_lexicon reads whose context IDs and cost are 0,0,0 the context IDs of another user lexicon entry: the one at the index of the seed row whose feature is the most similar to the entry's, or else the first one. An entry whose feature had no column in common with any seed row got the index of its first character's category in char.def as both IDs, which is not a context ID.
  • Model::write_dictionary gave every such entry with 0,0,0 the same cost, tocost(0.8, cost_factor), whatever its feature. Model::read_user_lexicon read an empty context ID or cost, and a value that is not a number, as 0, and a negative context ID wrapped around to 16 bits (-1 became 65535); the parameters were filled in only when all three were 0. So an entry with an empty cost and given context IDs got the cost 0, and one with empty context IDs and a given cost got the BOS/EOS IDs 0,0.

v7.0.0 trains as MeCab's learner does (see How training works):

  • The lattice has the seed words that start at each position, and the unknown words that the runtime creates there, with the same code: those of the character's default category, with its INVOKE, GROUP and LENGTH settings, for every unk.def entry of the category.
  • Every unk.def line is an entry and a CRF label of its own, with the ID of its category as %t, and lindera export writes every line, in file order. Comment lines and empty lines are skipped, and a line with fewer than five fields is an error.
  • A gold token gets the label of the first seed row with the same span and the same whole feature string; else that of the first unk.def entry of an unknown-word candidate with the same span whose feature columns other than * all equal the gold token's; else a virtual label, which is trained and not exported, as MeCab's learner adds a virtual node. lindera train prints the counts in a Lattice statistics: line, and warns on stderr when no gold token is a seed word, or fewer than half of the gold tokens whose surface has seed rows are, with the first gold token whose surface has seed rows but none with its feature string.
  • matrix.def covers every context ID, plus 0 for BOS/EOS, and model_info.connection_matrix_size gives its size, rows by columns.
  • A connection without a trained weight costs 0 in matrix.def, as in training and in MeCab.
  • model_info.training_iterations is the number of L-BFGS iterations that ran: --max-iterations when that stopped training, fewer when it converged earlier.
  • Training also stops once the relative change of the objective has stayed below --eta (Trainer::eta; default 0.00005, the default of MeCab's learner) for 3 iterations in a row; --eta 0 turns the test off. The bindings use the default. lindera train prints why the optimizer stopped, with the number of iterations and of evaluations of the loss and its gradient, and warns on standard error when an iteration left the objective unchanged or the line search failed far from the optimum. Near the optimum, where which of the two happens depends on the platform, it reports that training converged (#1300). An L2 run whose line search fails keeps the best weights of the run.
  • The export functions of the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP bindings write the files lindera export writes, with the same code: the char.def, feature.def and rewrite.def the model was trained with, and left-id.def and right-id.def too.
  • model.dat has the format version 3.0.0. lindera export and the bindings' export functions reject a model.dat of any other version, including every model.dat written by v6.2.0 or earlier, with an error that ends in "re-run lindera train to regenerate it".
  • The seed lexicon is read as CSV, as lindera build reads lex.csv (see Seed Lexicon): a field may be quoted, a line that starts with # is a row, and the feature columns are kept as written. A quoted field that spans lines is an error. lindera export quotes a surface that contains ,, " or a line break. The user lexicon that Model::read_user_lexicon reads is read the same way.
  • A feature is split into columns as MeCab's learner splits it (see Seed Lexicon): a quoted column is one column, spaces and tabs before a column are skipped, and the text from a closing quote to the next , is dropped. The rewrite rules join the columns they rewrite with ,, quoting a column that contains , or ", as MeCab does.
  • A template that reads past the last column of a feature gives no feature for it, with or without ?, as in MeCab's learner (see Feature Template). In the training files of mecab-ipadic, mecab-ipadic-neologd, unidic-mecab, mecab-ko-dic, mecab-jieba and resources/training/, only the unk.def lines of mecab-jieba have features that a template reads past the last column of, so only a model trained on mecab-jieba's files changes.
  • Model::write_dictionary fills in the parameters of a user lexicon entry separately, as mecab-dict-index does: an empty cost is computed, and when either context ID is empty or negative, both are inferred. 0,0,0 still fills in all three. A context ID or cost that is neither empty nor a number in its range is an error that names the entry.
  • A computed cost is the one MeCab's calcCost computes: the sum of the trained weights of the entry's unigram features, converted as the costs of lex.csv are, so an entry whose feature and first character's category are those of a seed row gets that row's cost.
  • Inferred context IDs are those that lex.csv gives the seed row whose feature is the most similar to the entry's. An entry whose feature has no column in common with any seed row is an error, and nothing is written, as mecab-dict-index fails for a user dictionary entry whose feature has no context ID.

Every lattice now has the seed words. On the mecab-ipadic data of #1110, the new default, L2 with --lambda 1.0 (MeCab's -c 1.0), converges in about as many iterations as MeCab's learner (see lindera train regularizes with L2 by default), where v6's L1 with --lambda 0.01 still reaches --max-iterations (#1167); training there takes about twice as long as MeCab's learner, about two thirds of it outside the optimizer: before it starts (#1263) and after it stops. The files in resources/training/ now define a SPACE category in char.def and a SPACE line in unk.def, so a dictionary trained from them tokenizes without --keep-whitespace, which it needed in v6 (#1166).

What you do: train every model again with the 7.0.0 lindera train or the bindings' training functions, then export it and build the dictionary again. Give every unk.def line at least five fields. An unk.def with several entries per category, such as mecab-ipadic's, is now trained and exported as it is. Remove the comment lines from your seed lexicons: a line that starts with # is now a row. Give the context IDs of a user lexicon entry whose feature has no column in common with any seed row. Write each context ID and cost of a user lexicon entry as a number, or leave it empty to have it filled in. There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior.

lindera train regularizes with L2 by default

lindera train, Trainer::new of lindera_trainer and lindera_crf, and the training functions of the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP bindings regularize with L2 and a coefficient of 1.0 by default: the objective of MeCab's learner with its default -c 1.0 (#1261). v6 used L1 with 0.01, and lindera_crf::Trainer::new L1 with 0.1. MeCab's learner adds ‖w‖² / (2C) to the loss, so the coefficient, --lambda, is 1 / C in general (-c 0.5 is --lambda 2.0); its help no longer gives it the range 0.0 to 1.0, which was never enforced. The new constant DEFAULT_LAMBDA of lindera_trainer and lindera_crf holds the default.

On a five-fold cross-validation with mecab-ipadic's files (#1110), with the default cap of 100 iterations, means over the folds:

RegularizationIterationsBoundary F1Span + POS (4 columns) F1matrix.def
L2, --lambda 1.0 (v7's default)77 to 82, converged0.96130.939718.9 MB
L1, --lambda 0.01 (v6's default)100, the cap0.95780.93508.3 MB
L2, --lambda 0.01 (--lambda 0.01 only)100, the cap0.95820.936119.0 MB
L1, --lambda 1.0 (--regularization l1 only)100, the cap0.96050.93803.3 MB
MeCab's learner, -c 1.075 to 83 evaluations, converged0.96110.939822.5 MB (fold 0)

lindera export gives labels with equal weights one context ID. L1 sets many weights to 0, so many labels share an ID; L2 sets none to 0, and its matrix.def there has about 1,200 by 1,200 IDs, close to the 1316 by 1316 of mecab-ipadic's own. The built dictionary is 4.0 % larger than with v6's default settings there (fold 0). On resources/training/, training stops after 8 iterations instead of 15, and the exported unk.def gets other context IDs and costs; the tokenize output in the docs does not change. These numbers include the first line search of lindera train starts its first line search at a unit step.

What you do: to use v6's default settings, give both. A setting given alone keeps its value, and the other one takes the new default:

v6 invocationMeaning in v7To use v6's settings
No regularization flagL2, --lambda 1.0--regularization l1 --lambda 0.01
--lambda X onlyL2, --lambda XAdd --regularization l1
--regularization l1 onlyL1, --lambda 1.0Add --lambda 0.01
BothUnchanged—

The model still differs from v6's, since the first line search starts at another step (see the next section). To stop as v6 did, also pass --eta 0 (see lindera train builds its lattices as MeCab's learner does). In Rust, call .use_l2(false).regularization_cost(0.01) on lindera_trainer::Trainer::new(config)?, and .regularization(Regularization::L1, 0.1)? on lindera_crf::Trainer::new(). The bindings take the type, the Elastic Net ratio and eta as the CLI does (#1262): pass regularization="l1", lambda_=0.01 in Python, regularization: "l1", lambda: 0.01 in Node.js, a lambda of 0.01 and regularization: 'l1' in Ruby, and regularization: 'l1', lambda: 0.01 in PHP. A model records the type, and the Elastic Net ratio, next to the coefficient: in model.dat and as regularization_type and elastic_net_l1_ratio in the model_info of the exported metadata.json (#1272).

A lambda that is NaN or infinite is now rejected: lindera train and lindera_crf::Trainer::regularization fail with `lambda must be finite and

= 0`, where v6 accepted it, and the bindings raise before they read any file (#1262).

lindera train starts its first line search at a unit step

The first line search of the L-BFGS and OWL-QN optimizers of lindera train, of Trainer in lindera_trainer and lindera_crf, and of the training functions of the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP bindings starts at a step of 1 / |d|, d being the first search direction, so that its first trial point lies at unit distance from the initial weights, as in MeCab's learner and libLBFGS; every later one starts at a step of 1, as before (#1290). v6 started the first one at 1 too, so its first trial point lay as far from the initial weights as the gradient was long: 1.1e5 on the corpus of #1260, where, with L1 and --lambda 0.01, the first search went so far that the loss became rounding error and training stopped with "no progress" after 3 iterations. It now converges after 53.

Every trained model changes, with every regularization type. On the cross-validation of the previous section, the accuracy stays within the spread between folds, and the first line search takes 1 evaluation instead of about 7 with L2 and 13 with L1 (means over the folds, the same build with each first step):

RegularizationFirst stepIterationsEvaluationsBoundary F1Span + POS (4 columns) F1

L1, --lambda 0.011 / |d|100101.40.95780.9350
